## Schema selection terminology

Schema holds Field roots and metadata; its equality ignores schema metadata, while configurable comparison can include it. Projectable exposes a borrowed Schema, and Projection selects field IDs plus four metadata-column flags and a blob policy. These are in-memory schemas/selections, not executed read plans. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:24-31; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:174-177; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1099-1108; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1191-1204)

Field paths use backticks/doubled backticks; minimal path formatting quotes literal dots/backticks, while expression-oriented formatting quotes other punctuation too. See the [schema API supplement](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-schema.md) for edge cases, validation and exact signatures. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1567-1735)

## Cache serialization vocabulary

LCE1 envelope carries a type identity and body version; CacheDecode distinguishes Hit from a reasoned Miss. CacheEntryWriter/Reader manage typed-body sections and absolute offsets, independently of the16-byte key digest. See [cache module](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md) and [format reconstruction](L3-symbols/format-spec.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:144-228; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:28-38; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:117-126)


## Weighted cache budgets

Moka and Quick are in-memory CacheBackend implementations. Their eviction weights include fixed key cost plus declared entry size; shared-buffer-aware deep traversal is a separate callback-based metric. Quick can partition a budget among shards or use a single shard, so fitting the total cache does not imply admission to one shard. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:25-47; rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:186-199; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:40-50; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:101-106; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:216-229)


## Typed cache handles

LanceCache clones and child namespaces share backend, counters and type-aware memory callbacks. WeakLanceCache preserves namespace without a strong state reference and can compute a sized value after expiry without caching it. CacheStats counts successful coalesced loads as hits and excludes loader errors; these semantics differ from a raw request success/failure counter. [Full cache surface](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:212-263; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:314-358; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:420-471; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:570-659)

## Encoded row identity and operation disposition

InlineRowIds keeps byte content and a shared lazy digest memo together so clones reuse both and replacing the wrapper does not carry an old digest into new bytes. Its digest identifies encoded content, not decoded-row equivalence. RowIdMeta chooses inline bytes or hidden-column storage. (rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:27-98; rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:141-166)

The format-layer Transaction is a public protobuf wrapper; its schema-change classification is a conservative operation disposition used to decide where validation may be needed, not validation itself. It has no commit lifecycle in its local body. (rust/lance-table/src/format/transaction.rs:16-82)


## Three version domains and manifest ownership

Dataset version is Manifest.version (with bit63 identifying a detached version), writer version is library-specific semver metadata, and data storage version is an exact ConcreteFileVersion. Treat these as separate domains. A Manifest is an in-memory snapshot with shared fragments and private cached logical offsets; its protobuf serialization is not a complete file or a commit. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:39-128; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:542-552; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:678-724)

Fragment metadata ties columns of the same physical rows to base DataFiles, ordered overlays, optional deletion and inline/column lineage. Every-file operations must account for overlays; lineage lookup intentionally uses base files only. These metadata rules now connect the flag policy to manifest decoding and shallow cloning; dataset IO and transaction publication are still untraced. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:519-558; rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:589-725; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:237-308; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:987-1021)


## Three distinct coverage domains

Index fragment_bitmap tracks fragment IDs; overlay bitmaps track physical offsets within a fragment; key-existence Bloom data tracks encoded join keys for conflict detection. They cannot substitute for one another. Unknown index coverage is None, sparse overlay coverage is positional per field, and a Bloom overlap is only a possible key conflict. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:62-67; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:65-74; rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:175-212)

Covered index fields are dependencies whose values are carried with results; keyed fields decide which search the index can answer. Physical metadata currently validates a suffix representation. The protobuf's future independent-covering feature must not be assumed implemented by that validator. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:36-51; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:156-243; rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:86-97)


## File-version request, identity and footer

Caller Stable/Next selectors resolve to exact2.2/2.3 in this snapshot. Persisted identities have no ordering; use explicit capabilities instead of comparing release numbers. V2.0 standard footer is(0,3), embedded footer and DataFile metadata are(2,0), while manifest string is2.0. These spellings describe the same exact identity. Footer-only detection reads8 bytes and does not certify a valid complete file. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-262; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60)

Overlay staleness is a metadata-derived conservative exclusion set: union newer changes to indexed dependency fields or their ancestors/descendants, then consumers must re-evaluate affected rows. This differs from resolving the newest value and from deleting rows; the helper only returns/accumulates physical offset sets. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:4-13; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:35-158)


## Positional lineage glossary

- **RowDatasetVersionRun / Sequence:** one dataset version per positional span, stored as runs aligned with row-ID order. Numeric span coordinates are not stable row IDs; consumers use cumulative lengths. [Version module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:44-80; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:272-311)
- **SpilledRowLineage:** preloaded row IDs/creation/update sequences keyed by fragment ID, allowing synchronous manifest preparation to preserve column-stored lineage. Loading itself remains a caller responsibility. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:25-42; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:750-769)
- **HoleRuns:** maximal missing-offset runs plus present-count prefixes, supporting offset-to-ordinal rank and inverse selection. It represents holes in a row-ID segment, not dataset-version runs or deletion-file IO. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:132-190)


## Row-ID representation terms

- **Bitmap:** internal presence bits indexed LSB first within each byte; logical length is separate from byte capacity. Constructors normalize padding, raw construction does not. The schema comment disagrees on bit order. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:7-105; protos/rowids.proto:51-58)
- **EncodedU64Array:** owned U16/U32 relative offsets plus a base or plain U64 values; compressed does not imply sorted. Wire packed integers are little-endian. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs:8-26; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:174-230)
- **Range folding:** decoder merges adjacency and groups ascending separated ranges through the segment helper; sequence writer expands the compact Ranges form back into plain wire Range arms. This changes in-memory representation without adding a protobuf arm. [Codec overview](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:60-96; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:232-255; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:376-398)


## Segment coordinates and scan state

- **U64Segment:** one of six in-memory representations of an intended distinct u64 sequence. Numeric values, present ordinals and enclosing numeric bounds are separate coordinates. Selection chooses five forms; compact Ranges comes from explicit range grouping/bitmap conversion. [Module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:16-82; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:196-299)
- **SegmentCursor / SegmentCursorState:** a public borrowed segment reader and its crate-visible bitmap byte/rank state. The wrapper fixes the source; reusable state alone does not. Dense expansion batches contiguous set-bit runs, while selection indices count present values. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-954)


## Row-ID sequences and ordinal selection

RowIdSequence preserves fragment row order across segments. Stable numeric IDs, ordinal positions and tree-map set membership are distinct: set conversion discards order, while masks translate selected IDs back into ordinal ranges. Public checked construction rejects duplicates within one input; raw range/slice conversions and extend do not enforce table-wide uniqueness. [Sequence analysis](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:39-52; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:209-265; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:302-319; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:609-797; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:865-905)

RowIdSeqSlice is a borrowed positional view. RowIdSequenceCursor instead owns scan counters without a source lifetime: it rewinds for decreasing requests and resets segment state at boundaries, but callers must keep its sequence stable across calls. Internal selection clips at EOF; the public ReadBatchParams adapter has separate bounds/error behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:54-170; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:456-494; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:559-592; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:908-943; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:1055-1127)



## Creation lineage during transaction preparation

Creation version records first appearance; last-update version records the commit changing values. The reviewed transaction helper resolves stable IDs back to source physical offsets, preserves known creation versions, falls back to1 for unavailable creation of a found source, and stamps new IDs with the supplied commit version. Writer-placed lineage means row-ID Column or creation-version Column; it is a metadata predicate, not a provenance check. [Table details](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) and [local scenario](L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) separate these synchronous metadata mutations from the separately documented [IO](L3-symbols/protocol-io.md) and [publication](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md) protocols. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:21-79; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:258-295)




## Transaction intent and one-attempt preparation

A Transaction stores read_version,UUID,Operation,optional tag and shared string properties. An Operation names one of16 change kinds with typed payloads. PreparedIndices separately carries current-attempt original/prepared index metadata and fragment-reuse intent; it is not persisted by these containers. Retry/conflict/publication behavior is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). [Transaction API](L1-modules/rust-lance-table-transactions.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/builder.rs:12-25; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:37-248; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:4-18; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:44-100)

CoverageIdentity means UUID plus optional fragment bitmap, with other index metadata excluded from equality. ReadVersionState means borrowed manifest/index evidence from a transaction's fixed read version; it carries no runtime check that the pair matches. UpdatedFragmentOffsets means per-fragment physical offset bitmaps for partial column-update lineage. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction.rs:62-102; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:263-268)




## Equality versus conflict compatibility

Operation equality compares represented intent; different operation kinds always differ. Separate metadata predicates compare config upserts/deletes or table/schema/field metadata scopes. Their bool results are consumed by the commit conflict resolver, whose directional matrix is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). Durable commit-outcome identity uses protobuf forms in the inspected path, not these in-memory payload comparisons. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:18-29; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:863-989; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2039-2052; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:246-283)




## Operation pre-validation

Pre-validation checks operation shape against an optional current manifest. It is synchronous metadata inspection with no storage IO; its success does not certify physical files, schema completeness in modern formats or transaction compatibility. Merge field-binding protection and a separate base-file rewrite detector serve different purposes: binding safety versus latest-version stamping. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:18-200; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:257-416; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1183-1213)




## Durable transaction representation

Operation intent converts to a generated protobuf transaction before storage. Rust optional-empty states and transient rewrite metadata may disappear; unknown update-mode values decode as row rewrite, and empty rewrite groups take a legacy fallback. Therefore in-memory equality, decoded operation equality and persisted protobuf identity are distinct contracts. Byte storage/outcome recovery is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:151-184; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:244-283; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:410-424; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:555-569; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:246-283)




## Stored index provenance versus live coverage

An index segment's stored fragment bitmap can name retired source fragments, while history maps their rows to later destinations. Unknown coverage (None), known empty coverage and known retired provenance have different retention behavior. TaggedLineage separates stored coverage membership from whether history is walkable; known-empty destination lists differ from unknown lineage. These distinctions drive invalidation and retention, with implementation navigation in the [index protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-index.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/index_maintenance.rs:219-348; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/index_maintenance.rs:517-625; rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/lineage.rs:23-140)




## Tagged format state and operation admission

A sticky manifest reader flag can keep the tagged format contract active after the entry is removed. Entry recognition, format recognition, paired-flag validation and operation admission are separate predicates: an Untagged admission does not imply the sticky bit is absent. MovesNoRows is also a reason name, while its admitted operations include in-place column rewrites. Use the exact gate branches for development decisions. (rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/metadata.rs:15-49; rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/gate.rs:77-224)




## Ledger, transition and mapping

A FragReuseLedger contains validated supported whole-fragment transitions ordered so producers precede consumers. Each transition owns source/destination digests and either an ordered bitmap/rank remap or an unopened stable-partition reference. ## Decoder facade glossary

Scheduling selects byte ranges and produces page messages; decoding materializes Arrow arrays through tasks. Array and structural message grammars are distinct. A ReadBatchTask carries a future plus expected row count. Structural byte targets adapt using reported decoded size and can overshoot; array i32-offset limits are a separate mechanism. RequestBatch aggregates I/O calls while preserving each caller's buffer order. [Module contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1542-1558; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1636-1734; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2089-2199; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2863-3064)


## Primitive index and value terms

A mini-block has distinct byte, top-level-row and leaf-value coordinates. A trailer begins a row continued in the next block; that next block has a preamble. Constant pages retain one scalar plus repetition/definition levels, then materialize selected leaf positions. Dictionary normalization moves null dictionary entries into key validity before encoding; physical null-key repair prevents invalid hidden indices when validity is removed. [Helper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/chunk_index.rs:185-343; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/constant.rs:341-492; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/dict.rs:30-170)


## Blob decode view and representation

Original BlobLayout stores position/size descriptions plus same-file payload buffers; descriptor-only reads and binary materialization use separate cache views. Blob-v2 prepared records become kind/position/size/blob_id/blob_uri descriptors, with sidecar/URI handling outside this encoder. A payload shard is a byte-targeted group of original Blob reads, distinct from dataset fragments or MemWAL shards;32MiB is a target that can be exceeded. [Blob contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:31-437; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:262-432; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:4708-4725)


## Fixed slots and map entries

A fixed-size-list dimension gives the number of child slots per outer row. Null outer rows still reserve those slots; variable-size descendants under them can be cleared with a garbage mask. Map entries are Struct key/value rows whose offsets and parent validity are reconstructed through rep/def layers. The current complex FSL path requires immediate Struct children, while Map requires unsorted entries and a nonnullable key. [Nested wrapper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/fixed_size_list.rs:48-91; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/fixed_size_list.rs:328-350; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/map.rs:191-238; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:189-258)

# Lance engine orientation

**Navigation and contracts; source access is expected.** Start here, choose a path, and open its ordered source set. Deep format details live in the [format contract](L3-symbols/format-spec.md), terminology in the [engine glossary](L0-glossary.md), and exact retained declarations in the [frozen symbol snapshot](L3-symbols/symbol-index.md). [Scope and trust](V21-PROTOCOL.md).

## Architecture and state ownership

Lance presents a versioned Dataset over immutable data files and versioned metadata. A fragment groups physical columns for the same rows; its manifest entry carries deletion, overlay and lineage metadata. A Dataset handle owns a manifest snapshot plus stores, commit handler and session/cache handles. Publishing a new manifest makes a mutation visible; finishing a data file alone does not publish a dataset. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-87; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-571; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:1-250)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  API[Dataset / Scanner / write and index builders] --> Plan[Scan planning and execution nodes]
  API --> Tx[Transaction preparation and commit]
  Plan --> Index[Scalar / vector / full-text indices]
  Plan --> Fragment[Fragment reads and row identity]
  Fragment --> File[lance-file exact-version readers]
  API --> Writer[Fragment / file writers]
  Writer --> File
  File --> Encoding[lance-encoding page and buffer mechanisms]
  File --> IO[lance-io stores and scheduled reads]
  Tx --> Table[lance-table manifests, operations and conflicts]
  Table --> Publish[CommitHandler publication]
  Publish --> IO
  Index --> IO
  Core[lance-core schemas, errors and common data structures] --> API
  Core --> Table
  Protos[Handwritten protobuf schemas] --> Table
  Protos --> File
```

The arrows identify ownership/call boundaries rather than a claim that every request crosses every box. Scanner creates a physical plan; the DataFusion adapter executes it and returns a RecordBatch stream. Encoding describes pages and schedules their bytes through an I/O seam; it does not commit Dataset versions. Index creation writes index state before committing CreateIndex metadata. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2648; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-134; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:688-735)

## Read path

**Entry:** `dataset.scan().try_into_stream().await?`. The stream must be consumed to execute reads. This is a trace of the public Rust path; it is not a command that was run during KB work.

1. `Dataset::scan` clones the snapshot into `Scanner`. Configure projection/filter/vector/limit before planning. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704)
2. `Scanner::create_plan_impl` validates options, resolves full-text/query filters, chooses vector, full-text, MinHash or filtered read source, and adds filtering, ordering, limit and final projection. Scalar index use is conditioned on prefiltering or absence of nearest search. Conflicting search modes error. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3210-3375)
3. `try_into_stream` passes the plan, batch size and statistics callback to `execute_plan`. Multiple output partitions are merged with order preservation when ordering exists; execution starts at partition 0 of that final plan. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2648; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)
4. The selected source reads fragment metadata/deletions/lineage and reaches exact-version file readers. File open loads footer/global/column metadata; prepared reads schedule pages, decode selected values and materialize batches. The local contract is in the [frozen shared-reader record](L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs.md); source ranges are rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028. No guarantee is made that every query reads every column or uses an index.

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2675,3210-3375` → `rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761` → `rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028`. For a particular scan operator, follow the scanner's selected source rather than opening all execution nodes.

## Write path

**Entry:** `Dataset::write(reader, destination, Some(params)).await?`.

1. `Dataset::write` constructs `InsertBuilder`, applies params and calls `execute_stream`; the input reader is converted into stream/schema. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-120)
2. Resolve destination/store/version, validate the write, resolve target bases and write fragments. A fixed data filename combined with target bases is rejected. `execute_uncommitted` stops after building a transaction: data objects may exist, but no manifest has been published. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:144-265)
3. Create and overwrite produce `Operation::Overwrite`; append produces `Operation::Append`. The transaction's read version comes from the destination snapshot or 0 for a new destination. File assembly/flush belongs to the fragment writer, and its exact bytes to the selected file-version writer. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:267-315; rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1724-1830)
4. `do_commit` configures `CommitBuilder`. Existing datasets use the retrying transaction path (or the explicitly selected detached path); new datasets use `commit_new_dataset`. Detached new-dataset creation is rejected; detached commit cannot use V1 manifest naming. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:148-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-513)
5. Successful publication returns a Dataset carrying the committed manifest/location and caches. Data-file existence is not commit evidence; error/outcome recovery belongs to `io/commit.rs`. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:515-571; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:258-283)

**Ordered initial read set (5 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-315` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1724-1830` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:294-571` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1581-1800`. The exact persisted manifest contract is already available through the [frozen table I/O record](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs.md).

## Compaction path

**Entry:** `compact_files(&mut dataset, options, remap_options).await?`.

1. Construct and run the compaction planner. Reject eager index remapping on a tagged fragment-reuse history. No planned tasks means no new committed version. Execute planned rewrites with bounded concurrency and collect successful results. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1034-1158)
2. Each rewrite validates its target exact file version, refreshes required fragment statistics and chooses binary-copy or scan/re-encode. A forced binary-copy request cannot silently fall back. Capture old physical row addresses only when a consumer needs remapping; stable row IDs use their own lineage. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2443-2514; rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2634-2730)
3. `commit_compaction` validates tagged-history/remap requirements and takes the **minimum RewriteResult.read_version**, so conflicts since task planning remain visible even if the caller opened a newer Dataset handle. Address-style outputs reserve fragment IDs; remap indices now or produce deferred fragment-reuse metadata according to the selected protocol. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3156-3260)
4. Commit a Rewrite operation through Dataset's normal commit boundary. Old files are not made safe to delete merely by writing replacements; retain manifest/version retention policy. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3574-3605; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:74-119)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1034-1158,2443-2730,3156-3260,3574-3605` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1581-1800` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1244-1535,2618-2855` → [frozen manifest application](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs.md). Split copy mechanics or a specific index remapper into a separate task instead of expanding this read set without bound.

## Index build and query path

**Entry:** `DatasetIndexExt::create_index` / `create_index_builder`; query through Scanner.

1. The Dataset extension constructs `CreateIndexBuilder`; optional name and replace settings are applied before awaiting it. The builder validates one-column admission and reserves names against all stored indices, including unsupported ones. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:1858-1892; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-210)
2. Build/train through the selected scalar/vector index implementation; `execute_uncommitted` yields metadata without publication. Multi-segment FM-Index construction has a separate atomic multi-index path. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-210; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:688-705)
3. On replacement, collect same-name metadata to remove, then commit CreateIndex with newly built metadata. Reload the committed index by UUID so the return value reflects commit-time changes; missing UUID after commit errors. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:698-735)
4. Scanner later selects index-backed or scan-backed sources from query/filter options. Data not covered by an index must be accounted for by that query path; never equate a stored index bitmap with all current rows. The distinctions are in the [frozen index metadata contract](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3290-3375)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/index.rs:1858-1892` → `rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-210,688-735` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3290-3375` → [frozen index metadata](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). Concrete scalar/IVF-PQ implementation choices belong to the M2 index Module Map, not an assumed universal build pipeline.

## Essential distinctions

- File format version, Dataset manifest version, per-row creation/update version and index version are different domains. Never compare them interchangeably. [Exact version matrix](L3-symbols/format-spec.md); [glossary](L0-glossary.md).
- Stable logical row IDs differ from physical `(fragment_id, offset)` addresses; compaction changes physical addresses. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:6-79; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-81)
- Declaration in a protobuf union does not establish acceptance in every exact file version. Reader grammar and writer selection are independent checks. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:93-110; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:93-118)
- Stable format compatibility is durable; unstable formats may change; frozen legacy paths are not new-feature extension points. (AGENTS.md:5-20)

This orientation completes M1's architecture and four public paths. Detailed subsystem/API contracts and navigation tests remain independently tracked in M2–M4; no build or runtime execution is claimed.

## Development entry

Choose a task in the [ordered navigation index](L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md), then read its contract and bounded implementation set. API-only questions start at [public contracts and bindings](L3-symbols/public-api.md).

## Representation and responsibility

`Field` is a public, mutable tree whose public members include name/id/parent_id, logical string, metadata, encoding, nullability, children, optional dictionary and primary/clustering key positions. `LogicalType` hides its String member, but `From<&str>` accepts arbitrary text. Consequently public construction does not guarantee validity; `Field::data_type` is infallible in signature and can panic when parsing malformed logical strings or indexing absent children. Arrow-to-Field conversion is a fallible boundary with partial validation; it is not a substitute for the separate Schema validation layer described in the schema supplement. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-195; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:244-285; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1204-1317)

Private `field` and `schema` modules are hidden behind `lance_core::datatypes` re-exports. `Field` owns local tree operations and metadata transformations. It performs no storage IO, asynchronous work or synchronization in its defined methods. It depends on Arrow datatypes/array casts, `lance_arrow` extension/type helpers, core errors/truthy parsing, and schema comparison/projection helpers. Lazy blob statics use `LazyLock` and shared `Arc` fields; loaded dictionaries share `ArrayRef` values. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:4-150; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:4-35; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:163-1348)

## Blob representations

Child order and types below are exact; `?` denotes nullable child. The source explicitly identifies stored v2 field names as part of the stable file format. These declarations do not prove a runtime version gate or value validator. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:31-150)

| Shape | Ordered children | Declaration / classifier contract |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy descriptor | position:UInt64?, size:UInt64? | Outer canonical description field nullable, blob metadata; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:31-49 |
| V2 logical minimal | data:LargeBinary?, uri:Utf8? | Exact two-field order/type/nullability; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:51-60; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:220-231 |
| V2 logical complete | data:LargeBinary?, uri:Utf8?, position:UInt64?, size:UInt64? | Classifier additionally accepts required position/size; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:62-82; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:220-231 |
| V2 prepared | kind:UInt8?, data:LargeBinary?, uri:Utf8?, blob_id:UInt32?, blob_size:UInt64?, position:UInt64? | Strict child nullability, metadata ignored; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:84-113; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:167-218 |
| V2 stored descriptor | kind:UInt8, position:UInt64, size:UInt64, blob_id:UInt32, blob_uri:Utf8 | Canonical outer description field required and packed; classifier accepts nullable children for released representations; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:115-188 |

Logical input documentation requires each non-null row to set exactly one of data/uri. The optional position/size range describes external objects, with provided size>0. Prepared `blob_size` differs from this input `size`; the stored descriptor uses `blob_uri`. `BlobKind` codes are Inline0, Packed1, Dedicated2, External3; unknown bytes return an InvalidInput error through `invalid_input_source`. The comments define storage meanings and external base-path interpretation; concrete writing, reading and range validation remain pending. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:62-137; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:595-629)

`Field::is_blob` accepts presence of the legacy blob metadata key even when its value is false, or the exact v2 extension name. `is_blob_v2` accepts the extension marker or a blob-marked descriptor matching child names/types. Thus `unloaded_mut` can replace the entire metadata map with descriptor metadata and still retain v2 recognition. It preserves outer identity/nullability but introduces synthetic unassigned child IDs. `apply_projection` treats Maps and blobs atomically by parent ID, preserving those children across repeated projection. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:274-310; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:548-567; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:623-658; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:2182-2220)

`promote_blob_v2` converts legacy blobs to the minimal logical v2 shape and recursively handles non-blob containers; callers persisting the result must assign child IDs. `binary_blob_mut` keeps the v2 extension marker while switching the logical type to LargeBinary and clearing children. `unload_blobs_recursive` directly unloads only v2 blobs; its test explicitly keeps a legacy blob as LargeBinary. These operations have different metadata effects and must not be substituted mechanically. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:569-695; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:2113-2159)

## Logical type strings and conversion failures

Primitive spellings and the complete grammar are in [the format supplement](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md). Utf8View/BinaryView normalize to Utf8/Binary. `json` and `blob` decode as LargeBinary. Containers require separately retained Field children except scalar/nested fixed-size-list logical strings. Timezones are verbatim strings joined after `timestamp:unit:`; `-` is the no-timezone sentinel, and timezone validity is not checked. Size/precision integer parsing does not enforce all Arrow semantic bounds. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:317-559; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:170-195)

Dictionary logical strings are `dict:value:index:false`, with exactly four colon-delimited components on decode. The last component is ignored by the parser. The encoder probes successful inverse parsing, rejecting colon-bearing or child-dependent components early; it allows view normalization and is not an exact-identity or integer-key validator. The tests cover every integer key and representative supported/rejected values. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:354-370; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:502-513; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:798-902)

`Dictionary` equality compares loaded values only when both are present, unloaded offset/length when both are absent, and rejects mixed states. `Field::set_dictionary_values` stores an Arc clone with zero placement after a dictionary-type assertion. Recursive `set_dictionary` supports integer-key dictionaries, Struct, List and LargeList; it does not descend into Map/FixedSizeList. It uses Arrow casts, indexing and unwrap, so a mismatched array/schema may panic. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:561-593; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:455-522)

## Comparison and tree operations

Derived `Field::PartialEq` compares the representation. Default `SchemaCompareOptions` instead ignores metadata, dictionaries and IDs, uses Strict nullability, and delegates child structure to schema helpers. OneWay nullability means a non-null actual can satisfy a nullable expected; not the reverse. ## IDs, metadata and boundary checks

Arrow import removes `lance:field_id`, parses i32 and clamps any negative to -1. Map import requires sorted=false, Struct entries, at least two children and a non-null first key, but does not enforce exactly two children or entries-field nullability here. Primary/clustering position parsing silently drops invalid u32 text; a truthy legacy primary-key flag supplies position0 when no parsed position exists. Schema import enforces primary-key leaf/non-null/List/LargeList/Map ancestry constraints, but not one-based position validity; see rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:835-908. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:37-60; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1204-1270)

`set_id` rewrites parent IDs, assigns only negative IDs and increments a caller-owned seed; it does not advance the seed for retained IDs or validate collisions/overflow. `reset_id` leaves parent IDs intact. Arrow export reconstructs datatypes and metadata but does not restore field-ID metadata or derive key-position metadata from the separate members. Moving through Arrow can therefore change representation details even if logical types remain equal. ## Established API contracts

`row_lineage_field_id(&str) -> Option<i32>` maps only _rowid, _row_created_at_version and _row_last_updated_at_version to -3/-4/-5. `is_system_column(&str) -> bool` recognizes these plus _rowaddr and _rowoffset. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. The root's UInt64 Arrow metadata fields are nullable for scan/selection use, while hidden persisted lineage columns have a separate non-null contract. (rust/lance-core/src/lib.rs:22-98; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305)

`DatasetTakeRows: Debug + Send + Sync` supplies `schema(&self) -> &Schema` and async `take_rows(&self, row_ids: &[u64], projection: &Schema) -> Result<RecordBatch>`. It is an extension boundary for internal consumers, not a promise of stable public behavior merely because Rust visibility is pub. No ordering or missing-ID policy is defined by the trait itself. (rust/lance-core/src/traits.rs:12-27)

`RowAddress(u64)` privately stores high-32 fragment and low-32 offset. The maximum fragment and all-ones row are tombstone constants, but constructors accept them. `address_range` computes fragment+1 without an overflow guard, so its maximum-u32 input is an unresolved caller-boundary risk, not evidence that every call is unsafe. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:23-79)

`blob_path(&Path, &str, u32) -> Path` constructs base/stem/32-bit-reversed-binary-id.blob without IO. Changing the bit reversal, width or suffix changes stored sidecar lookup identity. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/blob.rs:6-15)

## SIMD API and dispatch policy

Public `#[non_exhaustive] enum SimdSupport` has None, Neon, Sse, Avx, AvxFma, Avx2, Avx512, Avx512FP16, Lsx and Lasx. Its Display implementation emits lowercase labels (AVX512 FP16 uses `avx512_fp16`). Public `struct SimdInfo` has `pub tier: SimdSupport`, `pub target_arch: &'static str`, `pub host_features: Vec<&'static str>`. `pub fn simd_info() -> SimdInfo` reports cached `pub static SIMD_SUPPORT: LazyLock<SimdSupport>` and a newly constructed raw capability list; only x86 populates that list. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/cpu.rs:7-96; rust/lance-core/src/utils/cpu.rs:98-164)

On x86 the priority is AVX512F with optional FP16 bit, AVX2+FMA, AVX+FMA, AVX, None. Sse is never selected here. aarch64 iOS/tvOS and macOS select Neon; Linux requires HWCAP_FPHP; Windows/Android helpers return false. loongarch prefers LASX then LSX. This proves selection policy only; matching every selected tier to downstream unsafe kernels remains pending. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/cpu.rs:164-304)

## CPU pool API and failure contract

`pub fn get_num_compute_intensive_cpus() -> usize` reads a process-wide LazyLock. `pub static IO_CORE_RESERVATION: LazyLock<usize>` is public. Environment settings are cached on first relevant use, and invalid numeric values panic through the initializer. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:12-76)

| Setting | Accepted value | Default/interaction | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANCE_CPU_THREADS | Trimmed usize >=1 | If readable, overrides automatic sizing; otherwise max(1, CPU count minus reservation) | rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:23-61 |
| LANCE_IO_CORE_RESERVATION | Trimmed usize >=0 | 2 when env read fails; automatic sizing still leaves >=1 compute worker | rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:63-76 |

Full public submission signature follows; `Result` is std::result::Result with caller-selected E, not the Lance alias. Work is submitted synchronously when this function is called. The returned future awaits the join outcome and rethrows the original panic payload; pure-CPU restrictions are documented but not type-enforced. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:135-208)

```rust
pub fn spawn_cpu<
    E: std::error::Error + Send + 'static,
    F: FnOnce() -> std::result::Result<R, E> + Send + 'static,
    R: Send + 'static,
>(func: F) -> impl Future<Output = std::result::Result<R, E>>
```

The private Runtime is leaked for static lifetime, uses one async worker and the configured maximum blocking workers, and is lazily published through SeqCst atomics. Non-Windows child-after-fork hook clears pointer/election state. Initialization panic has no guard resetting the election flag; pthread_atfork errors are ignored. Neither these failure paths nor fork behavior has been runtime-tested during this extraction. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:78-134)

## Stream API and extension boundaries

Public `enum Capacity { Bounded(u32), Unbounded }` controls cloned-item backlog, not bytes. `SharedStream<'a,T:Clone>::new(inner:BoxStream<'a,T>,capacity:Capacity)->(Self,Self)` returns two handles with shared private mutex state. `impl<T:Clone> Stream for SharedStream<'_,T>` has Item=T. `Bounded(0)` is accepted but cannot acquire a permit, even after dropping one side. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:21-80; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:127-170)

```rust
pub trait SharedStreamExt<'a>: Stream + Send where Self::Item: Clone {
    fn share(self, capacity: Capacity)
        -> (SharedStream<'a, Self::Item>, SharedStream<'a, Self::Item>);
}
```

Only `BoxStream<'a,T>` implements the sharing extension here. The two consumers must advance sufficiently evenly under bounded capacity; unbounded capacity can retain the entire input. Dropping a lagging side discards its pending clones/releases permits; dropping a pending polling owner releases ownership and wakes the parked peer outside the mutex. Upstream panics and clone panics have no recovery guarantee. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:82-247; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:249-275)

Both callback wrappers are public structs generic over `S: Stream, F: FnOnce()`, expose `pub fn new(stream:S,f:F)->Self`, and implement Stream<Item=S::Item>. `FinallyStream` calls F synchronously on the first observed None; early destruction does not call it. `OnDropStream` calls F at destruction, including unpolled or early-dropped instances, and does nothing special at EOF. Callback panics propagate. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:277-361)

```rust
pub trait FinallyStreamExt<S: Stream>: Stream + Sized {
    fn finally<F: FnOnce()>(self, f: F) -> FinallyStream<Self, F>;
```

## IO extension contract and async lifecycle

EncodingsIo requires Debug + Send + Sync. submit_request returns a static boxed future with one Bytes per requested range, including empty ranges. Its priority documentation uses the lowest delivered row to prioritize late indirect reads. The trait itself supplies no scheduler, response-count check, range validation or cancellation policy. Implementations own those obligations. submit_single submits immediately and maps a successful vector to its last element with pop().unwrap(): an empty success panics when polled; surplus results are discarded. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-76)

Both optional derivation hooks default to None: bypass for indirect IO and additive per-scope statistics. Their documented fallback is the original service; the default stats implementation creates no recorder wrapper. BufferScheduler inherits these defaults. Its private Bytes owns the backing handle; new moves it into the scheduler. satisfy_request casts u64 endpoints to usize without checked narrowing and delegates to Bytes::slice without a Lance error conversion. submit_request eagerly slices and collects in input order before constructing a ready future, ignores priority, and owns the resulting vector independently of self. Dropping the future cannot undo this already executed work. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:78-134)

The reviewed lance-file implementation splits large ranges, omits physical IO for empty ranges and reinserts empty results; it checks returned chunk count before reassembling. Single chunks clone Bytes handles and multiple chunks copy into a combined allocation. These adapter checks are not checks in the trait or BufferScheduler. The broader FileScheduler queue and cancellation lifecycle remains pending. A contextual decode_batch call creates BufferScheduler from EncodedBatch.data; that partial caller read does not cover the rest of decoding. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:39-148; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:3412-3440)

### Configuration precedence and validation boundary

CompressionParams first merges an exact DataType::to_string key, then either an exact column key or the first matching wildcard entry in HashMap order. An exact empty record suppresses patterns, several matching patterns have no specificity priority, and None cannot clear inherited values. Pattern syntax is one simple prefix/suffix/middle star branch, not general globbing. Field-level parameters carry optional values without validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:45-169)

The reviewed V2.2 strategy then overlays field metadata. Its parser copies compression strings, silently drops invalid numeric level/threshold parses, warns and skips invalid BSS/chunk-size values, and returns partial fields. Thus the comment "using default" on invalid BSS can mean preserving an inherited setting after merge, not necessarily forcing Auto. Full compression selection and version-specific restrictions still require the complete policy files. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-38; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:554-585; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:122-141)

Metadata keys and two dictionary-value environment identifiers are literal public constants. They do not read the environment themselves. One contextual dictionary caller reads both env variables and delegates precedence to a resolver still pending full analysis. BSS default string is auto; CompressionFieldParams default contains no chosen BSS mode. (rust/lance-encoding/src/constants.rs:9-65; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:6381-6392; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:55-73)

### Memory ownership and row accounting

AccumulationQueue tracks Arrow-reported memory and caller-supplied top-level row counts. insert flushes only above the budget, includes the overshooting array and keeps that triggering array without copying. Retained arrays at/below budget are copied unless keep_original_array is set. The queue is synchronous and holds exclusive mutable state; callers separately synchronize rep/def builders. Row order/count validity and avoidance of the u64::MAX first-row sentinel collision are caller obligations. (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs:10-105; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7976-8007)

BytepackedIntegerEncoder stores 1/2/4/8-byte LE integers selected from declared maximum. Zero omits every appended value and carries no count. Checked append validates storage width, not the original maximum; trusted append has debug assertions only. ByteUnpacker requires external width1/2/4/8 and panics on an incomplete last integer; there is no zero-width decoder. Full-zip deliberately uses the Zero mode to omit repetition indices when repetition is absent. (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/bytepack.rs:73-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:6555-6607)

### Codec extension seam and errors

BufferCompressor is Debug+Send+Sync with compress/decompress/config. GeneralBufferCompressor creates feature-gated Zstd or LZ4 implementations, or a no-op copier; FSST is rejected because it has a separate path. Zstd initializes a reusable compression context lazily in OnceLock<Result<Mutex<_>,String>>: failure is cached and poisoning can panic. Compression is serialized on that mutex, while decompression creates no shared context here. Every implementation appends to output; failures after resizing/appending do not roll it back. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:141-432)

CompressionConfig::default is always Lz4,Some(0). CompressedBufferEncoder::default instead chooses Zstd,Some(0), otherwise Lz4,None, otherwise None,None according to features. A no-op buffer codec can work yet fail to build structural General metadata because pb21 conversion permits only LZ4/Zstd. A feature-disabled request returns an explicit InvalidInput; a Zstd factory success may still fail at lazy context initialization. These defaults and errors are distinct API contracts. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:65-110; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:183-200; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:394-509; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:406-431)

Whole-block compression preserves selected configuration, including level presence, in the descriptor. Per-value compression uses runtime config, which normalizes absent Zstd level to Some(0) and discards LZ4 level. GeneralBlockDecompressor composes any recursively selected inner decoder; CompressedBufferEncoder's own BlockDecompressor always delegates to BinaryBlockDecompressor and is only the variable-block convenience path. Do not decode arbitrary fixed-width output with that convenience implementation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:433-675; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1213-1231)

Per-value helpers require valid monotone in-bounds offsets and representable cumulative output offsets. They append into caller storage but start the returned offsets at zero, so ordinary standalone output requires an initially empty destination. Unsupported bit widths panic in typed adapters. No file IO, async cancellation, allocation cap or numeric version check is implemented by these codecs. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:512-677)

## Buffer ownership, chunk framing and general mini-block composition

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs.md): Public Arrow-backed owned byte-buffer abstraction, typed views, byte slicing, concatenation, raw-pointer interleaving and owned iteration. Alignment, ownership and unsafe preconditions are separate contracts.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs.md): Full-zip value-compression extension trait and fixed/variable owned result union; no concrete compression or file-version dispatch.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs.md): Parent-module-visible lazy automatic sparse-candidate selector. Eligibility is based on an optional explicit setting and dense rep/def budget, not directly on format version.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs.md): Mini-block page/chunk records, owned compression trait and process-wide maximum-value policy. Records describe framing but do not enforce their invariants.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs.md): Metadata-only constant/all-null decompressor with distinct whole-block and fixed-per-value input contracts.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs.md): Outer general-purpose compression of the first mini-block buffer, accepted only for an aggregate size improvement; decoder unwraps that first buffer before inner dispatch.

### Buffer ownership and unsafe preconditions

LanceBuffer owns Arrow Buffer storage. Consuming conversion, cloning and valid byte slicing preserve shared ownership; deep_copy and ordinary concat allocate/copy. concat_into_one preserves a singleton allocation. reinterpret_vec preserves the typed allocation through Arrow; reinterpret_slice retains Arc ownership through custom allocation. No conversion byte-swaps; the crate rejects big-endian targets. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:12-60; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:111-142; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:205-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:283-295; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:11-16)

borrow_to_typed_slice returns an owning ScalarBuffer, sharing only when aligned. borrow_to_typed_view returns Cow, borrowing only when aligned and otherwise copying. Both panic on nondivisible byte lengths. from_bytes conditionally copies on misalignment, but its Vec<u8> branch does not explicitly request the supplied alignment; typed access checks again. Width0 is not rejected and reaches problematic arithmetic/alignment. as_spaced_hex(0) divides by zero. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:62-109; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:144-203; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:8-17)

zip_into_one is a safe API containing unchecked raw copies. It validates bit-width divisibility by8, but not source length, sums, multiplication or usize conversion. Correct execution requires every buffer contain at least num_values*width bytes and all arithmetic/addressing fit. Malformed inputs can produce out-of-bounds raw access; this is a source-derived safety finding, not a reproduced failure. Its older packed-struct caller only debug-checks equal field counts in the inspected slice. Do not extend that frozen path while designing new format features. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:226-260; rust/lance-encoding/src/array_encoding/physical/packed_struct.rs:172-249; AGENTS.md:15-20)

### Chunk representation and layout selection

PerValueCompressor promises independent value decoding and returns Fixed or Variable data plus descriptor; variable size includes offsets. MiniBlockCompressor promises chunk-level decoding, nonfinal power-of-two counts and owned parallel buffers. These traits/records do not enforce metadata/data agreement. MiniBlockChunk log0 means total minus previous; otherwise1<<log, with unchecked subtraction/shift and no final-position check. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs:20-54; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:214-217; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:972-975; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:45-144)

MAX_MINIBLOCK_BYTES=8186 concerns value data. LANCE_MINIBLOCK_MAX_VALUES defaults4096, accepts integer input then clamps1..32768 and is cached once by LazyLock. Non-power-of-two inputs are retained. Rep/def budgeting separately computes min(131072/bits_per_level,65535); zero is invalid and huge widths can yield0. The private fields of MiniBlockCompressionContext are stored by new but repository lexical search found no field reads, so their names are not evidence of active enforcement. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-78; [lexical reference inventory](../analysis/iteration-073-lexical-use-sites.json))

Automatic sparse selection is lazy: any explicit setting suppresses it; only RequiresPageSplit or SingleRowOverBudget invokes the candidate. WithinBudget avoids work. The helper has no format-version argument: v2.2 composition installs rejection and dense_u32; v2.3 installs sparse planning then constant and dense_u32. Sparse planning returns dense fallback for unsupported values or preparation errors; planning errors still propagate. Explicit sparse follows a separate branch. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs:8-24; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:121-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:129-139; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7802-7877)

### Metadata-only and outer-compression decode

ConstantDecompressor whole-block mode requires absent payload, including rejecting Some(empty); scalarNone returns AllNull and scalarSome returns compact Constant with caller count. Fixed-per-value mode ignores the supplied block and uses the separate count. Some(empty) is distinct from None despite both reporting width0. These outputs do not allocate one scalar copy per value. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs:14-62; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:934-960)

GeneralMiniBlockCompressor first runs inner compression, then skips outer work when there is no buffer or first-buffer length<4096. Otherwise it compresses each first-buffer chunk independently; only aggregate strict savings are accepted. Remaining buffers move unchanged, sizes[0] are rewritten, count/logs retained and selected configuration wraps inner metadata. Missing sizes, invalid slices or arithmetic overflow are not converted to validation errors. Factory/config failures may be hidden by early fallback. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs:20-115)

GeneralMiniBlockDecompressor reconstructs the outer codec on each call, expands buffer0 and delegates with all remaining buffers and unchanged count. It expects an already separated chunk; the enclosing descriptor strategy recursively creates the inner decoder. decoded_size_bytes delegates to inner. Codec feature availability remains a factory-time concern; neither wrapper constructor validates it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs:117-145; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1054-1075; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:394-432)

### Raw values and fixed-size lists

ValueEncoder implements three distinct interfaces. Block compression accepts FixedWidth only and returns its unchanged buffer as Some, including empty buffers. Mini-block compression handles FixedWidth and nested FSL, with parallel validity buffers followed by the unchanged leaf buffer. Per-value compression handles FixedWidth or FSL; nullable FSL is copied into row-major validity bytes followed by leaf bytes, while nonnullable FSL moves its leaf storage. None of these paths performs IO. Invalid input handling differs: block/mini-block unsupported variants return errors, while per-value unsupported variants panic. Raw mini-block selection starts with two byte-aligned values, or eight nonaligned values using an estimated sixteen-value size. It doubles while estimated bytes remain strictly below 8186 and doubled count stays within the cached maximum. Initial count can already exceed a small configured maximum. Zero width reaches a debug assertion; malformed byte/count relationships are not validated. Full chunks retain a positive count log even when last; only a residual chunk gets log0. Partial FixedWidth chunks account for all remaining bytes, not a recomputed logical byte count. The comment's 4KiB bound is not the actual 8186-byte constant. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:30-115; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-34)

Nullable leaf AllNull is unsupported here, unlike the per-value route. Per-row validity estimates can overestimate actual chunk-wide bitmap bytes; initial validity-vector capacity omits rows-per-chunk and can grow despite the preallocation comment. The current bitpacking module is gated by feature bitpacking. It supports unsigned native widths8/16/32/64 and 1024-value FastLanes chunks. Constructors do not validate widths. Inline min_size_bytes is 128*compressed_width and excludes its native-width header; the policy's full mini-block estimator includes headers, whereas the small block check uses this header-excluding helper. ### Variable-width interfaces and validation

Binary mini-blocks encode their own offset table at the beginning of each chunk, using signed32/64-bit input offsets rebased to chunk start plus table bytes. Each chunk is padded with0x48 to4/8-byte alignment respectively. The output is one concatenated buffer plus external chunk descriptors; logical num_values is retained from input even though chunk partitioning uses offsets.len()-1. Per-value VariableEncoder and VariableDecoder instead move an existing VariableWidthBlock unchanged. Whole-block VariableEncoder writes a separate width/data-start header, then original offsets and all original value bytes. These interfaces are not interchangeable. BSS groups each byte position across values in a single chunk: out[j*n+i]=in[i*width+j]. ## Packed structs and statistics

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs.md): Row-major packed structs: fixed mini-block, fixed and variable per-value interfaces, child accumulators and nine local tests. File-version selection belongs to the caller.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs.md): DataBlock statistic keys, eager/lazy computation, shared cached Arrow arrays, approximate cardinality, bit/run/entropy estimators and ten local tests.

### Packed struct representation and policy

Fixed packing transposes child buffers into row-major bytes. Mini-block packing reads DataSize and all children as FixedWidth, forwards the zipped block to raw ValueEncoder and stores field widths plus nested Flat metadata. Fixed per-value packing validates nonempty/equal-count/direct-fixed children, checked-sums widths and stores raw interleaved bytes. Fixed-size-list and nullable wrappers fail the direct FixedWidth test even if their logical type has fixed size. Mini decode assumes width consistency; fixed per-value decode explicitly checks byte alignment and child-width sum, but accepts surplus bytes and takes external count instead of input block.num_values. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:40-187; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:298-326; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:418-494; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:879-980; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1037-1041)

Variable packing first compresses each child using the injected strategy. A fixed child contributes configured-width compressed bytes; a variable child contributes u32LE/u64LE compressed length followed by payload. The outer row-offset vector starts0 and selects32bits if total and maximum row size fitu32, otherwise64. Descriptors retain each child codec and fixed-width or length-prefix layout. Decoder copies row offsets, splits every field into builders, then runs each child decoder. It checks offset count, row bounds and exact nonempty-row consumption; it does not require outer first0/final=buffer length. ComputeStat has no Result and GetStat can panic for uninitialized maps. Fixed blocks eagerly populate DataSize, BitWidth, MaxLength, RunCount and BytePositionEntropy; variable blocks populate DataSize/MaxLength exactly once according to a non-atomic empty-map check. ### Shared compression selection and decoder dispatch

The public CompressionStrategy has separate block, per-value and mini-block factories. DefaultDecompressionStrategy implements the four read factories, but there is no default writer strategy in this module: production lance-file versions compose public selector helpers. None payload and Some(empty) are different states; compress_required_block rejects metadata-only output, while reader traits expose requires_payload and optional count inference. Exact decoded-size hooks are optional and default to None. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:86-152; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:896-987)

RLE selection accepts native widths8/16/32/64 and initialized RunCount. Only an explicitly supplied ratio threshold imposes runs<count*threshold; the named0.5 constant does not impose an automatic cutoff. Payload must be strictly smaller than raw, including an8-byte header for whole blocks; ties with a bitpacking estimate favor RLE. Mini estimators suppress errors into fallback, block estimators propagate them. Adaptive mini selection can trial-compress child streams when its initial estimate would lose; this can repeat work during actual encoding. Inline estimates pad each statistic segment to1024 values; out-of-line runt estimates choose raw tail on equal padding/savings cost. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:174-510; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1013-1039)

Metadata parsing is permissive: unknown compression strings remain strings; invalid numeric level/threshold parses become None, invalid BSS/minichunk parses warn, and signed/nonfinite parsed values receive no semantic validation here. Explicit codec settings have interface-specific behavior. Variable mini selection validates offsets and stats before the none shortcut, chooses FSST only explicitly or automatically for eligible nonbinary fields, and wraps explicit other codecs. Variable per-value none bypasses stats/offset validation; on sufficiently large payloads exact zstd honors its level but other explicit non-FSST strings select the feature-dependent default encoder. Small explicit general requests fall back raw without parsing. Whole-block automatic general compression uses physical size strictly greater than32768, whereas the per-value data threshold is inclusive. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:526-585; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:656-696; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:799-840; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:471-489)

Default decoder dispatch is interface-specific:

| Interface | Supported descriptors | Unsupported behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Mini | Flat, InlineBitpacking with feature, Variable, FSST, PackedStruct, FSL, RLE, BSS, General | VariablePackedStruct returns NotSupported; other unhandled tags panic via todo; Inline without feature returns NotSupported. |
| Fixed per-value | Constant, Flat, FSL, PackedStruct | Other tags panic. |
| Variable per-value | Variable, FSST, General, VariablePackedStruct | Other tags panic. |
| Block | InlineBitpacking, Flat, Constant, Variable, FSL, OutOfLineBitpacking, General, RLE | Other tags panic. |

All four unwrap missing outer compression. Inner descriptors mix explicit InvalidInput with unwrap/assert/panic assumptions. Variable per-value FSST hardcodes its raw inner reader; General ignores values/level for read; block Variable uses its payload header instead of nested descriptor contents. Mini FSST and RLE route through the supplied nested strategy, but General recurses via self while carrying that strategy onward. There is no local file-version or recursion-depth gate. Block bitpacking references are ungated despite feature-gated imports: potential no-bitpacking build failure inferred from source, not compiled. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:19-74; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:421-448; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:988-1236)

RLE children permit Flat, OutOfLineBitpacking->Flat, General->Flat, or General->OutOfLineBitpacking->Flat. The grammar excludes Inline, nested General, Constant and other tags before custom reader dispatch. Value width must be8/16/32/64; length width8/16/32. Out-of-line children require run count; both children may not require it, because decoding needs an independently inferable count. ### Physical RLE: writing, child selection and reading

Public RleEncoder::new uses U8 literal run lengths and raw children. Crate-internal constructors can choose U16/U32 lengths and mini child compression. Public RleDecompressor::new(value_bits) likewise uses raw U8 lengths. Constructors retain unchecked settings; shared strategy validation is a separate boundary. These codecs perform no IO, async work, mutation of shared state or local unsafe operation. Native value bytes rely on the crate little-endian guard. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:56-141; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:329-384; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1152-1312; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:27-31)

Each physical entry consists of one native unsigned value bit pattern and its positive literal repeat count. Signed integers and floats therefore group by bits, not arithmetic comparison. A run exceeding255/65535/4294967295 splits into repeated entries at the selected width. Adjacent physical entries can have equal values. Width cost uses entry_count*(value_bytes+length_bytes), with narrower widths winning ties; headers, child codecs and structural framing are excluded. Per-run segment estimation does not model aligned mini boundaries or the byte budget exactly. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:76-328; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:636-725)

| Contract | Mini writer/reader | Whole-block writer/reader |
|---|---|---|
| Input shape | Direct FixedWidth; zero count returns before byte/width validation. Nonzero bytes are visited as a prefix; surplus bytes can be ignored and short/misaligned bytes may error or panic. | Direct FixedWidth; checks native width, count conversion, checked byte size and exact input length even for zero count. |
| Framing | Two global child buffers plus per-chunk sizes/logical-count logs; outer mini framing belongs to the structural layer. | Present payload with an eight-byte LE values-byte-size header, values bytes, then all length bytes; empty output is eight zero bytes. |
| Chunking | Raw payload must fit8186 bytes and configured value cap; nonfinal chunks are powers of two greater than one, final log is zero. | No mini chunk boundaries; only run-width splitting. |
| Child compression | Flat, optional General and optional feature-gated OutOfLineBitpacking candidates. | Always raw Flat children, regardless of configured child settings. |
| Overflow | Eager expansion clamps the run that crosses expected logical count and stops. | Eager expansion rejects overflow. |
| Empty read | Count zero ignores children and buffer count. | Frame must parse first, then eager zero-count shortcut applies. Strict lazy RleRuns still validates coverage. |

The table summarizes exact local implementation, not file-version eligibility. Default value cap4096 is lazy environment-controlled by LANCE_MINIBLOCK_MAX_VALUES and clamped1..32768. The module comments claiming2048 and an automatic50% ratio are stale; explicit ratio and cost policy live in shared compression. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:29-55; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:385-634; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1049-1151; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1313-1345; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1533-1709; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-34; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:174-267)

General candidates compress each raw mini chunk separately and retain a concatenation of frames. They must save aggregate bytes, although an individual chunk can expand. Bitpacking chooses one unsigned bit width across the entire child, at least one bit, then packs each chunk separately; it needs the run count from the other child. Selection enumerates candidate pairs, forbids two count-dependent children and minimizes aggregate payload bytes with first-candidate tie preference. Errors while constructing an optional candidate propagate. No second per-chunk byte-budget check follows selection. selected_payload_size actually builds candidates and allocates, so estimation may repeat encoding work. These are source-derived costs and risks, not benchmark results. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:727-1048; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1084-1118)

On read, an independent child is decoded first when the other needs a run count. Run count comes from decoded byte length divided by native width, not infer_num_values. General Flat can return count zero with nonempty bytes; child validation intentionally skips expected-count equality for zero. Outer expansion checks divisibility and equal entry counts, rejects zero lengths and underflow, and reserves the complete expected logical output. Mini overflow ignores later entries only after the overflowing positive run; a zero entry immediately after exact coverage still errors. Whole-block parsing checks the header and section bounds, then child/coverage checks occur. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1215-1276; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1436-1709; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:601-619)

Legacy count inference is narrowly limited to value16/lengthU8 with two identity children. It sums validated raw lengths without expansion; all other configurations return None before inspecting the frame. The strict crate-internal decode_u16_runs path instead parses children and requires exact coverage, including expected zero. RleRuns retains physical u16 values and typed lengths, counts adjacent equal runs without merging them, and offers physical iteration. owned_size measures visible bytes, deep_size sums backing capacities, and into_owned copies visible arrays. Primitive lazy levels choose physical/coalesced/dense storage afterward; that caller is not yet fully analyzed. ### DataBlock: representation, validity and reconstruction

DataBlock is a public physical representation used between Arrow arrays and encoding strategies. Ten variants carry raw fixed/variable data, validity, fixed lists, structs, dictionary indices/items, constants, all-null or empty values, or opaque encoded buffers. Public fields permit states that constructors do not produce; callers must distinguish fallible checked conversion from infallible normalization and caller-validated helpers. No IO or asynchronous lifecycle occurs here. [Complete analysis](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1-38; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:40-217; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:444-654; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:977-1183)

| Operation | Current contract and failure boundary |
|---|---|
| into_arrow(type, validate) | Public flag is ignored and reconstruction always validates. Constant panics; Opaque returns Internal. Fixed-width checked Arrow layout does not separately compare declared physical width with requested type. Boolean physical width8 is repacked. |
| Variable-width Arrow conversion | Requested classic type must match offset width. Nonempty supported types check required offset prefix, monotonicity, nonnegative bounds and string UTF-8/boundaries before one private unchecked build. Zero count and other types use checked Arrow construction. |
| from_arrays(arrays, count) | Public, infallible and does not call validate_arrays. Uses first type and supplied count; zero/empty and all-null shortcuts occur before unsupported-type dispatch. Mismatched counts/types or unsupported non-null nested types can panic or create inconsistent metadata. |
| validate_arrays | Crate-internal pre-encoding boundary: Arrow basic validation plus recursive classic variable-offset checks; InvalidInput includes field and input index. It intentionally avoids a full UTF-8 rescan. |
| into_buffers | Flattens physical buffers without type/count/framing. Nullable validity first, variable offsets first, dictionary indices first; Struct own validity is omitted. |
| try_clone | Infallibly returns Ok, sharing Arrow buffers and BlockInfo maps; stale docs describing owned/borrowed modes do not describe this implementation. |
| data_size | Visible stored bytes, not retained capacity or expanded logical size. Constants count once; Struct parent validity is omitted; shared storage is not deduplicated. |

These contracts follow the dispatch and helper bodies, not just their names. Offset validation accepts nonzero first offsets and unused payload prefixes/suffixes despite normalized-start-zero module documentation; conversion ignores extra offset bytes after the required prefix. Builder append instead requires the whole offsets buffer to be width-divisible. (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:167-217; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:656-975; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:987-1048; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1185-1250; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1335-1349; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1825-2050)

BlockInfo exposes an Arc/RwLock map of statistic arrays. Cloning shares that mutable map; poisoned locks panic through unwrap. Changing public data or using mutable cast accessors does not invalidate statistics. from_arrays computes inner statistics before optional Nullable wrapping; the outer Nullable cache starts empty. Fixed-list flattening retains leaf statistics even when physical width/count change. Struct statistics require child MaxLength values, which may be absent for child kinds that do not compute them. These are source-level preconditions and risks, not reproduced failures. DataBlockBuilder::with_capacity_estimate is public and initializes no concrete builder. The first append pins shape, even when its validation later fails. Only variable-width append performs its full local offset/range checks; other implementations rely on shape, buffer and dimension preconditions and can panic. Variable append checks capacity overflow before copying, but composite appends are not transactional: child changes can precede later errors, and append_ranges retains prior successful ranges. finish without any initialized builder panics. Struct builder discards parent validity; Nullable builder appends child before validity. The private builder trait is Debug without Send/Sync bounds.
