Dictionary normalization concatenates Arrow dictionaries, promotes overflowing key capacity to UInt32, and represents logical null rows by keys pointing to a null dictionary item. It reuses an existing null item or appends one; indices then have no bitmap. Duplicate dictionary values can remain. Direct dictionary reconstruction verifies declared key width and checked-builds Arrow arrays. Expansion to a non-dictionary type interprets raw keys as unsigned by physical width and iterates the complete physical key buffer, not merely declared index count; empty dictionary/invalid keys and arithmetic overflow remain preconditions. ### Encoder facade, lifecycle and structural dispatch

ArrayEncoder (Debug+Send+Sync) consumes DataBlock with a type and mutable buffer index; ArrayEncodingStrategy selects it per page. FieldEncodingStrategy (Debug+Send+Sync) constructs a field encoder once using schema/metadata and recursive context. FieldEncoder requires Send only and manages buffering plus one-to-many field/column mapping. Public methods and fields are reproduced below in the module catalog; the complete source is in [encoder L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs.md) and [structural builders L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:39-74; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:162-234; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:288-329)

The intended lifecycle is construct → prepare every root → maybe_encode → optional intermediate flush → final flush → await all page tasks → finish once. maybe_encode can return zero or many tasks; each EncodeTask is a static BoxFuture of one page. finish borrows the encoder and returns multiple EncodedColumns, each with column buffers, Values-default metadata and final pages. Preserve within-column order and whole top-level rows, while retaining original top-row counts through flattening. These are trait contracts, not a checked lifecycle state machine. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:75-115; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:162-233)

EncodingOptions defaults are8MiB cache per column,32MiB page limit, keep_original_array=true and64-byte alignment. The field comment incorrectly calls false the default. encode_batch forces true even if the caller supplies false. No environment variables or file-version selection are introduced in these two files. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:256-286; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:419-425; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:1-285)

ColumnIndexSequence assigns u32 columns monotonically and records (field ID,index), while skip consumes an index without recording it. No duplicate/overflow/negative-ID validation or rollback is supplied. BatchEncoder uses one sequence across schema roots; each context retains that root's metadata through recursive child dispatch. Its local col_idx tally is not used to validate allocation. Primitive create_at clones the root HashMap anew into Arc for each call. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:235-254; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:313-365; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:75-88; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:125-129)

OutOfLineBuffers is an address reservation tool: add_buffer returns the current absolute position, advances by size+padding(size,alignment), and stores unpadded bytes. The starting position must already meet the consumer's alignment assumptions. reset_position does not clear queued buffers. By contrast, in-memory encode_batch appends external, page and column buffers without padding, despite validating configured alignment. Its returned addresses can diverge from reservations when required padding is nonzero; do not use this helper as proof of on-disk alignment. Zero alignment evaluates is_pwr_two(0) first and can underflow n-1 with overflow checks enabled before the intended InvalidInput branch. These are source deductions, not reproduced runtime failures. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:117-160; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:380-417; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:435-475; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:15-16; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:44-46)

encode_batch derives dispatch schema from the RecordBatch, prepares all roots, then processes roots sequentially: maybe_encode+flush, external payloads, task awaits in vector order, finish, external payloads, column buffers and final pages. It has no concurrent poll/spawn mechanism itself; encoders may have dispatched work already. Each error returns no batch. The separately supplied Arc<Schema> is returned unchanged without checking equality to the batch schema. Page buckets use page.column_idx, while ColumnInfo indices use enumeration of finish results; unreported or late buckets can be discarded. top_level_columns includes every sequence mapping index, not necessarily one per root. Custom strategies must satisfy these implicit agreements. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:402-501)

Structural builders are version-free mechanisms. PrimitiveFieldEncoding retains an ordered Arc slice of page behaviors without rejecting empty/duplicate lists. Its primitive predicate supports scalar numeric/temporal/decimal/null/binary/string families and recursively nested FSL of those families. It additionally recognizes packed/empty Struct and Dictionary of primitive-recognized values, but declines all blob fields. Unsupported logical Dictionary values return NotSupported; other unrecognized fields return None. Allocation precedes fallible construction. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:24-130)

| Builder | Local recognition and validation | Physical allocation |
|---|---|---|
| binary blob | blob flag plus Binary/LargeBinary | one original-field-ID descriptor column |
| structural blob | blob flag plus Struct | one original-field-ID descriptor column |
| list | List/LargeList, first child required | recursive child only |
| structural FSL | immediate child is Struct, first child required | recursive child only |
| map | unsorted Map, entries Struct with at least2 fields, first nonnullable | recursive entries only |
| struct | nonblob, nonpacked, nonempty Struct | recursive children in order |

All recursion uses the complete original strategy and original root context. Map does not enforce exactly two entries fields, names or actual key values locally. Structural FSL recognition is not recursive through outer FSL wrappers. Fallible child construction can leave sequence indices consumed. Full logical codec validation remains pending. ## Decoder facade — cycle82

### Decoder construction and execution contracts

The full decoder facade is covered by [L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs.md), including every line and437 declaration records. This closes the facade gap, not the concrete logical-codec gap. FieldScheduler is Send+Sync+Debug and initializes through &self; StructuralFieldScheduler is Send+Debug and initializes through &mut self with optional requested ranges. Both return jobs borrowing themselves. LogicalPageDecoder supplies asynchronous loading, counters and drain; structural page/field decoders separate loaded shards, rep/def and consuming CPU tasks. DecoderPlugins is an empty placeholder and the scheduler constructor ignores it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:267-342; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1211-1285; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:3153-3400)

DecodeBatchScheduler::try_new asserts positive rows in its internal constructor. It creates a synthetic nonnullable root, restores original field IDs and marks __lance_decoder_root=true. Empty column metadata or a structural first column selects structural planning; array planning prepends dummy root column0 and saturating-shifts the supplied mapping. Structural initialization can restrict itself to requested ranges; array initialization does not receive that restriction. ColumnInfo::is_structural examines only first page, returningfalse when empty. Mixed page grammar, mapping consistency and all numeric ranges are not universally validated here. (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:486-526; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1181-1285)

ColumnInfoIter has two cursors: sequential physical column position and supplied mapping position. next consumes physical columns; next_top_level jumps using the next mapping. peek/peek_transform direct-index and can panic; expect_next handles exhaustion with InvalidInput. peek_transform replaces an Arc only in its owned vector. Buffer descriptors are borrowed nested views; protobuf and array/structural tag accessors assume correct variants and may panic. (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:424-548; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:577-651)

| Structural field dispatch | Local contract |
|---|---|
| primitive, recursive primitive FSL/Dictionary | one lazy primitive scheduler; advance mapping after construction |
| packed Struct | same one-column path, before blob branch |
| blob Struct | any BlobLayout page selects one-column primitive; otherwise recurse |
| ordinary Struct | recurse all children, empty Struct consumes no column here |
| List/LargeList | require first child, recurse and wrap |
| direct FSL of Struct | require first child and wrap; deeper FSL wrappers not recognized by this guard |
| Map | reject keys_sorted=true, recurse entries; exact key/entry validation delegated |
| other | todo panic |

FSL dimensions are checked before dispatch. Decoder Dictionary recognition is broader than encoder primitive recognition, and empty Struct routing differs; concrete codec evidence is needed before claiming those combinations work. Array dispatch separately handles binary-as-list, Blob descriptors, primitive/binary dictionary values, list offsets and legacy simple/packed structs. Legacy helpers unwrap some malformed encodings and simple-struct Result. These are frozen read paths, not foundations for new format features. (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:686-1123; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:39-130; AGENTS.md:5-20)

Range scheduling flushes the request batch after every successful scheduling step. Structural jobs terminate with an empty vector; array jobs loop against reported remaining rows and advance SimplePriorityRange. No explicit zero-progress protection exists. Unbounded channel send failure halts scheduling; a schedule error is emitted then scheduling returns. schedule_ranges_to_vec collects every message in memory. Range ordering/nonoverlap is documented, not validated here. Indices are checked strictly increasing, reject u64::MAX, and coalesce contiguous values; file row bounds are outside this helper. Range num_rows uses unchecked subtraction/sum before public wrappers trim empty/reversed ranges. (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1300-1539; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2202-2262)

### Batch modes and lifecycle

| Path | CPU placement | Byte planning | Error/end behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| array async stream | tokio::spawn when task future polled | i32-offset prefix budget by default; optional byte target ignored with warning | planning/load error emits one error task then ends; CPU task errors do not fuse planning |
| structural async stream | spawn or inline policy | adaptive byte target; no array i32 prefix limiter here | planning/load error emits one error task then ends; CPU task errors do not fuse planning |
| blocking iterator | synchronous materialization | array i32 budget; structural default accepts rows; byte target ignored | any error fuses iterator |
| memory decode_batch | structural spawn unless env exactly never; array spawn | disables array i32 split; one-batch assumption | unwrap first stream item, return only its task |

Positive row count with empty columns can panic in convenience wrappers before the constructor's empty-column handling. Zero requested rows returns an empty result early. Row cap0 and byte target0 are not rejected locally. Initialization is awaited regardless of inline policy. Spawned scheduler body has no await; EOF awaits its JoinHandle and unwraps panics, drop aborts it, but prompt preemption of synchronous work or backend I/O cancellation is not guaranteed. Async wrapper retains an I/O Arc through a final closure. RequestBatch aggregates at8MiB. If existing queued bytes plus a new request exceed the target, it submits the old queue while holding the mutex, then queues the new request even if that request alone is larger. Equality does not trigger a flush. Explicit flush releases the mutex before delegate submission. A polled reply future yields once if not ready, flushes all pending work and awaits the oneshot. One queued request is forwarded unchanged; multiple requests are stable-sorted by(start,end), not merged/deduplicated, use minimum priority, and restore each caller's order through index vectors over shared Bytes results. Too-few result buffers can panic on indexing; dropped reply receivers do not exclude their ranges from submission. Bypass/statistics hooks delegate to inner I/O. SchedulerContext wraps I/O with RequestBatch, borrows its I/O/cache Arcs through getters, and manages path/name stacks. ScopedSchedulerContext::pop is explicit; dropping it alone does not pop. ListPriorityRange converts item progress into parent-row priority using shared offsets, including equal offsets for empty lists; monotonicity, normalization and overflow are caller assumptions. A contradictory layout can disagree with scheduler metadata. It casts row count to u32 and returns the first task only; zero rows reaches the constructor assertion. ### Dictionary validity and encoding budgets

normalize_dict_nulls supports eight signed/unsigned integer key types. With no null dictionary values it returns original Arc immediately; otherwise remove null values preserving order and unused valid entries, remap keys, and make keys selecting null values null. It does not deduplicate. Negative/unrepresentable keys return Internal when converting; out-of-bounds mapping can panic. Narrow native conversion can fail for high unused valid dictionary entries. All-null dictionary values become empty values with null keys. Unsupported key types return NotSupported, nondictionaries Internal. Before dropping key validity, clear_out_of_range_null_keys checks physical null slots. If any are negative/unrepresentable or beyond dictionary length, rebuild every null key physically as0 while preserving logical validity and sharing values. If all null slots are already in range, no validity exists, or dictionary empty, return original. Empty dictionary must retain validity because no replacement index is valid. Parent extract_validity calls normalize then repair then extracts validity; Null arrays add an unset bitmap. ### Blob representations and ownership

The complete [field encoders](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs.md) and [original-Blob page schedulers](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs.md) describe two distinct formats. Public BlobStructuralEncoder stores binary payload out of the page in the same file and wraps a two-field descriptor layout in BlobLayout. Public BlobV2StructuralEncoder transforms prepared six-field Struct input into five-field descriptors using normal structural encoding, without BlobLayout wrapping. It does not fetch URI objects or create packed/dedicated sidecars. Those storage operations remain in unreviewed higher layers. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:31-227; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:229-437)

Both constructors synthesize descriptor Fields using input name/nullability, new Arrow schema and only packed=true metadata. Original metadata/IDs/children are not copied directly, despite original-binary comment claiming metadata preservation. Factories reserve the physical column using original field ID before invoking the descriptor closure. Binary factory accepts Binary or LargeBinary shape, while BlobStructuralEncoder::maybe_encode directly requires LargeBinary; any normalization between broader callers and that boundary must be separately established. Exact V2.1 composition supports original binary Blob and rejects other marked shapes; V2.2/V2.3 try both factories. Blob v2 naming is a representation version, not file version2.0. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:43-71; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:105-125; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:234-252; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:133-165; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:69-90; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:67-93; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:75-101)

| Original binary descriptor | position | size | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| valid nonempty | reserved same-file byte position | payload length | read that byte range |
| valid empty |0|0| no payload read |
| null |(definition<<16)+repetition|0| packed levels, not a file offset |

Original encoder adds leaf validity, serializes supplied rep/def, and flushes descriptor buffering under the old interpretation whenever a later array changes meanings. It then stores new meanings, copies nonempty payloads into OutOfLineBuffers and encodes a nonnull position/size Struct with fresh empty RepDefBuilder. Encode futures wrap only Structural results and preserve page identity/data. flush uses cached meanings or dummy[AllValidItem]; finish delegates unchanged. Null-level indexing assumes correspondence with binary rows; nonnull/empty branches do not store repetition, so arbitrary nested behavior cannot be inferred from this loop alone. Earlier collector/state mutation is not rolled back if later work fails. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:73-227)

OutOfLineBuffers::add_buffer returns current reserved position, advances by length plus length-derived alignment padding and stores buffer. It does not write bytes; caller must supply a valid aligned base and later write in that order. The Blob encoder copies each payload before reserving it. V2 Inline also submits zero-length buffers; original empty binary does not. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:117-160; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:146-175; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:377-389)

### Original Blob read views and cache

BlobLayout dispatch recursively creates an inner scheduler, converts layer meanings, then selects descriptor wrapper when requested dtype is Struct, otherwise payload wrapper. Both scheduler types are pub(super), despite their pub constructors; TARGET_SHARD_SIZE is the public constant. Descriptor wrapper delegates initialization/cache loading, wraps each selected decode task and keeps task rows. Payload wrapper always requires initialization, eagerly schedules every descriptor row and requires exactlyone inner task. It awaits, drains and synchronously decodes that task inside its initialization future, converts to two-field Arrow descriptor, and caches shared UInt64 arrays. Returning cache does not install it into the outer wrapper: caller must invoke try_load. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:214-260; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:4583-4611; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:36-109; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:235-361)

PageCacheView values distinguish Native, BlobDescriptor and BlobPayload. Their text tags are n/bd/bp; typed key variant ordinals0/1/2 are each encoded as a variant field tag followed by little-endian u32, after column/page u32 fields and before the target-data-type string. Each variant write hashes five bytes, not one. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/key.rs:270-276) Key schema version2 is a cache-key version, not a file-format gate. Payload try_load rejects wrong erased cache type; descriptor try_load delegates inner. Keeping views distinct prevents interpreting inner decoder cache as fully materialized payload-descriptor state. Full outer cache lookup/initialization orchestration remains pending in parent. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:4708-4778; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:70-109; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:346-361)

Descriptor CPU wrapper requires Struct data with first two FixedWidth children, borrows buffers as u64, then zips positions/sizes to reconstruct levels. It does not check bit widths, equal buffer lengths or exact child count; extra children remain in returned data. Nonzero size means rep/def0. Zero-size position decodes low16/next16 bits, ignoring high32. It discards inner repdef and returns original data with new outer RepDefUnraveler. Fallback item count uses positions length even if zip was shorter. All-zero rep is omitted; def omitted only for exactly[AllValidItem]. Empty meanings can panic. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:151-214)

Payload scheduling requires loaded descriptor arrays, iterates selected row ranges in supplied order and reserves vectors from unchecked summed count. It ignores Arrow child null validity when reading physical values. Nonempty ranges use unchecked position+size and add size to shard budget; zero-sized descriptors decode packed levels, prefill Bytes::new when def0 and queue no I/O. This prefill ensures empty values do not steal a following payload reply. Shard priority is first selected page-local row plus page priority. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:363-405)

Flush after a row reaches or exceeds32MiB, so one blob may exceed target. Null/empty rows use no payload budget and can create a large descriptor vector. Final descriptor-only shard still calls submit_request with empty range vector. I/O future assigns replies only to def0 entries lacking bytes, errors if replies insufficient and checks surplus replies only via debug assertion. It does not validate returned byte lengths against descriptors. Underlying I/O defines actual submission/cancellation behavior; no local spawning or concurrency limit. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:262-290; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:406-432)

Decoder drain removes first requested blobs and can panic on over-drain; num_rows is original total. CPU task allocates contiguous payload/UInt64 offsets/level vectors, copies bytes and repeats offsets for missing bytes, then returns VariableWidth64 and outer repdef. Actual reply lengths determine offsets. Memory includes loaded Bytes plus newly allocated output during copying, and32MiB is no peak-memory bound. No decoded-byte estimator override exists locally. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/blob.rs:435-552)

### Blob-v2 prepared-to-descriptor conversion

Prepared input must be Struct with ordered fields kind:UInt8,data:LargeBinary,uri:Utf8,blob_id:UInt32,blob_size:UInt64,position:UInt64 matching BlobV2Layout::Prepared, otherwise InvalidInput. Output ordered children are kind,position,size,blob_id,blob_uri, all nonnull. Only original parent Struct nulls are carried to output. Incoming repdef and row metadata are passed to descriptor encoder. Unlike original binary Blob, null representation is ordinary parent validity and there is no BlobLayout wrapper. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:255-437)

| Input kind | Output position / size / id / URI | Local side effect |
|---|---|---|
| parent null or kind null |0 /0 /0 /empty; kind Inline | none; only parent nulls retained |
| Dedicated |0 /raw blob_size /raw blob_id /empty | none |
| Packed |raw position /raw blob_size /raw blob_id /empty | none |
| External |position or0 /blob_size or0 /blob_id or0 /copied URI | no remote access |
| Inline |reserved file position /data byte length /0 /empty | copies data into external-buffer collector |

Unknown nonnull kinds fail BlobKind conversion. Kind-null under valid parent becomes nonnull placeholder descriptor, not an output-null row. Dedicated/Packed required children, External URI and Inline data are read through physical value methods without rejecting null child validity. Schema classification does not establish those value invariants. The encoder also does not validate URI/base IDs/size/ranges/sidecar existence. A later row failure can follow earlier collector mutations. These are precise local preconditions/limitations; upstream prepared-record validation is not yet fully analyzed. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/blob.rs:276-420)

### Fixed-size-list coordinates and reconstruction

| Operation | FSL behavior | Map behavior |
|---|---|---|
| encode row metadata | row_number unchanged; num_rows multiplied by dimension | row_number and num_rows unchanged |
| scheduler request | both range endpoints multiplied by dimension with checked arithmetic | exact supplied ranges |
| initialization ranges | optional mapped ranges owned by future | direct borrowed delegation |
| scheduled row count | integer quotient child rows/dimension for each scan line | unchanged |
| decoder drain | child count=num_rows*dimension | same num_rows |
| decode levels | decimate by dimension, unravel outer validity | unravel i32 offsets and validity |

These are local wrapper coordinates; do not substitute entry count for Map top-level metadata. Child implementations determine their interpretation of forwarded structural levels. ### Garbage filtering preserves fixed slots

FSL must retain dimension child slots even for a null parent. If parent validity exists and descendants are variable-size, it expands inverse validity into a child-slot garbage mask. needs_garbage_filtering recursively recognizes Struct/FSL and List/LargeList/Map/ListView/LargeListView; dispatch for both list-view forms is nevertheless unimplemented. This local mismatch is distinct from full schema reachability. Some all-valid bitmap traverses filtering; no bitmap skips it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/fixed_size_list.rs:70-89; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/fixed_size_list.rs:307-350)

List/Map filtering keeps parent slot count, makes masked slots null with repeated zero-based offsets, gathers physical child ranges for unmasked slots and uses UInt64 indices plus Arrow take. Unmasked own-null rows still retain their physical ranges. Empty kept ranges use empty slices. It always builds Some validity, including all-valid. Struct filtering preserves its own nulls and applies the same supplied mask only to variable-size descendants; nested FSL expands supplied mask and preserves its own nulls. Neither ORs its own validity into the incoming mask. Descendant recursion after list/map gathering uses an all-false mask. These helpers remove garbage described by the supplied ancestor mask, not every possible null-descendant payload. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/fixed_size_list.rs:352-545)

Memory includes the boolean expansion, kept-index vectors/UInt64 arrays, offsets/validity and gathered Arrow output. Index arithmetic and capacities are unchecked; mask-length checks are debug assertions. Arrow take and Map reconstruction use expect, while other constructors may panic. The helper returns ArrayRef rather than Result. Preserve these preconditions or explicitly change error behavior when extending it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/fixed_size_list.rs:334-545)

### Map list levels and delayed validation

Map maybe_encode uses expect on runtime downcast. add_offsets normalizes offsets according to each row's length/own validity, identifies discarded physical values under null maps and returns that garbage flag. Conversion to ListArray then filters own-null garbage if necessary and trims values to visible first/last offsets. Underlying ListArrayExt builds a selection bitmap across the full values array, removes prefix/suffix and own-null spans, invokes Arrow filter with unwrap, and rebuilds list offsets. Without garbage, trimmed_values can share the visible child slice. The rep/def layers carry map structure; no separate map-offset page is emitted here. ## Responsibility and runtime values

The module copies complete encoded pages into an ordinary output file, relocating buffer offsets and priorities and regenerating metadata/footer. It does not publish a Dataset transaction, choose a fallback, reserve Blob IDs or own source storage. EncodedFileInput holds a scheduler and optional expected physical row count; the expectation is checked later. DataFilePart additionally retains normalized schema, cached metadata and optional Blob lease/target. Neither object pins an ETag/hash or rechecks immutability during copying. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:4-8; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:60-127; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:795-1035; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1172-1180)

BlobTargetId is an arbitrary Arc string compared by value. It is not persisted and does not establish Dataset/base/object-store authority. FileConcatTarget stores an exact version, Arc schema and optional target identity. FileConcatResult separates Written, Reused(index, output metadata) and Unsupported(reason); malformed/missing inputs instead return Err. All public declarations and fields, private helpers and exact generic bounds are cataloged below. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:39-58; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:500-525; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:545-678)

## Entry paths and validation order

1. Ordinary concat_files rejects empty inputs, concurrently reads raw metadata, then returns LegacyVersion if the target or any input is V1. It finalizes all current metadata before shared compatibility. IO/metadata errors can precede the legacy result. Ordinary target Blob fields are unsupported. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:684-712; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1078-1118)
2. DataFilePart::open first checks lease shape, reads full metadata and reconstructs anonymous Blob descriptor children, checks expected rows, rejects Blob v1, validates rectangular metadata and compares normalized/footer counts. Blob v2 descriptor validation happens before requiring a target ID. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:140-225)
3. concat_data_file_parts rejects empty input, compares optional target identities for every part, then sorts declared leases and rejects overlap. It borrows already validated metadata/schema without reopening or checking Blob descriptors again. Touching leases are legal. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1138-1180)
4. Shared preparation rejects read_batch_bytes=0, then checks compatibility and total-row overflow. A single ordinary input is reused with no output factory or writer-option use. Part mode always writes a new file after successful validation, including one part. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:916-955)

| Compatibility sequence | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expected row count differs | InvalidInput with path/actual/expected |
| Exact version differs | Unsupported VersionMismatch |
| Schema differs from full target or descriptor-projected target | Unsupported SchemaMismatch |
| External metadata validation fails or normalized rows differ from footer | CorruptFile |
| More than one global buffer | Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers |
| Column count differs from first input | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(None) |
| Any column-level buffers | Unsupported ColumnBuffers |
| Physical column index differs | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(Some(index)) |
| Serialized column-level encoding differs | Unsupported ColumnEncodingMismatch |

Order is per input after baseline encoding serialization. Column encodings compare protobuf Any bytes; page encodings and page counts may differ. These checks precede the output factory, but page ranges and IO response lengths are checked later. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:680-793)

## Blob schema and descriptor boundary

Footer reconstruction finds top-level consecutive runs matching anonymous descriptor children by ID=-1,parent=-1,name,logical type and empty children. It drains those runs and attaches them to childless Blob nodes in preorder. It does not compare child nullability/metadata/encoding, require all missing nodes be repaired or reject unconsumed queue entries. This is a local interpretation of existing footer metadata, not a migration or new persisted format. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:232-302)

Descriptor validation requires distinct nonnegative Blob field IDs, constructs exact physical-column projection, then opens another FileReader with no cache and streams8192 rows/readahead4. Thus Blob part opening can read metadata twice. It validates decoded descriptor arrays; managed Blob payloads are not loaded here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:316-377)

| Selected nonnull descriptor kind | Required here | Outside this check |
|---|---|---|
| Inline | size must equal0 | position and ID |
| Packed | lease present and ID contained | payload existence, range bounds, size, repeated IDs |
| Dedicated | lease membership and position0 | payload existence and complete-file size |
| External | recognized kind only | URI, base authority, offset and size |

Unknown kinds propagate BlobKind conversion error. Missing named kind/position/size/blob_id fields are CorruptFile; incorrect Arrow types can panic at downcasts. Descriptor child nulls have no separate guard, and blob_uri is not inspected. Lease shape requires1<=start<end, independently of descriptor content. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:304-314; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:379-444; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:595-629)

Struct validity intersects row selection; List/LargeList expand only selected valid parents into child offset ranges. Other containers receive no recursive branch here. A malformed Arrow array/selection can panic through indexing/casts; this function relies on typed decoded arrays. Whole leases are checked for overlap even for non-Blob parts that merely carry unused ranges. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:445-498; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1152-1170; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1506-1543)

## Copying, memory and failure lifecycle

Inputs and physical columns are processed sequentially. Consecutive complete pages are batched by summed payload bytes; the default16MiB threshold is soft because the first page is admitted even when larger. Zero-length buffers consume no read result but still call the writer's empty external-buffer path. Offsets and sums use checked arithmetic; actual range<=EOF is delegated to IO. The scheduler may coalesce/split requests internally, so one submit_request is not a proven single backend read. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:527-543; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:795-892)

Each positive buffer response must match its recorded length exactly. New PageInfo preserves rows and encoding, replaces physical offsets and checked-adds prior input row count to priority. Priority overflow and extra-response errors occur after potential writes. Metadata for all inputs and all output pages is retained even though payload reads are batched. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:893-915; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:937-1011; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1083-1117)

V2_0 structural header columns copy only until output pages exist, then normalize the first header page to total rows,priority0 and truncate to one. Other current versions copy every column and need no final page adjustment. Column-level encoding comes from the first input. An empty external-buffer write aligns the schema descriptor before initialize_with_external_columns and normal finish. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:962-1021; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:230-276; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:84-132)

The explicit abort runs only for errors inside the copy/finalize/finish async block. Factory and lazy-writer-construction failures occur before that block; cancellation does not reach its error match. Abort returns no Result at this boundary, so no successful deletion/durable rollback is established. A reused or unsupported result never invokes the output factory. Source and output object identity separation is not checked here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:942-956; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1025-1035; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:261-269)

## Dependencies and caller seam

Core supplies Schema/Field/Blob conventions, errors and cache; Arrow arrays expose descriptor/null/offset structure; lance-encoding provides normalized ColumnInfo/PageInfo and decoder plugins; lance-io provides schedulers, row selectors and writer trait; prost/prost-types provide exact encoding comparison. The std ordered collections make field-ID maps and lease/schema reconstruction deterministic locally, while futures drives concurrent metadata reads and streaming descriptors. No new feature flag or environment variable is defined. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:10-37; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:316-377; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:680-712; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1083-1088)

A narrowly inspected Dataset wrapper opens all parts, derives target path/store/ID, calls concat with default options, treats Reused as Internal, maps version/schema/other unsupported reasons to distinct errors and returns DataFile with output size. Its loader checks stored size before opening parts with expected rows and lease; its target ID builder uses base:id or primary plus filename. These are observed integration snippets, not full Dataset authority/recovery analysis. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:278-341; rust/lance/src/dataset/data_file_part.rs:104-129; rust/lance/src/dataset/data_file.rs:125-136)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. Empty/reversed/overflow/malformed-offset cases are not fully guarded. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:124-194)

These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. Do not turn a missing helper check into an assertion that every public reader call exposes it. The complete reader is now covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md), including sorted grouping, selector differences, cache assumptions and constructor validation limits. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396)

## Page-table representation and resource behavior

PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:16-35) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:147-160) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

On disk, table dimensions are implicit: inclusive min..=max field IDs and num_batches from surrounding schema/metadata. Each field has consecutive batches, each containing position and length as signed64 values; missing/struct slots emit0,0. For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-92) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145) (protos/file.proto:41-59)

load rejects max<min as Internal, then decodes the entire Int64 array and expands every cell into maps, including holes. Negative dimensions/values, arithmetic overflow and actual decoded shape are not independently validated; casts/downcasts/indexing rely on external invariants. Zero batches create nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:53-92)

write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. After tell it derives batch count=max batch key+1, builds two values per cell, writes the Arrow values buffer directly and returns starting position. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. This method has no explicit endian conversion, alignment, framing, flush, shutdown, abort or cancellation cleanup. It does not establish atomic persistence. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:103-145)

No local tests cover dictionary dispatch, projection edge cases, metadata object presence roundtrip, malformed offsets, negative dimensions, zero-batch rewrite or partial IO. ## Ownership and opening

FileReader shares its Reader, Metadata, ordinary PageTable and optional statistics PageTable through Arcs, while owning the supplied Schema. Clone retains shared underlying dictionary arrays through Schema's Clone behavior. object_reader is public and can be replaced without refreshing stored metadata. fragment_id is retained for Debug; this file does not generate row IDs. There is no custom Drop or shutdown protocol. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:41-66)

~~~text
try_new(store, path, supplied_schema)
`-- try_new_with_fragment_id(fragment=0, min=0, max=schema.max_id, cache=None)
    |-- ObjectStore.open
    |-- read_metadata
    `-- try_new_from_reader(metadata=Some)
        |-- ordinary PageTable load/cache using supplied path and bounds
        `-- statistics PageTable load/cache using Reader.path/stats
            `-- read_metadata again unless cache serves it
~~~

The two table futures are polled concurrently with try_join. Supplied metadata is trusted for ordinary-table loading; the statistics loader independently obtains metadata from the reader. Without a cache, ordinary construction reads metadata twice. The separate path, reader path, metadata, schema and field bounds are not reconciled. An error returns before construction; no rollback or explicit abort guard is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:139-208; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-294)

Every constructor here requires Schema. It neither discovers schema nor hydrates dictionary values, despite stale documentation about an optional manifest. Self-describing opening is a separate table-layer trait: it reads Metadata, requires manifest_position, reads Manifest, populates schema dictionaries, then calls try_new_from_reader. Dataset fragment opening supplies its schema and file field bounds; the full Dataset wrapper remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:126-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1126-1182; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:1374-1401)

## Cache and metadata contract

The private typed string key has stable schema `lance.file.previous.string-key`, version 1, and writes one string. Stable value IDs are `lance.file.previous.Metadata`, `lance.file.previous.PageTable` and `lance.file.previous.OptionalPageTable`; compiler type names are diagnostic only. The key contains no explicit schema, field bounds, fragment ID, object-store identity, ETag or file version. The supplied LanceCache may add a namespace; this local adapter adds no invalidation or persistent codec. Cached statistics absence is an Option value. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:68-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:181-198; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-288)

A cache miss reads the last min(file_size, block_size) bytes, extracts the eight-byte metadata position at footer[-16..-8], and either fetches the earlier framed struct or decodes its tail slice. That helper checks at least 16 tail bytes but does not check magic/version. Tail-position arithmetic and in-buffer framing do not locally guard malformed offsets/lengths; they can panic before decoding returns an error. Do not infer current-reader footer validation from this V1 path. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:210-234; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:221-231; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:248-263)

Statistics opening loads one batch covering field IDs 0 through max(leaf_field_ids), panicking on an empty leaf-ID list. page_stats_schema matches requested data IDs against parsed statistics root names, then projects their IDs and immediate children. It retains schema order and can return Some(empty). read_page_stats returns None for absent table or empty projection; otherwise reads batch 0. A disagreement between caller metadata and the independently loaded statistics table can reach an unwrap. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-267; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:398-445)

## Read APIs and scheduling

The method and free read_batch use the explicit per-call schema, rather than the stored reader schema promised by the method comment. Empty projection returns InvalidInput; the free-function comment about a with_row_id flag and panic is obsolete. No upfront subset/type validation occurs. Root fields are read with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), and RecordBatch construction performs the final assembled-array check. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:324-335; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:485-507)

read_range immediately accepts any empty/reversed range as an empty batch, even beyond the end. Otherwise metadata splits across batches; reads are ordered and all results are retained. A single result is cloned; multiple results are concatenated in spawn_blocking. take first uses metadata grouping, which copies and sorts input, preserving duplicates but losing original order. It checks grouped batch IDs afterward, and its secondary offset check compares against whole-file length rather than batch length. Both APIs materialize the complete result; no local abort-on-drop mechanism is provided for blocking concat. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:128-194)

batches_stream lazily filters ascending batch IDs and requests complete batches with fixed outer concurrency 2. It owns reader/projection through Arcs and advertises the supplied Arrow schema. Inner field reads retain their own Reader parallelism. This function does not spawn a Tokio task; a separately inspected Dataset ranges_to_tasks wrapper does spawn per-range tasks. Do not merge their cancellation or scheduling contracts. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:448-483; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:158-186)

## Recursive reconstruction and edge cases

read_array dispatches by reconstructed DataType, not field.encoding: fixed stride first, then Null, the four byte-array types, Struct, Dictionary and the two variable-list widths. Unsupported types reach unimplemented. Every FSL enters fixed-stride dispatch regardless of its child; Interval has a width helper but is absent from that predicate. get_page_info reports missing field/batch entries as InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:509-576; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181)

| Type/path | Local reconstruction | Relevant boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed stride | Page position/length and selector go to plain codec | No field-nullability bitmap passed |
| Binary/string | Same, plus field.nullable | Equal offsets become null only when nullable |
| Dictionary | Plain keys plus cloned loaded values Arc | Missing dictionary/values unwraps |
| Struct | Sequential recursive child reads | No parent page/validity restored |
| Null | Synthesize count, no payload IO | End/max checks differ from plain; reversed range can underflow; Ranges panics |
| List/LargeList | Read offsets, read child values, normalize and build | Parent validity absent; reconstructed child is item/nullable=true |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:559-808; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229.

List range offsets include the terminal endpoint. Direct empty Indices accesses first/last and panics; public empty FileReader.take avoids per-column reads because grouping yields no groups. List Indices reads the whole first-to-last offset span, then sequentially reads each selected child range and concatenates; duplicates repeat those reads. Its offset lookup uses reader.page_table even when the function received another table, while child recursion uses that argument. Null selector validity is ignored on list and Null paths. Sortedness, arithmetic, child existence and offset coherence are caller/file assumptions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:370-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:578-623; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:689-807)

The list constructor chooses a child field named item with nullable=true from actual child data type. It does not preserve arbitrary child metadata/name/nullability or parent nullness. Struct reconstruction similarly supplies no parent validity. These are frozen representation and reconstruction limits, not promises made by current-format readers. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:671-686; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:724-738; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:795-807; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Twelve active tests pin stable cache discriminator strings; seven-row multi-batch numeric/string/dictionary take; nullable empty-string conversion; combined-input struct/list roundtrip; one-row struct/list slice; Null lengths and weak is_err boundaries; List/LargeList take; sliced list equality plus file size<1000; one-batch numeric range; even-batch stream order; Boolean take with 256-byte blocks; and a narrow file opened under a wider schema with explicit field bounds. They do not prove malformed-file safety, cache invalidation, cancellation, parent-null preservation, arbitrary selectors or full multi-fragment behavior. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:827-1562)

The Boolean test is active reader-level coverage: 5,000 modulo-5 bits, indices [2,4,5,8,4555], expected [false,false,true,false,true]. It supplements the commented-out codec-local test and does not assert actual IO request counts. The projection test writes only f50 from a 100-field schema, then opens with full schema but min=max=f50; it does not test projection from a physically 100-column file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:1459-1561)

Dependencies provide Arrow arrays/arithmetic/concat, borrowed async Reader/ObjectStore IO, Lance typed cache and metadata framing, tracing and boxed recursion/ordered futures. There is no local environment variable, Cargo feature, runtime registry, mutable global, unsafe block, durability commit or writer lifecycle. The generic offset type and private cache trait adapt existing implementations; they are not new-format plugin seams. Preserve historical behavior unless legacy repair is explicitly in scope. ## Ownership and configuration

FileWriter<M: ManifestProvider + Send + Sync> owns a Box<dyn Writer>, Schema, signed next batch ID, ordinary page table, cumulative metadata and optional statistics collector. Only object_writer is public; the provider is a PhantomData marker, not a runtime instance. The writer has no closed flag, custom Drop, abort guard or ownership-consuming finish. Replacing the public writer does not reset stored state. The ignored example is obsolete: actual calls are try_new, write with a slice, and async finish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:66-87; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:98-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:255-290)

FileWriterOptions has one field: collect_stats_for_fields. None selects every schema ID; Some(empty) disables statistics; nonempty IDs are projected with include_all_children=true before supported fields become collector builders. Unknown IDs are not explicitly rejected here. The collector may return None even after a nonempty request. The fully analyzed support predicate accepts Boolean, signed/unsigned integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, UTF8/Binary with both offset widths and Decimal128; it excludes several types that collect_statistics can independently dispatch, including timestamps, duration, dictionary and fixed binary. Do not equate dispatcher support with automatic collection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:89-137; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:440-455; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:550-633)

try_new creates the target object before constructing local state. with_object_writer accepts an arbitrary writer position and supplied schema without validation or dictionary hydration. There is no local environment variable, version selector, compression setting or memory budget. Store creation/overwrite policy and backend cleanup are delegated and still require IO implementation analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:99-137)

## Per-call state transitions

| Stage | Effects and failure boundary |
|---|---|
| Empty input slice | Returns Ok without validation, stats, IO, flush or counter changes |
| Validate every input batch | Convert Arrow schema; compare with stored schema ignoring declared nullability, metadata, field IDs and dictionary contents; recursively reject actual nulls in stored nonnullable fields |
| Collect stats | One row per supported selected field for the entire slice; mutates builders before writes |
| Write roots sequentially | Clone schema fields, find batch columns by name, recursively encode all arrays at current batch ID; earlier page entries and bytes survive later failure |
| Append logical length | Unchecked i32 row casts/sum and cumulative offset mutation |
| Flush | Polls in-flight writer requests before caller regains control; a failure leaves cumulative metadata advanced |
| Advance batch ID | Happens only after successful flush |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:166-236. A single call with several batches creates one stored batch. A nonempty slice containing a zero-row batch still traverses encoding and advances the batch ID on success; it is not the empty-slice no-op. The zero-row UTF8 test explicitly reopens batch0. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:985-1014)

Schema comparison retains normal ordered name/logical-type/child matching, with the shared blob-child comparison exception inherited from Field. Recursive nullability checks zip field children with ArrayData child_data and inspect physical null counts without ancestor masks or list-child logical-span slicing. They do not independently validate counts; normal schema comparison occurs first. Dictionary equality is assumed by a comment to have been checked earlier, but this writer performs no comparison or unification. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:83-103; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:423-440; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:930-980; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:144-199)

Statistics traversal uses a LIFO stack: roots and struct children are visited in reverse schema order, structs are expanded without emitting their own node, and other nested types are skipped with descendants. It uses borrowed arrays, allocates per-field vectors and does no task spawning or ancestor-validity combination. Collector output ordering instead follows its BTreeMap by original field ID. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:654-692; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:612-670)

## Page grammar and recursive writes

```text
one nonempty write(slice)
+-- scalar/null root -> one (field ID, batch ID) PageInfo
+-- struct root
|   `-- each child recursively; no parent payload/validity page
+-- list root
|   +-- parent Int32 normalized offsets, logical row count + 1
|   `-- selected child spans recursively at same batch ID
`-- large-list root
    +-- parent Int64 normalized offsets, logical row count + 1
    `-- selected child spans recursively at same batch ID
```

Dispatch uses the first actual array DataType. Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary adapters assert the corresponding field.encoding rather than return a validation error. Arrays are processed sequentially; boxed async recursion does not spawn a task. Unsupported final match returns Schema error. The earlier fixed-stride guard already covers FixedSizeList/FixedSizeBinary, so the later explicit arm adds no extra support. The binary-like predicate includes view types; the concrete legacy BinaryEncoder rejects views as InvalidInput and does not normalize them. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:292-391; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:406-459; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105)

| Adapter | Stored position and length | Additional contract |
|---|---|---|
| Null | Current cursor; logical row count | No payload or encoding-tag check |
| Plain | Encoder return at value bytes; logical elements | Assert Plain and nonempty input; validity is delegated to frozen codec semantics |
| Binary | Offset table after payload; logical elements | Assert VarBinary; absolute i64 offsets rather than a separate validity bitmap |
| Dictionary | Key bytes; logical keys | Values come from stored schema at footer time, not batch arrays |
| Struct | No parent page | Assert child count, find children by name and recurse; no parent validity |
| List/LargeList | Parent offset bytes; rows+1 | Normalize selected child spans; recursively write children[0]; no parent validity |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-586; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-87. PageInfo length is not encoded byte length. Counts and offsets use unchecked casts/sums; encoding errors may occur after bytes are written but before the current page entry is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

List writers retain each sliced values array from first through final offset, excluding outside tails but retaining storage inside null-list spans. They append initial zero and normalized offsets using usize arithmetic, then cast to i32/i64. Builder capacity is rows although rows+1 positions are appended. Position bytes/table entry precede child writes, so child failure leaves partial output. children[0] is unchecked, and no list validity is persisted. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:491-586)

## Footer, provider and shutdown

```text
ordinary data pages, written across calls
`-- finish()
    +-- ordinary dense PageTable, minimum schema field ID
    +-- optional statistics arrays and separate PageTable at batch 0
    +-- schema dictionary values; update stored offset/length metadata
    +-- M::store_schema -> optional schema/manifest position
    +-- u32 LE framed Metadata protobuf
    +-- i64 LE metadata position, i16 LE 0, i16 LE 2, "LANC"
    `-- Writer::shutdown -> authoritative size_bytes
```

The minimum schema field ID includes struct roots and is unwrapped; an empty schema panics. A nonempty schema with no page entries returns the page-table empty InvalidInput. Holes and parent fields are represented by the dense page-table contract; the writer does not add alignment padding. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:83-106; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

Statistics finish mutates builders before writing any statistics bytes. A debug assertion compares stats rows to the next batch ID. Every root is written recursively under batch0 in a separate table; the field list named leaf_field_ids actually comes from all preorder schema IDs, including struct roots. Original data field IDs are encoded as statistics root names; newly converted statistics-schema IDs index statistics pages. None/zero-row collector output omits metadata; errors propagate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:588-625; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:600-604; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:635-670)

ManifestProvider is a public static async hook accepting &mut dyn Writer and &Schema, returning Result<Option<usize>>. The caller writes dictionaries first and trusts the returned position. Table ManifestDescribing creates a V1 Manifest with no fragments, then calls do_write_manifest directly with no indices/transaction, so dictionaries are not written a second time. The test-only NotSelfDescribing returns None and writes nothing. Metadata serialization maps None to zero; it is not an on-disk option-presence bit. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:35-64; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:639-650; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:177-230; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-250; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-75)

finish uses shutdown's authoritative size and the last cumulative row count, returning FileWriteSummary. It does not call tell afterward or retain other object identity fields. finish_with_metadata extends schema metadata first; both it and add_metadata overwrite duplicate keys. Failed/repeated finish is not locally guarded, and stats/dictionary/schema/footer side effects are not rolled back. No local abort or deletion follows cancellation; underlying Writer behavior remains a separate dependency. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:238-290; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:588-651)

## Manifest read lifecycle

read_manifest trusts optional size or HEADs for it, requests last64KiB, retries once without known size only after successful bytes fail minimum16/magic checks, then uses signed LE footer offset as usize. It does not inspect footer version bytes or invoke feature capability gates. Bounds arithmetic is unchecked: malformed offsets or a trimmed body too short for prefix+footer can panic via arithmetic/slices. Length mismatch after trimming is InvalidInput; short-tail/wrong-magic and slow-path minimum20 are CorruptFile(path). GET errors and decode errors do not trigger cached-size retry. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:32-128)

For a larger body it opens a sized reader and accumulates16MiB chunks in file order under bounded concurrency, appends tail and decodes through ChunkedBuf without one full concatenation. All body chunks are retained before Prost decoding, so this is not bounded-memory streaming parsing. Within-chunk Bytes fields can share backing; cross-boundary copy_to_bytes allocates. After conversion detach_sparse_inline_row_ids copies nonzero inline total when less than one quarter of recorded message length, reducing retained backing at a transient copy cost. Performance numbers in source comments are not measurements here. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:75-127; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:19-159; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:391-419)

read_manifest_indexes has a different retry: only a known size plus exact error-text substring file size is too small causes a second read without hint. Missing index_section returns empty without IO. It converts every metadata entry but does not verify uniqueness or dataset feature compatibility. Private read_index_section opens the selected view and invokes length-prefixed generic read_message. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:129-175; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:161-199)

## Manifest write lifecycle

V1 default format first writes schema dictionaries; exact V2 variants skip that step. do_write_manifest writes Some index vector even if empty, or clears inherited offset for None; then does the same for optional inline transaction; finally writes manifest. Successful earlier writes and offset mutations are not rolled back by later error/cancellation. The returned position is where the manifest length prefix begins. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:177-230; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:53-63; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:84-92)

Contextual canonical writer creates ObjectWriter, calls this body writer, appends footer via WriteExt, shuts down and only then logs create. It uses lance-file footer constants0/2/LANC, whereas table format facade declares0/1/LANC; read_manifest checks neither pair. Commit handler selection and local publication are now covered in the [commit supplement](rust-lance-table-commit.md). ManifestDescribing is a legacy V1 schema-only provider and directly calls do_write_manifest on a fresh V1 envelope. (rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:31-40; rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:199-230; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:95-107; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33; rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:51-56; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-251)

## Deletion path and representation

Paths combine supplied base with _deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{random_id}.arrow or .bin. base_id is ignored locally; caller must select directory/store. NoDeletions returns None; explicit Set(empty) and Bitmap(empty) still write. Representation is chosen by enum arm, not density at IO time. Set serialization uses unspecified HashSet order and a single Arrow IPC ZSTD batch with nonnullable row_id:UInt32. Bitmap serializes Roaring as-is with no explicit run optimization. Every payload is built in Vec before one put. (rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:25-134)

Array reader loads full object and all batches before checking exactly one batch and exact schema equality. It deduplicates offsets into HashSet, rejects nulls, and returns Set without normalization. Bitmap reader wraps Roaring errors with path and returns Bitmap. Neither validates physical bounds or num_deleted_rows, resolves base_id, or explicitly checks trailing bytes after Roaring decode. A malformed Arrow iterator error becomes CorruptFile(path), while constructor error uses generic conversion. Guarded unwraps rely on count/schema checks. (rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:135-216)

Contextual dataset reader resolves directory before cache lookup, uses DeletionFileKey, and on miss resolves store, reads and inserts Arc vector. It is get-then-read-then-insert, with no explicit single-flight in that wrapper. Fragment write_deletions drops a fully deleted fragment; when count>=physical but coverage differs it errors; otherwise writes metadata. That count-conditional check does not locally reject every out-of-range offset in a smaller set. These callers are contextual and remain pending whole-file analysis. (rust/lance/src/io/deletion.rs:11-43; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:3004-3035)

## Dependencies, extensibility and verification limits

Manifest depends on ObjectStore/Writer/CommitHandler location metadata, Prost and table codecs; chunk concurrency follows Reader::io_parallelism with minimum1. Deletion depends on Arrow IPC ZSTD and Roaring formats, core DeletionVector and audit tracing. Object-store implementations and Writer trait are storage extension boundaries; neither reviewed file declares environment settings or an index/encoding registry. Legacy ManifestProvider adapts the old writer and remains frozen compatibility scope. ## Preparation and ownership

prepare_indices runs tagged admission before cloning, derives physically rewritten columns and only then decodes/uses lineage if necessary; it preserves originals for coverage comparison. Supplied decoded ledger supports external history, while this method itself does no history IO. PreparedIndices binds only optional numeric manifest version. build_manifest_prepared checks that version, repeats admission and consumes original/prepared/reuse vectors. It does not bind source dataset identity or prove caller-supplied ledger/assembly correctness. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:453-522; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:580-611)

Convenience build_manifest supplies no read state; build_manifest_with_read_version prepares without ledger or settled FRI intent. External history rejection is conditional on actual rewrite decoding, not every operation on a tagged table. Normal dataset IO prepare_attempt loads current indices, and for Update with modified fields or Merge/DataReplacement loads first tagged ledger before calling preparation. This is a contextual caller excerpt, not complete retry analysis. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:527-577; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1470-1513)

## Finalization ordering and boundaries

After dispatch: stable-sort fragments by ID without deduplication; prune all-tombstone base files; reject overlay order violations; validate spilled carriers. Derive MemWAL catchup only if original list contained system metadata. Promote legacy blob schema roots referenced by V2_2/V2_3 files; choose Manifest constructor/default storage; set tag, optional auto flags, covering flags, sticky flags, timestamp and max fragment ID. Apply operation config/field metadata; range conversion; base additions; reservation; transaction path and next-row watermark; paired tagged flags; return. Later errors discard local candidate, not mutate current manifest. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1571-1919)

Config has distinct effects: existing stable reader flag keeps allocation active even when use_stable_row_ids=false, but RewriteRows index reuse additionally requires config true. Explicit storage_format wins over use_legacy_format; on an existing dataset only Overwrite applies requested default locally. disable_transaction_file influences feature derivation but final transaction_file is always Some supplied path. Primary/clustering guards reject reserved-key touches on established keys even if unchanged; only primary-key install calls schema verification. ## Failure and performance considerations

Local allocations include cloned manifest/index/fragment vectors, coverage bitmaps, name/ID maps and sorted offset Vecs. Delete uses lookup maps; selected offset updates still linearly locate original physical_rows for each target. Range conversion compares raw byte-start pointers without dereference and skips same backing by fragment ID only when both manifests opt in; it decodes all other inline data and uses copy-on-write fragments. No unsafe block is present. Integer high-water increments and several u64-to-u32 casts are unchecked. Partial Update's fallback bound is1<<24, while overlay stamping delegates its own bounds to row-version helper. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:81-141; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:691-752; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:776-928; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1507-1540; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1872-1943)

InvalidInput/NotSupported errors guard prepared version, admission/migration, base declarations, replacement layouts, offset bounds, missing overlay targets and key edits; helper errors propagate from decoding, row-version operations and validation.
