## Alignment and shared future lifecycle

MergeStream keeps one pending chunk from each input. It emits the minimum remaining count, splitting bigger chunks with shared futures and Arrow slices. A whole unsplit task moves its original future directly. Split errors become Wrapped with the original Error reachable through SharedReadError::source. Input task order determines column merge order; FuturesOrdered yields component results in that order. Any input stream ending stops the merge without checking remaining totals. Zero-row tasks are allowed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:41-216)

The outer stream does not await batch data; emitted futures perform the actual merge. Dropping one split future does not itself invalidate another shared handle, and retained slices can retain the whole source batch. Declared sizes must match actual data or slicing can panic; equal actual lengths are checked by RecordBatchExt::merge. Matching field names are not simple concatenation: nested structures may merge and other conflicts keep the left column. Left schema metadata survives. Certain nested-list merge branches can panic; those dependency internals are only contextually read, not fully analyzed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:90-159; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:653-673; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1227-1328)

## Ordered expansion, read-ahead and schema reuse

The wrapper chooses dense versus ordinary row-ID cursor expansion once, then expands IDs and multi-run versions while pulling tasks in order. Batch futures may complete concurrently without sharing mutable cursors. Metadata Results are captured in those futures: an input batch error propagates first and can mask a precomputed metadata error. Work done while pulling can be discarded if a future is never consumed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:648-691; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:692-848)

Uniform nonzero task sizes enable a 65,536-row read-ahead target and shared output-schema cache. Chunks are aligned to whole batches, capped by selected rows left; a larger task can exceed the target. A nonfinal size change permanently disables both fast paths after draining any usable cached ID chunk. Zero-size tasks do not alter the inferred size; a different final size is allowed. A batch straddling chunks copies its prefix and suffix; fitting slices share storage. Retained output futures/batches can hold multiple old buffers, so the current chunk is not a global memory cap. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:378-405; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:692-798)

The OnceLock caches the first completing batch's input/output schemas. Pointer-identical or structurally equal later schemas reuse its output Arc; differing schemas receive a fresh schema without replacing the cache. This path appends fields directly. The incremental fallback instead calls try_with_column repeatedly, which explicitly rejects duplicate names. Do not assume identical malformed-input behavior for both assembly paths. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:592-634; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:639-644; rust/lance-arrow/src/schema.rs:146-157)

## Selection, errors and deletion semantics

Selection offsets count rows in the requested selection, while ranges/indices identify physical positions in the sequence. Helpers slice params then often unwrap Results, so invalid selection can panic despite a Result-returning public transformer. ReadBatchParams materializers use raw index values and unchecked u32 endpoint conversions; the local total count is primarily a read-ahead estimate. The wrapper checks decoded stable-ID count and returns named CorruptFile on truncation. The direct fallback lacks that exact chunk check. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:266-315; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:407-545; rust/lance-io/src/lib.rs:156-219; rust/lance-io/src/lib.rs:248-277)

A one-run version sequence repeats its value without validating the run length against selection. Its O(1) comment concerns locating a version, not allocating/filling the output vector. Multi-run streaming reuses version cursors; direct calls create a new cursor and repeat selection construction. System columns appear in ID, address, last-updated, created order after payload. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:266-315; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:553-591; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:681-690)

Deletion predicates use physical addresses regardless of stable IDs. Some(NoDeletions) is normalized away. Filter mode removes rows from every column; null mode keeps physical length and combines existing validity with deletion validity only for _rowid/_rowaddr. Payload and version values remain present under deleted rows. If no ID/address field is present, null mode has no identifying null output; test code treats that as an upstream-invalid configuration, but production code does not reject it. Empty filtered batches are returned. ## State, errors and allocation boundaries

apply validates sticky pairing before mutation, then resets both words and derives content flags. Missing row IDs can fail after reset/deletion writes. Covered metadata is normalized from either word into both, whereas mismatched mixed/tagged-FRI bits fail. inherit validates only source paired bits and ORs8/10 into destination; it neither clears destination nor validates its other bits. ensure validates pairing before returning NotSupported for the selected unsupported word. (rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:127-232; rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:309-378)

The gates perform synchronous predicates over existing metadata and environment; apply repeatedly scans fragment lists and does not perform IO. InlineRowIds owns an Arc inner containing Bytes plus OnceLock<[u8;32]>. digest() borrows the memoized BLAKE3 digest of encoded bytes; bytes() borrows Bytes, and Deref exposes immutable [u8]. Clone shares memo and Bytes handle, while separately constructed equal contents use separate memos. Equality uses Arc identity or byte comparison, not the digest. Debug/serde show only bytes; Deserialize reconstructs from Vec and a fresh memo. This is encoded-content identity rather than guaranteed collision-free logical-sequence identity. (rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:49-126)

Memory sizing deduplicates the inner Arc in a Context, counts inner inline storage (including OnceLock), then delegates to Bytes. ## Fragment and manifest metadata

[Fragment L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs.md) and [Manifest L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs.md) preserve every line plus authored algorithms, error branches, ownership and test limits. All public fragment declarations are facade-reexported. Manifest's explicit facade exports omit ManifestSummary and VersionPart even though they are pub in their private defining module; summary callers can infer its return type and access public fields. (rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:7-25; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:130-171; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:762-767)

DataFile owns a path, shared field/column-index arrays, exact file numbers, cached size and optional external base ID. Constructors and protobuf/JSON conversions do not validate these lists. validate checks live V1 field IDs strictly increase after removing tombstones, or for other encodings checks column_indices.len>=fields.len. Extra columns are allowed. Exact version decoding is a separate file_version call. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:28-169; rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:241-310)

Projection is version-sensitive: V1 delegates Schema::project_by_ids; other layouts zip field IDs to nonnegative column indices. Blob/packed struct is atomic by own mapped ID; ordinary structural fields retain only mapped descendants, except V2.0 raw pairs(0,3)/(2,0) preserve a mapped parent header even when all children disappeared. This prevents substituting evolved children into an old file's projection. Metadata projection does not itself materialize nulls. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:171-239)

Fragment::referenced_lance_files yields base files then overlay files; use it for operations needing every Lance file. This supports exact-version inference, manifest max-field-ID calculation and shallow-clone base-ID rewriting. Lineage carrier lookup deliberately scans base files only. Column lineage metadata must have exactly one carrier and a non-V1 decoded version under validate_row_lineage_carriers; missing carrier is Internal, duplicated carriers CorruptFile. The lookup alone returns None for absence and checks no column index. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:589-725; rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:800-828; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:249-268; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:466-485)

DataFileFieldInterner has independent field-ID and column-index caches and one shared created/updated inline-version byte cache. Each starts a linear Vec search and promotes on its 17th unique value to HashMap, with no eviction. Manifest decoding creates one interner across fragments. Row-ID Bytes and overlay field lists are not interned through these caches. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:312-462; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:987-993)

Manifest new starts version1 with zero feature words and absent section references. new_from_previous increments dataset version, refreshes writer library version, retains only sticky paired capabilities in each word and clears timestamp/index/transaction references. shallow_clone retains source version/time and covered-index plus sticky bits, stamps local base/overlay/deletion references with the supplied base ID, replaces that base-map entry if already present, and performs no IO. Pair validity and capability support remain separate checks. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:173-308)

Protobuf manifest conversion requires row-ID metadata on every fragment only when the reader stable-row bit is set. Missing data_format infers one exact version across base/overlay files; with no files it falls back to current stable if deprecated writer bit2 is present, otherwise V1. Explicit data_format is parsed without cross-checking file versions. Encoding always writes an exact format string and fragment_tree=None; serialized() returns protobuf bytes, not the full manifest file framing. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:542-552; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:963-1124)

Offsets are cached N+1 logical prefix sums, treating unknown row counts as zero. Fragment::num_rows is known physical count minus known deletions, or None if insufficient metadata; counts can underflow on invalid inputs. Public replacement of manifest.fragments does not refresh private offsets. summary counts base files and their known sizes only; overlays are excluded. It derives data-file rows from known live+deleted counts, which need not equal total physical rows with unknown metadata. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:573-586; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:117-128; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:505-598)

detach_sparse_inline_row_ids copies row-ID Bytes only when nonzero combined visible length is strictly less than a quarter of caller-supplied buffer_len. Otherwise slices remain. Copy-on-write protects a shared fragment Arc and new wrappers get fresh digest memos. This is a retention policy, not a guarantee all owners release the old buffer. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:391-419; rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:75-84)

WriterVersion stores library, clean version and separate pre/build fields; lance_lib_version accepts only library lance, parses with semver, and overwrites embedded components when separate fields are present. Deprecated semver uses a different lenient three-u32 parser, while deprecated bump/older_than can panic. This crate's cfg(test) default uses Cargo version patch+1; normal default uses Cargo version directly. DataStorageFormat default delegates to stable_file_version, now resolved as exact V2_2 (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-22). (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:678-724; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:786-940)

SelfDescribingFileReader is a trait with an ObjectStore-opening default and a required reader constructor. Its only implementation in this file is the frozen V1 adapter: read metadata, require embedded manifest position, read manifest, hydrate V1 dictionaries, then initialize V1 reader. V2 dictionary hydration is a no-op; no V2 self-describing reader is implemented here. ManifestBuildConfig documents caller-provided clock, overwrite format selection, stable-row migration and prefetched lineage but enforces none itself. ## Index, overlay and conflict-key metadata

[Index metadata](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md), [overlay metadata](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs.md) and [key existence](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs.md) now have full physical-line analysis. Index types/codec/listing are facade reexports from a private module; overlay and key_existence are public modules. (rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:7-30)

IndexMetadata separates all dependency fields from the keyed prefix: covering_fields must be a duplicate-free proper suffix unless empty. Decode validates missing IDs first, duplicates second, all-fields coverage third and exact suffix order last. keyed_fields only subtracts lengths saturating at zero; direct construction bypasses validation. keyed_field is Some only for exactly one keyed column. No schema membership or overall fields uniqueness is checked. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:156-243; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:261-317)

Coverage None means unknown; effective/deleted bitmap methods compute intersection/difference with caller-supplied live fragments. Files None means unknown, but repeated-field encoding also loses Some(empty). file_size_map overwrites duplicate paths whereas total_size_bytes counts them all. list_index_files_with_sizes collects the recursive-list stream, aborts on error and derives paths with string prefix stripping; store traversal implementation remains pending. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:96-135; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:273-286; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:338-350; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:417-442)

results_are_row_addrs recognizes ZoneMap/Bloom by case-sensitive suffix and FM by a slash-delimited, case-insensitive full protobuf type name. It inspects only Any.type_url, not contents or ScalarIndex behavior. The Vec metadata codec uses type ID lance.table.IndexMetadataList, body version1, and a length-prefixed protobuf IndexSection. Wrong-type serialization and invalid timestamp conversion can panic; ordinary conversion errors propagate. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:137-154; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:299-313; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:371-415; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:62-71)

Overlay metadata covers physical offsets including deleted rows. Value rows correspond to zero-based rank in a field's bitmap; equal versions resolve by later list position. Shared coverage applies to all fields, while PerField must remain position-aligned. sort_overlays_newest_last is stable; verification rejects only descending versions. coverage_for_field bounds-checks the bitmap Vec only for PerField and never checks DataFile field bounds. Required protobuf options and bitmap syntax are checked, but shape/rank/physical bounds are not. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:192-240; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:297-327)

tombstone_overlay_fields replaces selected nonnegative IDs with-2 without moving coverage or column slots, then removes overlays with no field unequal to-2. It rebuilds every field array and performs no physical deletion. Roaring serialization clones/optimizes bitmaps; parsing errors carry a data-file path for protobuf and an empty path for isolated serde. DeepSizeOf counts each Arc bitmap once per Context plus sparse handle capacity, using serialized bytes as a heap proxy. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:76-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:242-295)

KeyExistenceFilterBuilder uses a fixed8192-item/0.00057 Sbbf configuration and counts insert calls, not unique keys. build preserves that configuration, serializes bitmap bytes and clones field IDs. KeyValue explicitly encodes little-endian64-bit integers, raw string/binary bytes, or child-byte concatenations with zero delimiters. No type tags or escaping make this encoding non-injective. hash_value uses DefaultHasher on these bytes; Sbbf uses its own xxHash64 path. (rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:26-148; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:297-337)

intersects Exact/Exact returns shared-hash presence with false-positive flag false; mixed filters always return(true,true); Bloom/Bloom checks configuration and equal byte lengths through the core helper, then any shared bit returns(true,true), otherwise(false,false). It ignores field IDs and num_bits. Protobuf decode defaults only zero capacity/probability and maps missing data to empty exact set without bitmap validation. (rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:150-280; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/sbbf.rs:399-417)

extract_key_value_from_batch resolves ordered top-level names; missing name, outer/child NULL, no columns or unsupported type returns None. Supported values are Utf8/LargeUtf8, Binary/LargeBinary, signed/unsigned32/64-bit integers, List/LargeList and Struct recursively. A single ON column remains scalar; multiple become Composite. Row bounds are not checked locally. These helpers do not enforce primary-key eligibility or define transaction retry/abort behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:282-389)

## Overlay-induced index staleness

[Staleness L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs.md) calculates exclusion sets using metadata only. Newer means overlay.committed_version > segment.dataset_version, not > index_version algorithm revision. Fields are segment.fields including covering dependencies. For each changed field it matches exact ID, indexed ancestor or indexed descendant using Schema ancestry; siblings alone do not match. Union only that field position's coverage. No deleted-row removal or actual flat-path query occurs here. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:24-85; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:113-157; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:633-648)

overlaid_fragments scans all fragments into borrowed HashMap keyed by truncating id as u32; duplicates overwrite. Missing segment.fragment_bitmap is conservatively all-covered, while Some excludes absent IDs. Fragment collector skips already-stale IDs and adds only nonempty exclusions; row collector unions nonempty offset bitmaps into existing map entries. Errors can leave earlier fragments mutated, with no rollback; map keys are trusted independently of Fragment.id. Both collectors return Result, not a complete query plan. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:88-158)

The version-only early return avoids schema work when all overlays are old/equal. Otherwise field-ancestry traversal may repeat and allocate inside nested loops; O(overlaid fragments) in comments is only the outer traversal bound. No sorted-order requirement, global latest-write elimination or value equality comparison changes the union. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:42-85; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:96-158; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:634-647)

Exact version delegation is now resolved in [lance-file](rust-lance-file.md): DataFile metadata writes V2_0 as(2,0), while standard file footer writes(0,3); both decode as V2_0. Manifest strict version string is2.0 and stable fallback/default is2.2. Capability support remains separate from identity recognition. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-261; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:708-722)

## Row versions: positional values and preloaded lineage

[Version L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs.md) covers public rowids::version; format reexports RowDatasetVersionMeta, RowDatasetVersionRun and RowDatasetVersionSequence. LoadedRowLineage has optional Arc row_ids/created_at/last_updated_at, and SpilledRowLineage maps u64 fragment IDs to those values for synchronous commit preparation. The declaration supplies no IO loader. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24; rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:15-17; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:25-42)

Each version run has a U64Segment span and one u64 dataset version. Readers concatenate span lengths, ignoring absolute span coordinates; local tests deliberately use overlapping coordinates. Constructors support empty, uniform and RLE-from-values forms. version_at scans runs linearly; get_version_for_row_id finds a row-ID segment position then calls it. Threshold filtering zips row IDs and versions and silently stops at the shorter sequence. No alignment validation is implicit. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:44-80; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:212-313; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:890-914)

The crate-internal cursor caches position/run length for adjacent requests. First rewind builds O(runs) starts; later nonadjacent requests use binary search plus a walk over duplicate starts. Empty spans are skipped. It appends to a caller Vec and can leave partial output/progress on bounds error; empty/reversed selections are no-ops. The cursor is not tied to a source identity or lifetime, so changing/replacing the sequence invalidates its caches. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:82-210)

VersionsIter differs: it advances at most one run when a run is exhausted. If that next run is empty, it still returns its version once. A length1/version7 run followed by length0/version9 therefore yields7,9; this is a control-flow deduction, not an executed test. mask removes empty spans but direct construction and decoding do not. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:314-390; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:537-559)

Inline metadata shares Arc bytes; Column is a marker for hidden creation/update fields. JSON is an untagged inline byte list or column empty object. Inline decoding can fail; load_sequence(Column) is NotSupported. Protobuf arm conversions copy/move bytes without validation, and write/read sequence functions use repeated protobuf runs with nested spans. Nested codecs now establish LE arrays, LSB bitmap bytes and validated segment conversion; standalone Ranges serialization panics, so version spans with that variant cannot pass this writer. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:98-338) (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:392-559; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:818-847)

| Helper | Count and update behavior | Failure/memory boundary |
|---|---|---|
| build_version_meta | Known positive physical rows -> uniform inline metadata; does not inspect existing version metadata | Panics if row-ID metadata missing; unknown/zero count -> None |
| Full rewrite refresh | Physical count first; otherwise inline row-ID length; column/absent ->0. Positive count overwrites all last-updated versions | Inline row-ID decode unwrap can panic; zero count preserves existing metadata |
| Partial rewrite refresh | Same count priority, but column row IDs without count error. Preserve/pad base values then patch valid offsets and RLE inline | Column versions require preload; inline decode errors silently default. O(rows) vector; excess offsets ignored; old metadata changes only at final assignment |

The table follows rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:654-815. None of these helpers checks monotonic current_version, touches created_at, changes feature flags or deletes a former column file. Complete transaction trigger/retry policy is still pending.

rechunk_version_sequences slices owned run spans by positional length into every requested chunk. allow_incomplete permits short/empty outputs on input exhaustion, but excess input is always an error, including a leftover empty run. Zero-sized requested chunks do not consume runs. It collects all chunk sizes/results and does not merge adjacent equal versions. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:561-652)

## HoleRuns: missing offsets with rank/select

[Runs L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs.md) covers a pub struct inside private rowids::runs. Private fields retain span:u32, starts and present-before prefix counts; ends are reconstructed. try_new rejects unequal bounds, empty/reversed/out-of-span runs, overlap, ordering violations and adjacency. CorruptFile uses the name row ID metadata. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:14-81; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:13-17)

position maps present offset to ordinal; offset_at is its inverse. Both use partition_point and return None for out-of-range/hole values. present_ranges is lazy and double-ended. extend_values clips its ordinal end, searches once and streams base+offset gaps into an existing Vec; arithmetic is unchecked. Bitmap conversion scans whole bytes and only branches per bit at mixed edges, treating padding as present; its documented u32-length precondition is not checked. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:83-215)

## Row-ID bitmaps, arrays and codec boundary

[Bitmap L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs.md), [array L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs.md) and [codec L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs.md) cover private child modules. read_row_ids/write_row_ids have a public reexport, while Bitmap and EncodedU64Array do not have public module routes. The exact signatures below distinguish local pub declarations, crate/super visibility and public trait implementations. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-33)

Bitmap stores Vec bytes plus logical len. Bit i uses byte i/8 and mask1<<(i%8); constructors zero padding. Direct fields/from_parts/slice/access do not enforce logical bounds. Full popcount counts every storage bit, but iteration truncates to len and can underproduce when storage is short. BitmapSlice borrows coordinates and counts edge/middle bytes; converting it back to Bitmap copies selected bits into fresh storage. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:7-179)

EncodedU64Array owns U16/U32 base-relative offsets or U64 values. Vec conversion uses inclusive max-minus-min thresholds, preserves input order and chooses U16 even for a singleton. Range conversion materializes all values and instead uses strict range-length thresholds. Compressed slicing decodes/rebases; U64 slicing stays U64. min on nonempty deltas returns base without scanning, assuming an offset0 that decoded/direct values need not have. binary_search assumes sortedness. Borrowed/owned iterators are boxed. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs:8-254; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:174-214)

The decoder checks reverse ranges, required oneofs/holes, packed widths, base+maximum offset overflow, sorted strictness/hole bounds, bitmap length/padding and total u64 length. It hand-parses only outer field1/LengthDelimited and rejects other outer fields; plain positive ranges bypass generated message allocation and feed folding. Adjacent ranges merge; overlap/out-of-order flushes instead of rejecting. Compact grouping accepts at least two ranges whose enclosing span fits u32 and gap validation succeeds; it does not compare wire cost. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:245-266) (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:19-230; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:346-426)

Sequence serialization clones all segments, expands Ranges into ordinary wire Range messages, then encodes protobuf. Standalone U64Segment serialization panics for Ranges; version-run writer calls that path directly. Packed arrays are little-endian. Bitmap bytes are LSB-first in implementation/test, contradicting the MSB-first schema comment; use the implementation evidence to describe this checkout and retain the discrepancy until historical compatibility is examined. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:232-344; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:436-451; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:520-535; protos/rowids.proto:51-58)

## U64Segment: encoding choices and positional operations

[Segment L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs.md) covers public rowids::segment, including U64Segment and a borrowing SegmentCursor; SegmentCursorState is crate-visible. The nearby parent comment calls structures private, but segment is declared pub. Variants expose bounds and bitmap/array/runs values without an invariant-checking constructor barrier. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:40-82; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-768)

from_slice/FromIterator collect values and scan min/max/count/nondecreasing order. Unsorted chooses Array. Sorted empty becomes Range0..0, contiguous distinct values become Range when max+1 fits, and values ending at u64MAX always use SortedArray. Other sorted values select the minimum estimated cost below, with ties favoring holes then bitmap then array. The estimate is heuristic: actual compressed array widths and protobuf overhead differ. | SortedArray |24 +2 × value count | Encode collected values using actual U16/U32/U64 choice |

Cost arithmetic uses u128 and saturates to usizeMAX; it does not validate duplicates, cap allocations or ensure32-bit span fit. Distinctness is a documented precondition. ## Segment cursors and dense byte expansion

Cursor state is byte index plus count of set bits in preceding bytes. Backward requests reset only when requested ordinal precedes that count; an early return in a target byte keeps state at its beginning. Ordinary extension walks set bits; dense extension uses whole-byte or contiguous-one-run expansion when a fully selected byte has at least six set bits. Both rely on zero padding and can emit malformed padding past logical end. Requests past EOF silently truncate. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-954)

The density advisory uses caller-supplied segment_len>=logical_len-floor(logical_len/4). It is separate from dense extension, which never checks density itself. SegmentCursor binds a shared borrow to one segment; SegmentCursorState accepts a new source on every call without resetting by identity, and nonbitmap operations leave old bitmap state intact. RowIdSequence cursor reset and density selection are now documented below; full stream ownership is now covered in the stream supplement. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:346-354; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-855; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:925-954)

## Cursor policy and ReadBatchParams adapter

get/range cursor operations rewind on backward requests, cache each segment length and reset SegmentCursorState when advancing. Reusing a cursor with changed/different sequence can retain wrong cached lengths/counters. Dense policy applies only to a single bitmap segment and seeds its computed cardinality; multi-segment sequences use sparse mode. Range selection preallocates requested cardinality even when EOF clips output. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:67-170; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:538-591)

| ReadBatchParams | Validation and order |
|---|---|
| Indices | Reads values buffer without validity check; sorted path validates last and uses cursor; unsorted path independent get; preserves duplicates |
| Range / RangeTo | Checks end only; reversed Range subtraction is unchecked |
| Ranges | Preallocates sum before per-range end validation; preserves supplied range order; casts u64 to usize |
| RangeFrom | No explicit start bound check; subtracting an excessive start can panic |

## ID masks, set conversion and rechunking

mask_to_offset_ranges returns ordered half-open ordinals grouped within each segment; adjacent groups across segment boundaries stay separate. Plain ranges walk tree-map runs. Holes remove missing IDs, sort decoded holes and subtract earlier-hole count. Bitmaps use finite allow IDs when allowed cardinality<=summed bitmap span: a single bitmap filters the iterator, multiple bitmaps cache sorted IDs once and binary-search subranges. Other masks fall back to a full-span set/bitmap scan. Ranges inserts present gaps and translates rank; arrays test mask membership in stored order. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:609-798)

The bitmap helper popcounts only intervals between selected present IDs, retaining the prior position so the next interval includes that selected bit. RowAddrMask cannot carry both allow and block lists simultaneously. The dependency row_addrs allocates a Vec of iterators even on the streaming path, so no-copy of all IDs is not zero allocation. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:843-863; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:24-79; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:497-515)

Set conversion unions independently built segment sets so one bitmap's holes cannot erase IDs belonging to another overlapping segment. Order and multiplicity disappear. Contextual dependency inspection exposes two edge cases: empty Range0..0 inserts0 through saturating excluded-end conversion, and mask's plain-range run-end expression mishandles a low32 carry for odd high32 values. These are source-derived, unexecuted counterexamples requiring dedicated regressions before any fix. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:621-646; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:865-905; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:545-588; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:801-810; rust/lance-select/src/mask.rs:1014-1019)

rechunk_sequences returns one sequence per requested size, consuming owned inputs. It slices/re-encodes even whole segments, so range input can materialize every row; it is not a metadata-only split. allow_incomplete permits short/empty outputs but not excess input. Empty input segments are skipped only while filling a positive remaining count; a trailing empty after the final full chunk still triggers too-many error. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:959-1052; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:378-387)

The narrowly read manifest helper gates use_range_segments through config key lance.row_ids.range_segments and str_is_truthy. It skips prior opted-in inline data by fragment ID and byte-start pointer, decodes other inline sequences and rewrites only if conversion changed; column metadata is skipped. The reviewed truthy helper accepts ASCII-case-insensitive 1/true/on/yes/y without trimming; other strings return false. ## Transaction row-ID allocation and creation lineage

[Complete row-version L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs.md) covers1,461 lines. The private transaction::row_version module exposes has_writer_placed_lineage through the public transaction facade; resolve_update_version_metadata and the two Transaction methods are pub(super), usable within transaction. All are synchronous and operate on supplied metadata/preloads. No store, feature gate, lock, retry or atomic commit appears in this file. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction.rs:29-54; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:12-19; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:73-96; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:298-405)

| New-fragment metadata | Creation behavior | Last-update behavior / validation |
|---|---|---|
| Creation Column, any row-ID state | Retain marker without decoding | build_version_meta(new_version); positive count without row-ID metadata can panic |
| Row-ID Column + creation Inline | Preserve supplied creation bytes | Decode and require creation count==physical_rows.unwrap_or(0); stamp new_version |
| Row-ID Column + no creation | Error | NotSupported |
| Row-ID Inline + creation Inline/None | Decode row IDs; recompute every creation value | Found source -> cached version or1; absent source -> new_version; debug-only count check |
| No row IDs or inline decode failure, with no creation Column | Uniform creation via build_version_meta | Uniform last update; malformed row-ID bytes remain unchanged; absent IDs with positive count can panic |

The table follows ordered match arms at rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:206-295 and delegated count/panic behavior at rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:655-678. Creation Column overrides other classification. Zero/unknown rows clear latest metadata to None through build_version_meta, while valid empty inline row IDs produce Some(empty creation sequence). These are local contracts; builder preparation can exclude malformed combinations.

Source discovery materializes distinct needed IDs in HashSet, sorts existing-fragment references by ID, and scans row sequences whose inclusive bounds overlap. ## Role and visibility

Public lance.table contracts for dataset manifests, index metadata, fragment-reuse mappings, and MemWAL shard/index state. This is a broad persisted-state schema; it records conflict-sensitive metadata but does not execute commits, recovery, fencing, or index catch-up. (protos/table.proto:1-769)

SPDX, proto3, lance.table, imports of Any, Timestamp and file.proto, and public import of fragment_metadata.proto establish type visibility. The public import makes the separated fragment definitions accessible through table.proto rather than redeclaring them. (protos/table.proto:1-12)

### Lines 13-35

The opening historical-looking layout diagram lists encoded chunks, indices, chunk-position matrix, optional manifest, metadata, i64 metadata position, version pair and LANC. It is not the newer file2 footer diagram and should not be applied to every current file. UUID is a message with bytes uuid=1 documented as exactly 16 bytes; no validation is implemented in protobuf. Manifest carries repeated lance.file.Field fields=1 including nested fields, repeated DataFragment fragments=2, uint64 version=3, uint64 version_aux_data=4, and bytes-valued schema_metadata map=5. fragment_tree=22 replaces the inline fragment list for tree tables: fragments must be empty and bit 12 set in both feature words so unaware readers do not see an empty dataset. Auxiliary data is version-specific, not inherited, and not loaded by default on query. (protos/table.proto:36-60)

### Lines 61-106

Nested WriterVersion stores library string=1, version string=2, optional prerelease string=3, optional build_metadata string=4. Version is a string because library versions may not be semver; semver has no leading v. New manifests should store core major.minor.patch in version and separate prerelease/build to remain parseable by older readers. Absent prerelease leaves version as-is, absent build means none. Manifest.writer_version=13 enables detection of files affected by writer-specific bugs; this is not itself a file-format gate. (protos/table.proto:61-106)

Manifest.index_section optional uint64=6 points to index metadata. timestamp=7 is a protobuf Timestamp documented UTC; tag string=8 is described as optional but has no explicit scalar presence, so empty and absent wire values are not distinguishable in the declaration. (protos/table.proto:107-115)

### Lines 116-139

reader_feature_flags uint64 tag 9 requires rejection when any set bit is unrecognized. The comment lists bit 0 deletions, 1 stable row IDs, 2 deprecated v2 indicator, 3 table config, 4 multiple bases, 5 disabled transaction-file writes, 6 overlays, 7 covering columns. Without bit 13, covering columns are the trailing fields suffix. Both readers and writers must reject unknown covering semantics to avoid querying/maintaining an index as if merely carried columns were indexed keys. (protos/table.proto:116-139)

### Lines 140-161

Bit 8 enables mixed recognized exact v2 data-file versions, paired in reader/writer flags and one-way; use each DataFile version rather than snapshot default for decoding. Bit 9 combines stable row IDs and a fragment reuse index. Bit 12 means fragment-tree records and empty fragments. Bit 13 independently declares key fields versus covering_fields; it requires bit 7 in both words, and both bits persist even after dropping the final covering index. One field may appear in both lists. Enabling bit 13 reinterprets every index entry, so normalize all legacy entries atomically (or enable only when none covers), retain the bit in descendants until an atomic reverse conversion. The list omits bit 11 although fragment_metadata separately documents spilled lineage at 2048; do not treat this comment as exhaustive (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51). ### Lines 406-444

FragmentReuseIndexDetails.content chooses InlineContent inline=1 or ExternalFile external=2; comment threshold is below 200 KB inline, otherwise external InlineContent bytes, with exact unit/threshold selection to verify in code. OrderedCompaction.changed_row_addrs bytes=1 is a RoaringTreemap of surviving source addresses; missing addresses are deleted. Legacy Group summarizes a rewrite with RoaringTreemap changed_row_addrs=1, old_fragments=2 and new_fragments=3; together these reconstruct old-to-new/deleted addresses for index remapping or queries against newly unindexed fragments. ### Lines 489-529

The MemWAL section introduces ShardStatus ACTIVE=0 and SEALED=1. Drop-table two-phase commit seals a shard to refuse claims reversibly, then deletes on commit or returns ACTIVE on rollback. ShardManifest documents exactly one active writer per shard; shard_id UUID=11 is v4, version uint64=1 matches manifest filename, shard_spec_id uint32=10 is immutable at creation with zero for manual/unmanaged shards, and shard_field_entries repeated=14 stores raw Arrow scalar bytes keyed by field ID and interpreted by ShardingSpec.result_type. The comment explicitly gives little-endian int32 and raw UTF-8 examples. (protos/table.proto:489-529)

### Lines 530-564

ShardManifest.writer_epoch uint64=2 is a monotonically increasing fencing token incremented on claim. replay_after_wal_entry_position uint64=3 is latest flushed WAL position; positions are one-based, zero means never flushed, replay begins at watermark+1. wal_entry_position_last_seen uint64=4 is only a hint; recovery must list storage, not trust it. current_generation uint64=6 numbers next SSTable and advances per MemTable flush. Removed field 7's progress now lives in index metadata, but this text does not reserve tag 7. sstables repeated=8 lists flush results. status ShardStatus=15 defaults ACTIVE; SEALED refuses claim_epoch. (protos/table.proto:530-564)

### Lines 565-575

ShardFieldEntry has field_id string=1 matching ShardingField.field_id and value bytes=2 in raw little-endian Arrow representation; matching result_type gives the data type. There is no self-describing per-value type tag here. (protos/table.proto:565-575)

### Lines 576-611

SsTable is an immutable flushed MemTable stored as a Lance dataset. generation uint64=1 and shard-relative path string=2 identify it. Optional in_memory_bytes=3 estimates accounted buffer windows, excluding reader array structure and requiring headroom; absent means unknown, not zero. Optional physical_rows=4 includes older primary-key duplicates masked by its deletion vector. Optional primary_key_bytes=5 sums key-column payload over all physical rows, is not per-row/encoded-sort-key size, and is also absent without a primary key. Treating these estimates as hard bounds or defaults as zero risks underbudgeting. (protos/table.proto:576-611)

### Lines 612-635

CompactedSsTable has shard_id UUID=1 and generation uint64=2 for latest compaction into base data. IndexCatchupProgress has base index_name=1 (must match maintained_indexes) and caught_up_generations repeated=2. The protobuf comment says an absent shard means unknown progress, requiring retained SSTables and repair. This conflicts with the Rust getter comment saying absence is assumed fully caught up; the getter itself simply returns None (rust/lance-table/src/system_index/mem_wal.rs:157-164). Complete consumers must resolve policy; neither comment proves safe deletion. (protos/table.proto:612-635)

### Lines 636-670

MemWalIndexDetails centralizes configuration, base compaction progress, and shard snapshots. Writers read configuration; snapshots are point-in-time optimizations, while readers requiring current shards list directories and latest shard manifests. Background refresh does not make snapshots authoritative mutable shard state. Snapshot Lance-file schema lists shard_id utf8, shard_spec_id uint32, typed shard_field_{id}. snapshot_ts_millis int64=1 and num_shards uint32=2 describe it; optional inline_snapshots bytes=3 holds Lance bytes for small counts. The threshold example 100 is explicitly implementation-defined, not a specified constant. (protos/table.proto:636-670)

### Lines 671-697

sharding_specs repeated=7 configures partitioning. maintained_indexes repeated string=8 names base indices mirrored in MemTables; primary-key btree is implicit and must not be listed; vector quantization parameters are inherited for comparable distances. maintain_all_indexes optional bool=12 selects automatic eligible-index discovery according to prose: the named list is ignored, new/dropped indices follow current table state, unsupported kinds are skipped. Absent uses the explicit list and unsupported requested names error. The comment does not separately define present-false handling; inspect runtime conversion before asserting whether 'set' means presence or true. (protos/table.proto:671-697)

### Lines 698-723

compacted_sstables repeated=9 updates atomically with merge-insert data commits for concurrent-compactor conflict resolution, independently of background shard snapshots. index_catchup repeated=10 records asynchronous base-index rebuild coverage. When catch-up generation trails compaction, indexed readers use SSTable indices for the gap. Missing index progress keeps needed SSTables live until repair. Only the dedicated WAL repair path adds progress; ordinary index-changing operations remove entries because they cannot attest coverage. (protos/table.proto:698-723)

### Lines 724-745

writer_config_defaults map<string,string>=11 persists common process/restart defaults, while each ShardWriterConfig may override at runtime without persisting those overrides. ShardingSpec has spec_id uint32=1 unique within index and never reused, plus repeated ShardingField fields=2. Concrete map keys and defaults are not enumerated here. (protos/table.proto:724-745)

### Lines 746-769

ShardingField declares field_id string=1, repeated int32 source_ids=2, optional transform string=3 (examples identity/year/bucket), optional DataFusion SQL expression string=4, result_type string=5 as Arrow type name, parameters string map=6 (example num_buckets). transform and expression are mutually exclusive by comment but are separate optional fields, so an implementation must reject both being present. Valid transforms, SQL restrictions, and result-type validation are not enforced here. (protos/table.proto:746-769)

## Interaction and interpretation limits

This document analyzes every schema line, not the algorithms alluded to in those comments. Current feature support, stable/unstable designation, commit conflict matrices, writer fencing, recovery listing, and catch-up/cleanup safety require Rust source. In particular, covering declarations may legally exceed payload availability (protos/table.proto:380-386), snapshots are not current shard truth (protos/table.proto:642-650), and absence is not zero progress (protos/table.proto:628-633).

## Role and visibility

Public lance.table.Transaction persisted/wire representation for reconstructing a manifest during commit retries and deciding transaction compatibility.   317 | impl TryFrom<&DataType> for LogicalType {
  318 |     type Error = Error;
  319 | 
  320 |     fn try_from(dt: &DataType) -> Result<Self> {
  321 |         let type_str = match dt {
  322 |             DataType::Null => "null".to_string(),
  323 |             DataType::Boolean => "bool".to_string(),
  324 |             DataType::Int8 => "int8".to_string(),
  325 |             DataType::UInt8 => "uint8".to_string(),
  326 |             DataType::Int16 => "int16".to_string(),
  327 |             DataType::UInt16 => "uint16".to_string(),
  328 |             DataType::Int32 => "int32".to_string(),
  329 |             DataType::UInt32 => "uint32".to_string(),
  330 |             DataType::Int64 => "int64".to_string(),
  331 |             DataType::UInt64 => "uint64".to_string(),
  332 |             DataType::Float16 => "halffloat".to_string(),
  333 |             DataType::Float32 => "float".to_string(),
  334 |             DataType::Float64 => "double".to_string(),
  335 |             DataType::Decimal128(precision, scale) => format!("decimal:128:{precision}:{scale}"),
  336 |             DataType::Decimal256(precision, scale) => format!("decimal:256:{precision}:{scale}"),
  337 |             DataType::Utf8 | DataType::Utf8View => "string".to_string(),
  338 |             DataType::Binary | DataType::BinaryView => "binary".to_string(),
  339 |             DataType::LargeUtf8 => "large_string".to_string(),
  340 |             DataType::LargeBinary => "large_binary".to_string(),
  341 |             DataType::Date32 => "date32:day".to_string(),
  342 |             DataType::Date64 => "date64:ms".to_string(),
  343 |             DataType::Time32(tu) => format!("time32:{}", timeunit_to_str(tu)),
  344 |             DataType::Time64(tu) => format!("time64:{}", timeunit_to_str(tu)),
  345 |             DataType::Timestamp(tu, tz) => format!(
  346 |                 "timestamp:{}:{}",
  347 |                 timeunit_to_str(tu),
  348 |                 tz.as_ref()
  349 |                     .map(|v| v.to_string())
  350 |                     .unwrap_or("-".to_string())
  351 |             ),
  352 |             DataType::Duration(tu) => format!("duration:{}", timeunit_to_str(tu)),
  353 |             DataType::Struct(_) => "struct".to_string(),
  354 |             DataType::Dictionary(key_type, value_type) => {
  355 |                 let value_logical = Self::try_from(value_type.as_ref())?.0;
  356 |                 let index_logical = Self::try_from(key_type.as_ref())?.0;
  357 |                 let logical_type = format!("dict:{value_logical}:{index_logical}:false");
  358 |                 // `dict:{value}:{index}:false` inlines both component strings, but
  359 |                 // the parser splits on ':', requires exactly four segments, and
  360 |                 // resolves only leaf types - so a component carrying ':' of its own
  361 |                 // (decimal, timestamp, ...) or a struct/list value composes a string
  362 |                 // it can never parse back. `Field::data_type` unwraps that parse, so
  363 |                 // without this check `Schema::try_from` panics instead of erroring.
  364 |                 if DataType::try_from(&Self::from(logical_type.as_str())).is_err() {
  365 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  366 |                         "Cannot encode dictionary type {dt:?}: the logical type \"{logical_type}\" does not parse back"
  367 |                     )));
  368 |                 }
  369 |                 logical_type
  370 |             }
  371 |             DataType::List(elem) => match elem.data_type() {
  372 |                 DataType::Struct(_) => "list.struct".to_string(),
  373 |                 _ => "list".to_string(),
  374 |             },
  375 |             DataType::LargeList(elem) => match elem.data_type() {
  376 |                 DataType::Struct(_) => "large_list.struct".to_string(),
  377 |                 _ => "large_list".to_string(),
  378 |             },
  379 |             DataType::FixedSizeList(field, len) => {
  380 |                 if is_bfloat16_field(field) {
  381 |                     // Don't want to directly use `bfloat16`, in case a built-in type is added
  382 |                     // that isn't identical to our extension type.
  383 |                     format!("fixed_size_list:lance.bfloat16:{}", *len)
  384 |                 } else if !is_supported_fixed_size_list_child(field.data_type(), false) {
  385 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported data type: {:?}", dt)));
  386 |                 } else {
  387 |                     format!(
  388 |                         "fixed_size_list:{}:{}",
  389 |                         Self::try_from(field.data_type())?.0,
  390 |                         *len
  391 |                     )
  392 |                 }
  393 |             }
  394 |             DataType::FixedSizeBinary(len) => format!("fixed_size_binary:{}", *len),
  395 |             DataType::Map(_, keys_sorted) => {
  396 |                 // TODO: We only support keys_sorted=false for now,
  397 |                 //  because converting a rust arrow map field to the python arrow field will
  398 |                 //  lose the keys_sorted property.
  399 |                 if *keys_sorted {
  400 |                     return Err(Error::schema(format!(
  401 |                         "Unsupported map data type with keys_sorted=true: {:?}",
  402 |                         dt
  403 |                     )));
  404 |                 }
  405 |                 "map".to_string()
  406 |             }
  407 |             _ => {
  408 |                 return Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported data type: {:?}", dt)));
  409 |             }
  410 |         };
  411 | 
  412 |         Ok(Self(type_str))
  413 |     }
  414 | }

  417 |     type Error = Error;
  418 | 
  419 |     fn try_from(lt: &LogicalType) -> Result<Self> {
  420 |         use DataType::*;
  421 |         if let Some(t) = match lt.0.as_str() {
  422 |             "null" => Some(Null),
  423 |             "bool" => Some(Boolean),
  424 |             "int8" => Some(Int8),
  425 |             "uint8" => Some(UInt8),
  426 |             "int16" => Some(Int16),
  427 |             "uint16" => Some(UInt16),
  428 |             "int32" => Some(Int32),
  429 |             "uint32" => Some(UInt32),
  430 |             "int64" => Some(Int64),
  431 |             "uint64" => Some(UInt64),
  432 |             "halffloat" => Some(Float16),
  433 |             "float" => Some(Float32),
  434 |             "double" => Some(Float64),
  435 |             "string" => Some(Utf8),
  436 |             "binary" => Some(Binary),
  437 |             "large_string" => Some(LargeUtf8),
  438 |             "large_binary" => Some(LargeBinary),
  439 |             BLOB_LOGICAL_TYPE => Some(LargeBinary),
  440 |             "json" => Some(LargeBinary),
  441 |             "date32:day" => Some(Date32),
  442 |             "date64:ms" => Some(Date64),
  443 |             "time32:s" => Some(Time32(TimeUnit::Second)),
  444 |             "time32:ms" => Some(Time32(TimeUnit::Millisecond)),
  445 |             "time64:us" => Some(Time64(TimeUnit::Microsecond)),
  446 |             "time64:ns" => Some(Time64(TimeUnit::Nanosecond)),
  447 |             "duration:s" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Second)),
  448 |             "duration:ms" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Millisecond)),
  449 |             "duration:us" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Microsecond)),
  450 |             "duration:ns" => Some(Duration(TimeUnit::Nanosecond)),
  451 |             _ => None,
  452 |         } {
  453 |             Ok(t)
  454 |         } else {
  455 |             let splits = lt.0.split(':').collect::<Vec<_>>();
  456 |             match splits[0] {
  457 |                 "fixed_size_list" => {
  458 |                     if splits.len() < 3 {
  459 |                         return Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported logical type: {}", lt)));
  460 |                     }
  461 | 
  462 |                     let size: i32 = splits
  463 |                         .last()
  464 |                         .unwrap()
  465 |                         .parse::<i32>()
  466 |                         .map_err(|e: _| Error::schema(e.to_string()))?;
  467 | 
  468 |                     let inner_type = splits[1..splits.len() - 1].join(":");
  469 | 
  470 |                     match inner_type.as_str() {
  471 |                         BFLOAT16_EXT_NAME => {
  472 |                             let field = ArrowField::new("item", Self::FixedSizeBinary(2), true)
  473 |                                 .with_metadata(
  474 |                                     [
  475 |                                         (ARROW_EXT_NAME_KEY.into(), BFLOAT16_EXT_NAME.into()),
  476 |                                         (ARROW_EXT_META_KEY.into(), "".into()),
  477 |                                     ]
  478 |                                     .into(),
  479 |                                 );
  480 |                             Ok(FixedSizeList(Arc::new(field), size))
  481 |                         }
  482 |                         data_type => {
  483 |                             let elem_type = (&LogicalType(data_type.to_string())).try_into()?;
  484 | 
  485 |                             Ok(FixedSizeList(
  486 |                                 Arc::new(ArrowField::new("item", elem_type, true)),
  487 |                                 size,
  488 |                             ))
  489 |                         }
  490 |                     }
  491 |                 }
  492 |                 "fixed_size_binary" => {
  493 |                     if splits.len() != 2 {
  494 |                         Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported logical type: {}", lt)))
  495 |                     } else {
  496 |                         let size: i32 = splits[1]
  497 |                             .parse::<i32>()
  498 |                             .map_err(|e: _| Error::schema(e.to_string()))?;
  499 |                         Ok(FixedSizeBinary(size))
  500 |                     }
  501 |                 }
  502 |                 "dict" => {
  503 |                     if splits.len() != 4 {
  504 |                         Err(Error::schema(format!(
  505 |                             "Unsupported dictionary type: {}",
  506 |                             lt
  507 |                         )))
  508 |                     } else {
  509 |                         let value_type: Self = (&LogicalType::from(splits[1])).try_into()?;
  510 |                         let index_type: Self = (&LogicalType::from(splits[2])).try_into()?;
  511 |                         Ok(Dictionary(Box::new(index_type), Box::new(value_type)))
  512 |                     }
  513 |                 }
  514 |                 "decimal" => {
  515 |                     if splits.len() != 4 {
  516 |                         Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported decimal type: {}", lt)))
  517 |                     } else {
  518 |                         let bits: i16 = splits[1]
  519 |                             .parse::<i16>()
  520 |                             .map_err(|err| Error::schema(err.to_string()))?;
  521 |                         let precision: u8 = splits[2]
  522 |                             .parse::<u8>()
  523 |                             .map_err(|err| Error::schema(err.to_string()))?;
  524 |                         let scale: i8 = splits[3]
  525 |                             .parse::<i8>()
  526 |                             .map_err(|err| Error::schema(err.to_string()))?;
  527 | 
  528 |                         if bits == 128 {
  529 |                             Ok(Decimal128(precision, scale))
  530 |                         } else if bits == 256 {
  531 |                             Ok(Decimal256(precision, scale))
  532 |                         } else {
  533 |                             Err(Error::schema(format!(
  534 |                                 "Only Decimal128 and Decimal256 is supported. Found {bits}"
  535 |                             )))
  536 |                         }
  537 |                     }
  538 |                 }
  539 |                 "timestamp" => {
  540 |                     if splits.len() < 3 {
  541 |                         Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported timestamp type: {}", lt)))
  542 |                     } else {
  543 |                         let timeunit = parse_timeunit(splits[1])?;
  544 |                         // A fixed-offset timezone such as "+08:00" contains a colon, so the
  545 |                         // trailing segments must be rejoined instead of read as a single one.
  546 |                         let tz_str = splits[2..].join(":");
  547 |                         let tz: Option<Arc<str>> = if tz_str == "-" {
  548 |                             None
  549 |                         } else {
  550 |                             Some(tz_str.into())
  551 |                         };
  552 |                         Ok(Timestamp(timeunit, tz))
  553 |                     }
  554 |                 }
  555 |                 _ => Err(Error::schema(format!("Unsupported logical type: {}", lt))),
  556 |             }
  557 |         }
  558 |     }
  559 | }

  579 | impl PartialEq for Dictionary {
  580 |     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  581 |         // Compare the values when both sides have them: the write path leaves
  582 |         // offset/length at 0 until the dictionary is persisted, so one append
  583 |         // can legitimately hold the same dictionary at two positions.
  584 |         // `From<&pb::Dictionary>` yields no values at all, and comparing only
  585 |         // the values made that case non-reflexive, so there offset and length
  586 |         // stand in for the content.
  587 |         match (&self.values, &other.values) {
  588 |             (Some(a), Some(b)) => a == b,
  589 |             (None, None) => self.offset == other.offset && self.length == other.length,
  590 |             _ => false,
  591 |         }
  592 |     }
  593 | }

  598 | pub enum BlobKind {
  599 |     /// Stored in the main data file’s out-of-line buffer; `position`/`size` point into that file.
  600 |     Inline = 0,
  601 |     /// Stored in a shared packed blob file; `position`/`size` locate the slice, `blob_id` selects the file.
  602 |     Packed = 1,
  603 |     /// Stored in a dedicated raw blob file; `blob_id` identifies the file, `size` is the full file length.
  604 |     Dedicated = 2,
  605 |     /// Not stored by Lance data files.
  606 |     ///
  607 |     /// For external blobs:
  608 |     /// - `blob_id == 0` means `blob_uri` is an absolute external URI.
  609 |     /// - `blob_id > 0` means `blob_uri` is a path relative to `manifest.base_paths[blob_id]`.
  610 |     ///
  611 |     /// External blobs can have a position and a size. If the position is not set,
  612 |     /// it defaults to 0, which points to the beginning of the blob.
  613 |     External = 3,
  614 | }

  624 |             3 => Ok(Self::External),
  625 |             other => Err(Error::invalid_input_source(

  270 | fn normalize_blob_footer_schema(schema: &Schema) -> Schema {
  271 |     let expected = &BLOB_V2_DESC_LANCE_FIELD.children;
  272 |     let missing_descriptor_count = schema
  273 |         .fields_pre_order()
  274 |         .filter(|field| field.is_blob() && field.children.is_empty())
  275 |         .count();
  276 |     if missing_descriptor_count == 0 {
  277 |         return schema.clone();
  278 |     }
  279 |     let mut normalized = schema.clone();
  280 |     let mut descriptor_children = VecDeque::new();
  281 |     let mut field_index = 0;
  282 |     while descriptor_children.len() < missing_descriptor_count
  283 |         && field_index + expected.len() <= normalized.fields.len()
  284 |     {
  285 |         if normalized.fields[field_index..field_index + expected.len()]
  286 |             .iter()
  287 |             .zip(expected)
  288 |             .all(|(field, expected)| descriptor_child_matches(field, expected))
  289 |         {
  290 |             descriptor_children.push_back(
  291 |                 normalized
  292 |                     .fields
  293 |                     .drain(field_index..field_index + expected.len())
  294 |                     .collect(),
  295 |             );
  296 |         } else {
  297 |             field_index += 1;
  298 |         }
  299 |     }
  300 |     attach_blob_descriptor_children(&mut normalized.fields, &mut descriptor_children);
  301 |     normalized
  302 | }

  492 |                 path,
  493 |             )?;

  556 | /// A compatibility reason that requires a caller-controlled decode/re-encode fallback.
  557 | #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  558 | pub enum FileConcatReason {
  559 |     /// Lance v1 does not support encoded-file concatenation.
  560 |     LegacyVersion,
  561 |     /// An input uses a different exact grammar than the target.
  562 |     VersionMismatch {
  563 |         /// Zero-based input position.
  564 |         input_index: usize,
  565 |         /// Version found in the file footer.
  566 |         actual: ConcreteFileVersion,
  567 |         /// Version requested by the target.
  568 |         expected: ConcreteFileVersion,
  569 |     },
  570 |     /// An input's persisted schema differs from the target schema.
  571 |     SchemaMismatch {
  572 |         /// Zero-based input position.
  573 |         input_index: usize,
  574 |     },
  575 |     /// Inputs do not describe the same physical columns.
  576 |     ColumnLayoutMismatch {
  577 |         /// Zero-based input position.
  578 |         input_index: usize,
  579 |         /// Zero-based physical column when one could be identified.
  580 |         column_index: Option<usize>,
  581 |     },
  582 |     /// A column-level encoding cannot safely combine its buffers.
  583 |     ColumnEncodingMismatch {
  584 |         /// Zero-based input position.
  585 |         input_index: usize,
  586 |         /// Zero-based physical column.
  587 |         column_index: usize,
  588 |     },
  589 |     /// A column uses file-level buffers whose page references cannot be relocated.
  590 |     ColumnBuffers {
  591 |         /// Zero-based input position.
  592 |         input_index: usize,
  593 |         /// Zero-based physical column.
  594 |         column_index: usize,
  595 |         /// Number of column buffers referenced by the column metadata.
  596 |         count: usize,
  597 |     },
  598 |     /// A file contains global buffers whose relocation semantics are not defined.
  599 |     ExtraGlobalBuffers {
  600 |         /// Zero-based input position.
  601 |         input_index: usize,
  602 |         /// Number of global buffers, including the schema descriptor.
  603 |         count: usize,
  604 |     },
  605 |     /// The schema contains offsets into external blob storage.
  606 |     BlobColumns,
  607 | }

  609 | impl fmt::Display for FileConcatReason {

  611 |         match self {
  612 |             Self::LegacyVersion => f.write_str("Lance v1 files cannot be concatenated"),
  613 |             Self::VersionMismatch {
  614 |                 input_index,
  615 |                 actual,
  616 |                 expected,
  617 |             } => write!(
  618 |                 f,
  619 |                 "input {input_index} has file version {actual}, expected {expected}"
  620 |             ),
  621 |             Self::SchemaMismatch { input_index } => {
  622 |                 write!(f, "input {input_index} has a different file schema")
  623 |             }
  624 |             Self::ColumnLayoutMismatch {
  625 |                 input_index,
  626 |                 column_index,
  627 |             } => match column_index {
  628 |                 Some(column_index) => write!(
  629 |                     f,
  630 |                     "input {input_index} has a different layout for physical column {column_index}"
  631 |                 ),
  632 |                 None => write!(
  633 |                     f,
  634 |                     "input {input_index} has a different physical column count"
  635 |                 ),
  636 |             },
  637 |             Self::ColumnEncodingMismatch {
  638 |                 input_index,
  639 |                 column_index,
  640 |             } => write!(
  641 |                 f,
  642 |                 "input {input_index} has an incompatible encoding for physical column {column_index}"
  643 |             ),
  644 |             Self::ColumnBuffers {
  645 |                 input_index,
  646 |                 column_index,
  647 |                 count,
  648 |             } => write!(
  649 |                 f,
  650 |                 "input {input_index} physical column {column_index} has {count} column buffers whose references cannot be relocated"
  651 |             ),
  652 |             Self::ExtraGlobalBuffers { input_index, count } => write!(
  653 |                 f,
  654 |                 "input {input_index} has {count} global buffers; only the schema descriptor is supported"
  655 |             ),

  657 |                 f.write_str("schemas containing blob columns cannot be concatenated")
  658 |             }
  659 |         }
  660 |     }

  684 | fn check_compatibility(
  685 |     target: &FileConcatTarget,
  686 |     inputs: &[PreparedInput<'_>],
  687 |     allow_blob_columns: bool,
  688 | ) -> Result<Option<FileConcatReason>> {
  689 |     if !allow_blob_columns
  690 |         && target
  691 |             .schema
  692 |             .fields_pre_order()
  693 |             .any(|field| field.is_blob())
  694 |     {
  695 |         return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::BlobColumns));
  696 |     }
  697 | 
  698 |     let Some(first) = inputs.first() else {
  699 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(
  700 |             "concat_files requires at least one complete input file",
  701 |         ));
  702 |     };
  703 |     let baseline_columns = &first.metadata.column_infos;
  704 |     let expected_schema = if allow_blob_columns {
  705 |         descriptor_projection_schema(target.schema.as_ref())
  706 |     } else {
  707 |         target.schema.as_ref().clone()
  708 |     };
  709 |     let baseline_encodings = baseline_columns
  710 |         .iter()
  711 |         .map(|column| encoded_column_encoding(column))
  712 |         .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  713 | 
  714 |     for (input_index, prepared) in inputs.iter().enumerate() {
  715 |         let metadata = &prepared.metadata;
  716 |         if let Some(expected_num_rows) = prepared.input.expected_num_rows
  717 |             && metadata.num_rows != expected_num_rows
  718 |         {
  719 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  720 |                 "input {input_index} at '{}' has {} physical rows but {} were expected",
  721 |                 prepared.input.path(),
  722 |                 metadata.num_rows,
  723 |                 expected_num_rows
  724 |             )));
  725 |         }
  726 |         if metadata.version != target.version {
  727 |             return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::VersionMismatch {
  728 |                 input_index,
  729 |                 actual: metadata.version,
  730 |                 expected: target.version,
  731 |             }));
  732 |         }
  733 |         if prepared.schema != &expected_schema {
  734 |             return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::SchemaMismatch { input_index }));
  735 |         }
  736 |         let normalized_rows =
  737 |             versions::validate_external_metadata(metadata.version, prepared.schema, metadata)
  738 |                 .map_err(|error| {
  739 |                     Error::corrupt_file(
  740 |                         prepared.input.path().clone(),
  741 |                         format!("input {input_index} has incomplete file metadata: {error}"),
  742 |                     )
  743 |                 })?;
  744 |         if normalized_rows != metadata.num_rows {
  745 |             return Err(Error::corrupt_file(
  746 |                 prepared.input.path().clone(),
  747 |                 format!(
  748 |                     "input {input_index} descriptor reports {} physical rows but its columns normalize to {normalized_rows}",
  749 |                     metadata.num_rows
  750 |                 ),
  751 |             ));
  752 |         }
  753 |         if metadata.file_buffers.len() > 1 {
  754 |             return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::ExtraGlobalBuffers {
  755 |                 input_index,
  756 |                 count: metadata.file_buffers.len(),
  757 |             }));
  758 |         }
  759 |         if metadata.column_infos.len() != baseline_columns.len() {
  760 |             return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::ColumnLayoutMismatch {
  761 |                 input_index,
  762 |                 column_index: None,
  763 |             }));
  764 |         }
  765 |         for (column_index, (column, baseline)) in metadata
  766 |             .column_infos
  767 |             .iter()
  768 |             .zip(baseline_columns)
  769 |             .enumerate()
  770 |         {
  771 |             if !column.buffer_offsets_and_sizes.is_empty() {
  772 |                 return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::ColumnBuffers {
  773 |                     input_index,
  774 |                     column_index,
  775 |                     count: column.buffer_offsets_and_sizes.len(),
  776 |                 }));
  777 |             }
  778 |             if column.index != baseline.index {
  779 |                 return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::ColumnLayoutMismatch {
  780 |                     input_index,
  781 |                     column_index: Some(column_index),
  782 |                 }));
  783 |             }
  784 |             if encoded_column_encoding(column)? != baseline_encodings[column_index] {
  785 |                 return Ok(Some(FileConcatReason::ColumnEncodingMismatch {
  786 |                     input_index,
  787 |                     column_index,
  788 |                 }));
  789 |             }
  790 |         }
  791 |     }
  792 |     Ok(None)
  793 | }
