  795 | async fn copy_page_buffers(
  796 |     writer: &mut crate::writer::FileWriter,
  797 |     scheduler: &FileScheduler,
  798 |     pages: &[PageInfo],
  799 |     read_batch_bytes: u64,
  800 |     input_index: usize,
  801 |     column_index: usize,
  802 |     row_offset: u64,
  803 | ) -> Result<Vec<PageInfo>> {
  804 |     let mut copied = Vec::with_capacity(pages.len());
  805 |     let mut page_index = 0;
  806 |     while page_index < pages.len() {
  807 |         let batch_start = page_index;
  808 |         let mut batch_bytes = 0u64;
  809 |         let mut batch_ranges = Vec::new();
  810 |         let mut batch_buffer_counts = Vec::new();
  811 |         while page_index < pages.len() {
  812 |             let page = &pages[page_index];
  813 |             let page_bytes = page.buffer_offsets_and_sizes.iter().try_fold(
  814 |                 0u64,
  815 |                 |total, (offset, size)| {
  816 |                     offset.checked_add(*size).ok_or_else(|| {
  817 |                         Error::corrupt_file(
  818 |                             scheduler.reader().path().clone(),
  819 |                             format!(
  820 |                                 "input {input_index} column {column_index} page {page_index} buffer range overflows"
  821 |                             ),
  822 |                         )
  823 |                     })?;
  824 |                     total.checked_add(*size).ok_or_else(|| {
  825 |                         Error::corrupt_file(
  826 |                             scheduler.reader().path().clone(),
  827 |                             format!(
  828 |                                 "input {input_index} column {column_index} page {page_index} buffer sizes overflow"
  829 |                             ),
  830 |                         )
  831 |                     })
  832 |                 },
  833 |             )?;
  834 |             if page_index > batch_start
  835 |                 && batch_bytes
  836 |                     .checked_add(page_bytes)
  837 |                     .is_none_or(|total| total > read_batch_bytes)
  838 |             {
  839 |                 break;
  840 |             }
  841 |             batch_bytes = batch_bytes.checked_add(page_bytes).ok_or_else(|| {
  842 |                 Error::corrupt_file(
  843 |                     scheduler.reader().path().clone(),
  844 |                     format!("input {input_index} column {column_index} read batch size overflows"),
  845 |                 )
  846 |             })?;
  847 |             batch_buffer_counts.push(page.buffer_offsets_and_sizes.len());
  848 |             batch_ranges.extend(
  849 |                 page.buffer_offsets_and_sizes
  850 |                     .iter()
  851 |                     .filter(|(_, size)| *size > 0)
  852 |                     .map(|(offset, size)| *offset..(*offset + *size)),
  853 |             );
  854 |             page_index += 1;
  855 |         }
  856 | 
  857 |         let batch_data = if batch_ranges.is_empty() {
  858 |             Vec::new()
  859 |         } else {
  860 |             scheduler.submit_request(batch_ranges, 0).await?
  861 |         };
  862 |         let mut batch_data = batch_data.into_iter();
  863 |         for (relative_page_index, (page, buffer_count)) in pages[batch_start..page_index]
  864 |             .iter()
  865 |             .zip(batch_buffer_counts)
  866 |             .enumerate()
  867 |         {
  868 |             let source_page_index = batch_start + relative_page_index;
  869 |             let mut relocated_buffers = Vec::with_capacity(buffer_count);
  870 |             for (buffer_index, (_, size)) in page.buffer_offsets_and_sizes.iter().enumerate() {
  871 |                 let data = if *size == 0 {
  872 |                     None
  873 |                 } else {
  874 |                     let data = batch_data.next().ok_or_else(|| {
  875 |                         Error::io(format!(
  876 |                             "short read for input {input_index} column {column_index} page {source_page_index} buffer {buffer_index}: expected {size} bytes"
  877 |                         ))
  878 |                     })?;
  879 |                     if data.len() as u64 != *size {
  880 |                         return Err(Error::io(format!(
  881 |                             "short read for input {input_index} column {column_index} page {source_page_index} buffer {buffer_index}: expected {size} bytes, got {}",
  882 |                             data.len()
  883 |                         )));
  884 |                     }
  885 |                     Some(data)
  886 |                 };
  887 |                 relocated_buffers.push(
  888 |                     writer
  889 |                         .write_external_buffer(data.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
  890 |                         .await?,
  891 |                 );
  892 |             }
  893 |             copied.push(PageInfo {
  894 |                 num_rows: page.num_rows,
  895 |                 priority: page.priority.checked_add(row_offset).ok_or_else(|| {
  896 |                     Error::invalid_input_source(
  897 |                         format!(
  898 |                             "input {input_index} column {column_index} page {source_page_index} priority overflows after row relocation"
  899 |                         )
  900 |                         .into(),
  901 |                     )
  902 |                 })?,
  903 |                 encoding: page.encoding.clone(),
  904 |                 buffer_offsets_and_sizes: Arc::from(relocated_buffers),
  905 |             });
  906 |         }
  907 |         if batch_data.next().is_some() {
  908 |             return Err(Error::io(format!(
  909 |                 "read for input {input_index} column {column_index} returned more buffers than requested"
  910 |             )));
  911 |         }
  912 |     }
  913 |     Ok(copied)
  914 | }

  916 | async fn concat_prepared<Factory, FactoryFuture>(
  917 |     target: &FileConcatTarget,
  918 |     prepared: &[PreparedInput<'_>],
  919 |     allow_blob_columns: bool,
  920 |     reuse_single_input: bool,
  921 |     output_factory: Factory,
  922 |     options: FileConcatOptions,
  923 | ) -> Result<FileConcatResult>
  924 | where
  925 |     Factory: FnOnce() -> FactoryFuture,
  926 |     FactoryFuture: Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn ObjectWriter>>>,
  927 | {
  928 |     if options.read_batch_bytes == 0 {
  929 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(
  930 |             "FileConcatOptions.read_batch_bytes must be greater than zero",
  931 |         ));
  932 |     }
  933 |     if let Some(reason) = check_compatibility(target, prepared, allow_blob_columns)? {
  934 |         return Ok(FileConcatResult::Unsupported(reason));
  935 |     }
  936 | 
  937 |     let total_rows = prepared.iter().try_fold(0u64, |total, input| {
  938 |         total.checked_add(input.metadata.num_rows).ok_or_else(|| {
  939 |             Error::invalid_input_source("concat_files total physical row count overflows".into())
  940 |         })
  941 |     })?;
  942 |     if prepared.len() == 1 && reuse_single_input {
  943 |         return Ok(FileConcatResult::Reused(
  944 |             0,
  945 |             FileConcatOutput {
  946 |                 version: target.version,
  947 |                 num_rows: total_rows,
  948 |                 size_bytes: prepared[0].metadata.file_size_bytes,
  949 |             },
  950 |         ));
  951 |     }
  952 | 
  953 |     let object_writer = output_factory().await?;
  954 |     let mut writer =
  955 |         versions::create_lazy_writer(target.version, object_writer, options.writer_options)?;
  956 |     let write_result: Result<FileWriteSummary> = async {
  957 |         let column_count = prepared[0].metadata.column_infos.len();
  958 |         let mut output_pages = std::iter::repeat_with(Vec::new)
  959 |             .take(column_count)
  960 |             .collect::<Vec<Vec<PageInfo>>>();
  961 |         let mut row_offset = 0u64;
  962 | 
  963 |         for (input_index, prepared_input) in prepared.iter().enumerate() {
  964 |             for (column_index, column) in prepared_input.metadata.column_infos.iter().enumerate() {
  965 |                 let has_existing_pages = !output_pages[column_index].is_empty();
  966 |                 versions::copy_external_metadata_column(
  967 |                     target.version,
  968 |                     target.schema.as_ref(),
  969 |                     column_index,
  970 |                     has_existing_pages,
  971 |                     || async {
  972 |                         let pages = copy_page_buffers(
  973 |                             &mut writer,
  974 |                             &prepared_input.input.scheduler,
  975 |                             &column.page_infos,
  976 |                             options.read_batch_bytes as u64,
  977 |                             input_index,
  978 |                             column_index,
  979 |                             row_offset,
  980 |                         )
  981 |                         .await?;
  982 |                         output_pages[column_index].extend(pages);
  983 | 
  984 |                         Ok(())
  985 |                     },
  986 |                 )
  987 |                 .await?;
  988 |             }
  989 |             row_offset = row_offset
  990 |                 .checked_add(prepared_input.metadata.num_rows)
  991 |                 .ok_or_else(|| {
  992 |                     Error::invalid_input_source("concat_files physical row offset overflows".into())
  993 |                 })?;
  994 |         }
  995 | 
  996 |         let mut columns = Vec::with_capacity(column_count);
  997 |         for (column_index, pages) in output_pages.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  998 |             versions::finalize_external_metadata_column(
  999 |                 target.version,
 1000 |                 target.schema.as_ref(),
 1001 |                 column_index,
 1002 |                 pages,
 1003 |                 total_rows,
 1004 |             )?;
 1005 |             let baseline = &prepared[0].metadata.column_infos[column_index];
 1006 |             columns.push(Arc::new(ColumnInfo::new(
 1007 |                 baseline.index,
 1008 |                 Arc::from(std::mem::take(pages)),
 1009 |                 Vec::new(),
 1010 |                 baseline.encoding.clone(),
 1011 |             )));
 1012 |         }
 1013 |         // The schema descriptor is the first global buffer and must start at
 1014 |         // the page-buffer alignment required by the reader.
 1015 |         writer.write_external_buffer(&[]).await?;
 1016 |         writer.initialize_with_external_columns(
 1017 |             target.schema.as_ref().clone(),
 1018 |             &columns,
 1019 |             total_rows,
 1020 |         )?;
 1021 |         writer.finish().await
 1022 |     }
 1023 |     .await;
 1024 | 
 1025 |     match write_result {
 1026 |         Ok(summary) => Ok(FileConcatResult::Written(FileConcatOutput {
 1027 |             version: target.version,
 1028 |             num_rows: summary.num_rows,
 1029 |             size_bytes: summary.size_bytes,
 1030 |         })),
 1031 |         Err(error) => {
 1032 |             writer.abort().await;
 1033 |             Err(error)
 1034 |         }
 1035 |     }
 1036 | }

 1038 | /// Concatenate complete compatible encoded files in the supplied order.
 1039 | ///
 1040 | /// Metadata is read exactly once per input. The factory is invoked only after
 1041 | /// all compatibility checks succeed and is never invoked for [`FileConcatResult::Reused`]
 1042 | /// or [`FileConcatResult::Unsupported`]. Page payloads are copied without Arrow
 1043 | /// decoding; offsets, priorities, exact-version structural metadata, and the
 1044 | /// footer are regenerated.
 1045 | ///
 1046 | /// ```
 1047 | /// # use std::sync::Arc;
 1048 | /// # use lance_core::Result;
 1049 | /// # use lance_file::concat::{concat_files, EncodedFileInput, FileConcatOptions, FileConcatResult, FileConcatTarget};
 1050 | /// # use lance_io::object_store::ObjectStore;
 1051 | /// # use object_store::path::Path;
 1052 | /// # async fn stitch(
 1053 | /// #     target: &FileConcatTarget,
 1054 | /// #     inputs: &[EncodedFileInput],
 1055 | /// #     output_store: Arc<ObjectStore>,
 1056 | /// #     output_path: Path,
 1057 | /// # ) -> Result<FileConcatResult> {
 1058 | /// let store = output_store.clone();
 1059 | /// concat_files(
 1060 | ///     target,
 1061 | ///     inputs,
 1062 | ///     move || async move { store.create(&output_path).await },
 1063 | ///     FileConcatOptions::default(),
 1064 | /// )
 1065 | /// .await
 1066 | /// # }
 1067 | /// ```
 1068 | pub async fn concat_files<Factory, FactoryFuture>(
 1069 |     target: &FileConcatTarget,
 1070 |     ordered_inputs: &[EncodedFileInput],
 1071 |     output_factory: Factory,
 1072 |     options: FileConcatOptions,
 1073 | ) -> Result<FileConcatResult>
 1074 | where
 1075 |     Factory: FnOnce() -> FactoryFuture,
 1076 |     FactoryFuture: Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn ObjectWriter>>>,
 1077 | {
 1078 |     if ordered_inputs.is_empty() {
 1079 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(
 1080 |             "concat_files requires at least one complete input file",
 1081 |         ));
 1082 |     }
 1083 |     let raw_metadata = futures::future::try_join_all(

 1121 | /// Concatenate validated data-file parts in caller-supplied row order.
 1122 | ///
 1123 | /// Unlike [`concat_files`], this entry point accepts Blob v2 columns because
 1124 | /// every [`DataFilePart`] has already rejected file-relative Inline payloads
 1125 | /// and validated managed descriptors against an explicit ID lease. Leases from
 1126 | /// different parts must not overlap. No logical values or Blob payloads are
 1127 | /// decoded and re-encoded during concatenation.
 1128 | pub async fn concat_data_file_parts<Factory, FactoryFuture>(
 1129 |     target: &FileConcatTarget,
 1130 |     ordered_parts: &[DataFilePart],
 1131 |     output_factory: Factory,
 1132 |     options: FileConcatOptions,
 1133 | ) -> Result<FileConcatResult>
 1134 | where
 1135 |     Factory: FnOnce() -> FactoryFuture,
 1136 |     FactoryFuture: Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn ObjectWriter>>>,
 1137 | {
 1138 |     if ordered_parts.is_empty() {
 1139 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(
 1140 |             "concat_data_file_parts requires at least one data-file part",
 1141 |         ));
 1142 |     }
 1143 |     for (part_index, part) in ordered_parts.iter().enumerate() {
 1144 |         if part.blob_target_id != target.blob_target_id {
 1145 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
 1146 |                 "part {part_index} Blob target ID {:?} does not match target ID {:?}",
 1147 |                 part.blob_target_id.as_ref().map(BlobTargetId::as_str),
 1148 |                 target.blob_target_id.as_ref().map(BlobTargetId::as_str)
 1149 |             )));
 1150 |         }
 1151 |     }
 1152 |     let mut ranges = ordered_parts
 1153 |         .iter()
 1154 |         .enumerate()
 1155 |         .filter_map(|(part_index, part)| {
 1156 |             part.blob_ids
 1157 |                 .clone()
 1158 |                 .map(|range| (range.start, range.end, part_index))
 1159 |         })
 1160 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1161 |     ranges.sort_unstable_by_key(|(start, _, _)| *start);
 1162 |     for pair in ranges.windows(2) {
 1163 |         let (left_start, left_end, left_index) = pair[0];
 1164 |         let (right_start, right_end, right_index) = pair[1];
 1165 |         if right_start < left_end {
 1166 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
 1167 |                 "part Blob ID ranges overlap: part {left_index} uses {left_start}..{left_end}, part {right_index} uses {right_start}..{right_end}"
 1168 |             )));
 1169 |         }
 1170 |     }
 1171 | 
 1172 |     let prepared = ordered_parts
 1173 |         .iter()
 1174 |         .map(|part| PreparedInput {
 1175 |             input: &part.input,
 1176 |             metadata: part.metadata.as_ref(),
 1177 |             schema: part.schema.as_ref(),
 1178 |         })
 1179 |         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 1180 |     concat_prepared(target, &prepared, true, false, output_factory, options).await
 1181 | }

  257 | fn mark_supported(flags: &mut u64, flag: u64, feature_enabled: bool) {
  258 |     if !feature_enabled {
  259 |         *flags &= !flag;
  260 |     }
  261 | }
  262 | 
  263 | /// The feature-flag bits this build understands, given which unstable features
  264 | /// are enabled. Split out from [`supported_flags`] so the policy is testable
  265 | /// without toggling the build profile or environment.
  266 | fn supported_flags_when(
  267 |     overlay_enabled: bool,
  268 |     spilled_row_lineage_enabled: bool,
  269 |     frag_reuse_with_stable_row_ids_enabled: bool,
  270 | ) -> u64 {
  271 |     let mut supported = FLAG_UNKNOWN - 1;
  272 |     mark_supported(
  273 |         &mut supported,
  274 |         FLAG_UNSTABLE_DATA_OVERLAY_FILES,
  275 |         overlay_enabled,
  276 |     );
  277 |     mark_supported(
  278 |         &mut supported,
  279 |         FLAG_FRAG_REUSE_WITH_STABLE_ROW_IDS,
  280 |         frag_reuse_with_stable_row_ids_enabled,
  281 |     );
  282 |     mark_supported(
  283 |         &mut supported,
  284 |         FLAG_UNSTABLE_SPILLED_ROW_LINEAGE,
  285 |         spilled_row_lineage_enabled,
  286 |     );
  287 |     // Reserved, not implemented: see the flag's doc comment.
  288 |     mark_supported(&mut supported, FLAG_FRAGMENT_TREE, false);
  289 |     mark_supported(&mut supported, FLAG_INDEPENDENT_COVERING_FIELDS, false);
  290 |     supported
  291 | }
  292 | 
  293 | fn supported_flags() -> u64 {
  294 |     supported_flags_when(
  295 |         data_overlay_files_enabled(),
  296 |         spilled_row_lineage_enabled(),
  297 |         frag_reuse_with_stable_row_ids_enabled(),
  298 |     )
  299 | }

  301 | pub fn can_read_dataset(reader_flags: u64) -> bool {
  302 |     reader_flags & !supported_flags() == 0
  303 | }
  304 | 
  305 | pub fn can_write_dataset(writer_flags: u64) -> bool {
  306 |     writer_flags & !supported_flags() == 0
  307 | }
  308 | 
  309 | /// Refuse reads from manifests whose required reader features this build does
  310 | /// not support or whose paired capabilities are inconsistent.
  311 | pub fn ensure_can_read_manifest(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<()> {
  312 |     validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest)?;
  313 |     if !can_read_dataset(manifest.reader_feature_flags) {
  314 |         return Err(Error::not_supported_source(
  315 |             format!(
  316 |                 "This dataset cannot be read by this version of Lance. Please upgrade \
  317 |                  Lance to read this dataset. Flags: {}",
  318 |                 manifest.reader_feature_flags
  319 |             )
  320 |             .into(),
  321 |         ));
  322 |     }
  323 |     Ok(())
  324 | }
  325 | 
  326 | /// Refuse writes to manifests whose required writer features this build does
  327 | /// not support or whose paired capabilities are inconsistent.
  328 | pub fn ensure_can_write_manifest(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<()> {
  329 |     validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest)?;
  330 |     if !can_write_dataset(manifest.writer_feature_flags) {
  331 |         return Err(Error::not_supported_source(
  332 |             format!(
  333 |                 "This dataset cannot be written by this version of Lance. Please upgrade \
  334 |                  Lance to write this dataset. Flags: {}",
  335 |                 manifest.writer_feature_flags
  336 |             )
  337 |             .into(),
  338 |         ));
  339 |     }
  340 |     Ok(())
  341 | }
  342 | 
  343 | pub fn has_deprecated_v2_feature_flag(writer_flags: u64) -> bool {
  344 |     writer_flags & FLAG_USE_V2_FORMAT_DEPRECATED != 0
  345 | }
  346 | 
  347 | /// Refuse a manifest whose paired reader and writer capability bits disagree.
  348 | ///
  349 | /// One word set and the other not is neither mode: it would let a legacy reader
  350 | /// or a legacy writer through on a table where the other half is enforcing. The
  351 | /// commit path refuses to *produce* this, so seeing it on read means the
  352 | /// manifest was written by something that did not.
  353 | pub fn validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<()> {
  354 |     if (manifest.reader_feature_flags ^ manifest.writer_feature_flags) & FLAG_FRAGMENT_REUSE_INDEX
  355 |         != 0
  356 |     {
  357 |         return Err(Error::corrupt_file_named(
  358 |             "manifest",
  359 |             "FRI requires both reader and writer feature flags",
  360 |         ));
  361 |     }
  362 | 
  363 |     let reader = manifest.reader_feature_flags & FLAG_MIXED_DATA_FILE_VERSIONS != 0;
  364 |     let writer = manifest.writer_feature_flags & FLAG_MIXED_DATA_FILE_VERSIONS != 0;
  365 |     if reader != writer {
  366 |         return Err(Error::corrupt_file_named(
  367 |             "manifest",
  368 |             "Manifest has only one of the mixed data-file-version reader and writer feature bits set, \
  369 |              so its semantics are undefined",
  370 |         ));
  371 |     }
  372 |     Ok(())
  373 | }
  374 | 
  375 | fn validated_sticky_paired_flags(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<u64> {
  376 |     validate_paired_feature_flags(manifest)?;
  377 |     Ok(manifest.reader_feature_flags & STICKY_PAIRED_FLAGS)
  378 | }

  171 |     pub fn schema(&self, full_schema: &Schema) -> Schema {
  172 |         // Structural field IDs describe physical headers in V2.0 and may also
  173 |         // appear with column_index=-1 in older V2.1+ manifests. They do not, by
  174 |         // themselves, mean that every child in the current dataset schema is
  175 |         // present in this file. In particular, a struct can retain its ID while
  176 |         // schema evolution replaces its last old child with a new one.
  177 |         fn project_field(
  178 |             field: &lance_core::datatypes::Field,
  179 |             mapped_columns: &HashMap<i32, i32>,
  180 |             is_v2_0: bool,
  181 |         ) -> Option<lance_core::datatypes::Field> {
  182 |             if field.is_blob() || field.is_packed_struct() {
  183 |                 return mapped_columns
  184 |                     .contains_key(&field.id)
  185 |                     .then(|| field.clone());
  186 |             }
  187 | 
  188 |             let children = field
  189 |                 .children
  190 |                 .iter()
  191 |                 .filter_map(|child| project_field(child, mapped_columns, is_v2_0))
  192 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  193 |             if !children.is_empty() {
  194 |                 return Some(lance_core::datatypes::Field {
  195 |                     children,
  196 |                     ..field.clone()
  197 |                 });
  198 |             }
  199 | 
  200 |             if field.children.is_empty() && mapped_columns.contains_key(&field.id) {
  201 |                 return Some(field.clone());
  202 |             }
  203 | 
  204 |             // V2.0 stores a physical header for structural fields. Keep that
  205 |             // header to preserve the parent's row count and validity, but leave
  206 |             // its children empty so missing descendants are null-filled by the
  207 |             // fragment reader instead of being added to this file's projection.
  208 |             if is_v2_0 && mapped_columns.contains_key(&field.id) {
  209 |                 return Some(lance_core::datatypes::Field {
  210 |                     children: Vec::new(),
  211 |                     ..field.clone()
  212 |                 });
  213 |             }
  214 |             None
  215 |         }
  216 | 
  217 |         if self.uses_v1_data_file_encoding() {
  218 |             return full_schema.project_by_ids(&self.fields, false);
  219 |         }
  220 |         let mapped_columns = self
  221 |             .fields
  222 |             .iter()
  223 |             .copied()
  224 |             .zip(self.column_indices.iter().copied())
  225 |             .filter(|(_, column_index)| *column_index >= 0)
  226 |             .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>();
  227 |         let is_v2_0 = matches!(
  228 |             (self.file_major_version, self.file_minor_version),
  229 |             (0, 3) | (2, 0)
  230 |         );
  231 |         Schema {
  232 |             fields: full_schema
  233 |                 .fields
  234 |                 .iter()
  235 |                 .filter_map(|field| project_field(field, &mapped_columns, is_v2_0))
  236 |                 .collect(),
  237 |             metadata: full_schema.metadata.clone(),
  238 |         }
  239 |     }

  241 |     fn uses_v1_data_file_encoding(&self) -> bool {
  242 |         self.file_major_version == 0 && self.file_minor_version < 3
  243 |     }

  253 |     pub fn validate(&self, base_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
  254 |         if self.uses_v1_data_file_encoding() {
  255 |             // A tombstone marks a field superseded by a later data file. It is
  256 |             // not a field id, so it carries no ordering; the live ids around it
  257 |             // must still be sorted and distinct.
  258 |             let live: Vec<i32> = self
  259 |                 .fields
  260 |                 .iter()
  261 |                 .copied()
  262 |                 .filter(|field| *field != TOMBSTONE_FIELD_ID)
  263 |                 .collect();
  264 |             if !live.windows(2).all(|w| w[0] < w[1]) {
  265 |                 return Err(Error::corrupt_file(
  266 |                     base_path.clone().join(self.path.clone()),
  267 |                     "contained unsorted or duplicate field ids",
  268 |                 ));
  269 |             }
  270 |         } else if self.column_indices.len() < self.fields.len() {
  271 |             // Every recorded field id must have a column index, but not every column needs
  272 |             // to be associated with a field id (extra columns are allowed).
  273 |             return Err(Error::corrupt_file(
  274 |                 base_path.clone().join(self.path.clone()),
  275 |                 "contained fewer column_indices than fields",
  276 |             ));
  277 |         }
  278 |         Ok(())
  279 |     }
  280 | }

  312 | /// Interns repeated data so that fragments with identical content share a
  313 | /// single heap allocation via `Arc`.
  314 | ///
  315 | /// At 20M fragments the deduplication typically saves multiple GB of heap
  316 | /// because every fragment in a homogeneous table carries the same field list,
  317 | /// and post-compaction fragments share identical version metadata bytes.
  318 | ///
  319 | /// Uses a `Vec`-based linear scan when the cache is small (<=16 entries)
  320 | /// and upgrades to `HashMap` for larger caches. In the common homogeneous
  321 | /// case (1-3 unique values), linear scan avoids per-fragment hashing overhead.
  322 | #[derive(Default)]
  323 | pub struct DataFileFieldInterner {
  324 |     fields: InternCache<i32>,
  325 |     column_indices: InternCache<i32>,
  326 |     inline_bytes: InternCache<u8>,
  327 | }
  328 | 
  329 | /// A cache that uses linear scan for small sizes and HashMap for large.
  330 | /// The threshold is chosen so that scan + compare is cheaper than hash for
  331 | /// typical payload sizes (20-200 bytes).
  332 | enum InternCache<T: Eq + std::hash::Hash + Clone> {
  333 |     Small(Vec<Arc<[T]>>),
  334 |     Large(HashMap<Arc<[T]>, ()>),
  335 | }
  336 | 
  337 | const INTERN_CACHE_UPGRADE_THRESHOLD: usize = 16;
  338 | 
  339 | impl<T: Eq + std::hash::Hash + Clone> Default for InternCache<T> {
  340 |     fn default() -> Self {
  341 |         Self::Small(Vec::new())
  342 |     }
  343 | }
  344 | 
  345 | impl<T: Eq + std::hash::Hash + Clone> InternCache<T> {
  346 |     fn intern(&mut self, v: Vec<T>) -> Arc<[T]> {
  347 |         match self {
  348 |             Self::Small(entries) => {
  349 |                 for existing in entries.iter() {
  350 |                     if existing.as_ref() == v.as_slice() {
  351 |                         return existing.clone();
  352 |                     }
  353 |                 }
  354 |                 let arc: Arc<[T]> = Arc::from(v);
  355 |                 entries.push(arc.clone());
  356 |                 if entries.len() > INTERN_CACHE_UPGRADE_THRESHOLD {
  357 |                     let mut map = HashMap::with_capacity(entries.len());
  358 |                     for e in entries.drain(..) {
  359 |                         map.insert(e, ());
  360 |                     }
  361 |                     *self = Self::Large(map);
  362 |                 }
  363 |                 arc
  364 |             }
  365 |             Self::Large(map) => {
  366 |                 if let Some((existing, _)) = map.get_key_value(v.as_slice()) {
  367 |                     existing.clone()
  368 |                 } else {
  369 |                     let arc: Arc<[T]> = Arc::from(v);
  370 |                     map.insert(arc.clone(), ());
  371 |                     arc
  372 |                 }
  373 |             }
  374 |         }
  375 |     }
  376 | }

  391 |     /// Copy inline row ids out of the manifest buffer they were decoded from
  392 |     /// when they are a small share of it.
  393 |     ///
  394 |     /// Inline row ids decoded from a `Bytes` buffer are slices of that buffer
  395 |     /// (see [`InlineRowIds`]), and a slice keeps the whole allocation alive.
  396 |     /// That is the right trade when the row ids are most of the manifest, as
  397 |     /// they are for a compacted stable-row-id table, but a manifest whose row
  398 |     /// ids are a few percent of its bytes would pin the rest for nothing.
  399 |     /// `buffer_len` is the size of the decoded buffer.
  400 |     pub fn detach_sparse_inline_row_ids(&mut self, buffer_len: usize) {
  401 |         let inline_bytes: usize = self
  402 |             .fragments
  403 |             .iter()
  404 |             .filter_map(|fragment| match &fragment.row_id_meta {
  405 |                 Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) => Some(data.len()),
  406 |                 _ => None,
  407 |             })
  408 |             .sum();
  409 |         // Keep the slices while the row ids are at least a quarter of the buffer.
  410 |         if inline_bytes == 0 || inline_bytes.saturating_mul(4) >= buffer_len {
  411 |             return;
  412 |         }
  413 |         for fragment in Arc::make_mut(&mut self.fragments) {
  414 |             if let Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) = &fragment.row_id_meta {
  415 |                 let copied = InlineRowIds::from(Bytes::copy_from_slice(data));
  416 |                 fragment.row_id_meta = Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(copied));
  417 |             }
  418 |         }
  419 |     }

  421 |     /// Check the current fragment list and update the high water mark
  422 |     pub fn update_max_fragment_id(&mut self) {
  423 |         // If there are no fragments, don't update max_fragment_id
  424 |         if self.fragments.is_empty() {
  425 |             return;
  426 |         }
  427 | 
  428 |         let max_fragment_id = self
  429 |             .fragments
  430 |             .iter()
  431 |             .map(|f| f.id)
  432 |             .max()
  433 |             .unwrap() // Safe because we checked fragments is not empty
  434 |             .try_into()
  435 |             .unwrap();
  436 | 
  437 |         match self.max_fragment_id {
  438 |             None => {
  439 |                 // First time being set
  440 |                 self.max_fragment_id = Some(max_fragment_id);
  441 |             }
  442 |             Some(current_max) => {
  443 |                 // Only update if the computed max is greater than current
  444 |                 // This preserves the high water mark even when fragments are deleted
  445 |                 if max_fragment_id > current_max {
  446 |                     self.max_fragment_id = Some(max_fragment_id);
  447 |                 }
  448 |             }
  449 |         }
  450 |     }
  451 | 
  452 |     /// Return the max fragment id.
  453 |     /// Note this does not support recycling of fragment ids.
  454 |     ///
  455 |     /// This will return None if there are no fragments and max_fragment_id was never set.
  456 |     pub fn max_fragment_id(&self) -> Option<u64> {
  457 |         if let Some(max_id) = self.max_fragment_id {
  458 |             // Return the stored high water mark
  459 |             Some(max_id.into())
  460 |         } else {
  461 |             // Not yet set, compute from fragment list
  462 |             self.fragments.iter().map(|f| f.id).max()
  463 |         }
  464 |     }

  466 |     /// Get the max used field id

  468 |     /// This is different than [Schema::max_field_id] because it also considers
  469 |     /// the field ids in the data files that have been dropped from the schema,
  470 |     /// including overlay files referenced by fragments.
  471 |     pub fn max_field_id(&self) -> i32 {
  472 |         let schema_max_id = self.schema.max_field_id().unwrap_or(-1);
  473 |         let fragment_max_id = self
  474 |             .fragments
  475 |             .iter()
  476 |             .flat_map(|fragment| {
  477 |                 fragment
  478 |                     .referenced_lance_files()
  479 |                     .flat_map(|file| file.fields.iter())
  480 |             })
  481 |             .copied()
  482 |             .max()
  483 |             .unwrap_or(-1);
  484 |         schema_max_id.max(fragment_max_id)
  485 |     }

  487 |     /// Return the fragments that are newer than the given manifest.
  488 |     /// Note this does not support recycling of fragment ids.
  489 |     pub fn fragments_since(&self, since: &Self) -> Result<Vec<Fragment>> {
  490 |         if since.version >= self.version {
  491 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  492 |                 "fragments_since: given version {} is newer than manifest version {}",
  493 |                 since.version, self.version
  494 |             )));
  495 |         }
  496 |         let start = since.max_fragment_id();
  497 |         Ok(self
  498 |             .fragments
  499 |             .iter()
  500 |             .filter(|&f| start.map(|s| f.id > s).unwrap_or(true))
  501 |             .cloned()
  502 |             .collect())

  505 |     /// Find the fragments that contain the rows, identified by the offset range.
  506 |     ///
  507 |     /// Note that the offsets are the logical offsets of rows, not row IDs.
  508 |     ///
  509 |     ///
  510 |     /// Parameters
  511 |     /// ----------
  512 |     /// range: `Range<usize>`
  513 |     ///     Offset range
  514 |     ///
  515 |     /// Returns
  516 |     /// -------
  517 |     /// Vec<(usize, Fragment)>
  518 |     ///    A vector of `(starting_offset_of_fragment, fragment)` pairs.
  519 |     ///
  520 |     pub fn fragments_by_offset_range(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> Vec<(usize, &Fragment)> {
  521 |         let start = range.start;
  522 |         let end = range.end;
  523 |         let idx = self
  524 |             .fragment_offsets
  525 |             .binary_search(&start)
  526 |             .unwrap_or_else(|idx| idx - 1);
  527 | 
  528 |         let mut fragments = vec![];
  529 |         for i in idx..self.fragments.len() {
  530 |             if self.fragment_offsets[i] >= end
  531 |                 || self.fragment_offsets[i] + self.fragments[i].num_rows().unwrap_or_default()
  532 |                     <= start
  533 |             {
  534 |                 break;
  535 |             }
  536 |             fragments.push((self.fragment_offsets[i], &self.fragments[i]));
  537 |         }
  538 | 
  539 |         fragments
  540 |     }

  554 |     /// Get the summary information of a manifest.
  555 |     ///
  556 |     /// This function calculates various statistics about the manifest, including:
  557 |     /// - total_files_size: Total size of all data files in bytes
  558 |     /// - total_fragments: Total number of fragments in the dataset
  559 |     /// - total_data_files: Total number of data files across all fragments
  560 |     /// - total_deletion_files: Total number of deletion files
  561 |     /// - total_data_file_rows: Total number of rows in data files
  562 |     /// - total_deletion_file_rows: Total number of deleted rows in deletion files
  563 |     /// - total_rows: Total number of rows in the dataset
  564 |     pub fn summary(&self) -> ManifestSummary {
  565 |         // Calculate total fragments
  566 |         let mut summary =
  567 |             self.fragments
  568 |                 .iter()
  569 |                 .fold(ManifestSummary::default(), |mut summary, f| {
  570 |                     // Count data files in the current fragment
  571 |                     summary.total_data_files += f.files.len() as u64;
  572 |                     // Sum the number of rows for the current fragment (if available)
  573 |                     if let Some(num_rows) = f.num_rows() {
  574 |                         summary.total_rows += num_rows as u64;
  575 |                     }
  576 |                     // Sum file sizes for all data files in the current fragment (if available)
  577 |                     for data_file in &f.files {
  578 |                         if let Some(size_bytes) = data_file.file_size_bytes.get() {
  579 |                             summary.total_files_size += size_bytes.get();
  580 |                         }
  581 |                     }
  582 |                     // Check and count if the current fragment has a deletion file
  583 |                     if f.deletion_file.is_some() {
  584 |                         summary.total_deletion_files += 1;
  585 |                     }
  586 |                     // Sum the number of deleted rows from the deletion file (if available)
  587 |                     if let Some(deletion_file) = &f.deletion_file
  588 |                         && let Some(num_deleted) = deletion_file.num_deleted_rows
  589 |                     {
  590 |                         summary.total_deletion_file_rows += num_deleted as u64;
  591 |                     }
  592 |                     summary
  593 |                 });
  594 |         summary.total_fragments = self.fragments.len() as u64;
  595 |         summary.total_data_file_rows = summary.total_rows + summary.total_deletion_file_rows;
  596 | 
  597 |         summary
  598 |     }
  599 | }

  627 |         ConcreteFileVersion::V2_0

  786 | impl WriterVersion {
  787 |     /// Split a version string into clean version (major.minor.patch), prerelease, and build metadata.
  788 |     ///
  789 |     /// Returns None if the input is not a valid semver string.
  790 |     ///
  791 |     /// For example:
  792 |     /// - "2.0.0-rc.1" -> Some(("2.0.0", Some("rc.1"), None))
  793 |     /// - "2.0.0-rc.1+build.123" -> Some(("2.0.0", Some("rc.1"), Some("build.123")))
  794 |     /// - "2.0.0+build.123" -> Some(("2.0.0", None, Some("build.123")))
  795 |     /// - "not-a-version" -> None
  796 |     fn split_version(full_version: &str) -> Option<(String, Option<String>, Option<String>)> {
  797 |         let mut parsed = semver::Version::parse(full_version).ok()?;
  798 | 
  799 |         let prerelease = if parsed.pre.is_empty() {
  800 |             None
  801 |         } else {
  802 |             Some(parsed.pre.to_string())
  803 |         };
  804 | 
  805 |         let build_metadata = if parsed.build.is_empty() {
  806 |             None
  807 |         } else {
  808 |             Some(parsed.build.to_string())
  809 |         };
  810 | 
  811 |         // Remove prerelease and build metadata to get clean version
  812 |         parsed.pre = semver::Prerelease::EMPTY;
  813 |         parsed.build = semver::BuildMetadata::EMPTY;
  814 |         Some((parsed.to_string(), prerelease, build_metadata))
  815 |     }

  817 |     /// Try to parse the version string as a semver string. Returns None if
  818 |     /// not successful.
  819 |     #[deprecated(note = "Use `lance_lib_version()` instead")]
  820 |     pub fn semver(&self) -> Option<(u32, u32, u32, Option<&str>)> {
  821 |         // First split by '-' to separate the version from the pre-release tag
  822 |         let (version_part, tag) = if let Some(dash_idx) = self.version.find('-') {
  823 |             (
  824 |                 &self.version[..dash_idx],
  825 |                 Some(&self.version[dash_idx + 1..]),
  826 |             )
  827 |         } else {
  828 |             (self.version.as_str(), None)
  829 |         };
  830 | 
  831 |         let mut parts = version_part.split('.');
  832 |         let major = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().ok()?;
  833 |         let minor = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().ok()?;
  834 |         let patch = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().ok()?;
  835 | 
  836 |         Some((major, minor, patch, tag))
  837 |     }

  842 |     /// This method reconstructs the full semantic version by combining the version field
  843 |     /// with the prerelease and build_metadata fields (if present). For example:
  844 |     /// - version="2.0.0" + prerelease=Some("rc.1") -> "2.0.0-rc.1"
  845 |     /// - version="2.0.0" + prerelease=Some("rc.1") + build_metadata=Some("build.123") -> "2.0.0-rc.1+build.123"
  846 |     pub fn lance_lib_version(&self) -> Option<semver::Version> {
  847 |         if self.library != "lance" {

  852 | 
  853 |         if let Some(ref prerelease) = self.prerelease {
  854 |             version.pre = semver::Prerelease::new(prerelease).ok()?;
  855 |         }

  857 |         if let Some(ref build_metadata) = self.build_metadata {

  171 |     // Each legacy group owns a compaction remap. Address resolution follows its
  172 |     // fragment lineage, rather than searching every group in a legacy version.
  173 |     fn decode_content(index_version: i32, content: Bytes) -> Result<Self> {
  174 |         validate_index_version(index_version)?;
  175 |         let mut remaining = content;
  176 |         let mut transitions = Vec::new();
  177 |         let mut has_unsupported_transitions = false;
  178 |         while remaining.has_remaining() {
  179 |             let (tag, payload) = next_field(&mut remaining)?;
  180 |             match tag {
  181 |                 1 => {
  182 |                     let version = pb::Version::decode(require_message(tag, payload)?)
  183 |                         .map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  184 |                     for group in version.groups {
  185 |                         transitions.push(decode_transition(pb::Transition {
  186 |                             sources: group.old_fragments,
  187 |                             destinations: group.new_fragments,
  188 |                             mapping: Some(transition::Mapping::OrderedCompaction(
  189 |                                 pb::OrderedCompaction {
  190 |                                     changed_row_addrs: group.changed_row_addrs,
  191 |                                 },
  192 |                             )),
  193 |                         })?);
  194 |                     }
  195 |                 }
  196 |                 2 => {
  197 |                     if index_version == 0 {
  198 |                         return Err(corrupt("tagged transitions require FRI index_version 1"));
  199 |                     }
  200 |                     let raw = require_message(tag, payload)?;
  201 |                     let mut fields = raw.clone();
  202 |                     let mut has_mapping = false;
  203 |                     let mut has_unknown_fields = false;
  204 |                     while fields.has_remaining() {
  205 |                         let (tag, payload) = next_field(&mut fields)?;
  206 |                         if matches!(tag, ORDERED_COMPACTION_FIELD | STABLE_PARTITION_FIELD) {
  207 |                             require_message(tag, payload)?;
  208 |                             if has_mapping {
  209 |                                 return Err(corrupt(
  210 |                                     "transition contains multiple mapping alternatives",
  211 |                                 ));
  212 |                             }
  213 |                             has_mapping = true;
  214 |                         } else if !matches!(tag, 1 | 2) {
  215 |                             has_unknown_fields = true;
  216 |                         }
  217 |                     }
  218 |                     if has_unknown_fields {
  219 |                         // The field number does not tell us whether this is metadata
  220 |                         // or a mapping. Neither is safe to partially interpret.
  221 |                         has_unsupported_transitions = true;
  222 |                         continue;
  223 |                     }
  224 |                     if !has_mapping {
  225 |                         return Err(corrupt("transition has no mapping"));
  226 |                     }
  227 |                     let decoded =
  228 |                         pb::Transition::decode(raw).map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  229 |                     transitions.push(decode_transition(decoded)?);
  230 |                 }
  231 |                 _ => {} // Unknown envelope fields do not participate in address resolution.
  232 |             }
  233 |         }
  234 |         let transitions = order_lineage(transitions)?;
  235 |         let consumers = transitions
  236 |             .iter()
  237 |             .enumerate()
  238 |             .flat_map(|(position, transition)| {
  239 |                 transition
  240 |                     .sources()
  241 |                     .iter()
  242 |                     .map(move |source| (source.id as u32, position))
  243 |             })
  244 |             .collect();
  245 |         let producers = transitions
  246 |             .iter()
  247 |             .enumerate()
  248 |             .flat_map(|(position, transition)| {
  249 |                 transition
  250 |                     .destinations()
  251 |                     .iter()
  252 |                     .map(move |destination| (destination.id as u32, position))
  253 |             })
  254 |             .collect();
  255 |         Ok(Self {
  256 |             transitions,
  257 |             consumers,
  258 |             producers,
  259 |             has_unsupported_transitions,
  260 |         })
  261 |     }

  310 |                         }
  311 |                 })

  333 | // Keep length-delimited payloads as zero-copy slices of the original history.
  334 | fn next_field(input: &mut Bytes) -> Result<(u32, Option<Bytes>)> {
  335 |     let (tag, wire) = decode_key(input).map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  336 |     let payload = if wire == WireType::LengthDelimited {
  337 |         let length = decode_varint(input).map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  338 |         if length > input.remaining() as u64 {
  339 |             return Err(corrupt(format!(
  340 |                 "field {tag} length {length} exceeds remaining {} bytes",
  341 |                 input.remaining()
  342 |             )));
  343 |         }
  344 |         Some(input.split_to(length as usize))
  345 |     } else {
  346 |         skip_field(wire, tag, input, DecodeContext::default())
  347 |             .map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  348 |         None
  349 |     };
  350 |     Ok((tag, payload))
  351 | }

  357 | fn validate_digests(digests: &[pb::FragmentDigest], is_destination: bool) -> Result<u64> {
  358 |     let mut ids = RoaringBitmap::new();
  359 |     let mut live_rows = 0_u64;
  360 |     for digest in digests {
  361 |         if digest.id >= u64::from(RowAddress::TOMBSTONE_FRAG)
  362 |             || digest.physical_rows > u32::MAX as u64
  363 |             || digest.num_deleted_rows > digest.physical_rows
  364 |         {
  365 |             return Err(corrupt(format!("invalid fragment digest {digest:?}")));
  366 |         }
  367 |         if !ids.insert(digest.id as u32) {
  368 |             return Err(corrupt(format!(
  369 |                 "duplicate fragment {} in transition",
  370 |                 digest.id
  371 |             )));
  372 |         }
  373 |         if is_destination && digest.num_deleted_rows != 0 {
  374 |             return Err(corrupt(format!(
  375 |                 "destination fragment {} has creation-time deletions",
  376 |                 digest.id
  377 |             )));
  378 |         }
  379 |         live_rows = live_rows
  380 |             .checked_add(digest.physical_rows - digest.num_deleted_rows)
  381 |             .ok_or_else(|| corrupt("fragment row count overflow"))?;
  382 |     }
  383 |     Ok(live_rows)
  384 | }

  386 | fn decode_transition(value: pb::Transition) -> Result<Transition> {
  387 |     if value.sources.is_empty() {
  388 |         return Err(corrupt("transition has no source fragments"));
  389 |     }
  390 |     let source_rows = validate_digests(&value.sources, false)?;
  391 |     let destination_rows = validate_digests(&value.destinations, true)?;
  392 |     if source_rows != destination_rows {
  393 |         return Err(corrupt(format!(
  394 |             "transition row counts differ: {source_rows} source rows, {destination_rows} destination rows"
  395 |         )));
  396 |     }
  397 |     let fingerprint = *blake3::hash(&value.encode_to_vec()).as_bytes();
  398 |     let mapping = match value.mapping {
  399 |         Some(transition::Mapping::OrderedCompaction(ordered)) => {
  400 |             let mut cursor = Cursor::new(&ordered.changed_row_addrs);
  401 |             let bitmap = RoaringTreemap::deserialize_from(&mut cursor)
  402 |                 .map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  403 |             if cursor.position() != ordered.changed_row_addrs.len() as u64 {
  404 |                 return Err(corrupt("trailing bytes in ordered compaction bitmap"));
  405 |             }
  406 |             for source in &value.sources {
  407 |                 let survivors =
  408 |                     bitmap.range_cardinality(RowAddress::address_range(source.id as u32));
  409 |                 if survivors != source.physical_rows - source.num_deleted_rows {
  410 |                     return Err(corrupt(format!(
  411 |                         "fragment {} bitmap has {survivors} survivors inconsistent with its digest",
  412 |                         source.id
  413 |                     )));
  414 |                 }
  415 |             }
  416 |             let layout = |fragments: &[pb::FragmentDigest]| {
  417 |                 fragments
  418 |                     .iter()
  419 |                     .map(|f| (f.id as u32, f.physical_rows as u32))
  420 |                     .collect()
  421 |             };
  422 |             let remap = RowAddrRemap::compact_with_layout([GroupInputWithLayout {
  423 |                 rewritten_old_row_addrs: bitmap,
  424 |                 old_frags: layout(&value.sources),
  425 |                 new_frags: layout(&value.destinations),
  426 |             }])
  427 |             .map_err(|e| corrupt(e.to_string()))?;
  428 |             Mapping::OrderedCompaction(Arc::new(remap))
  429 |         }
  430 |         Some(transition::Mapping::StablePartition(partition)) => {
  431 |             Uuid::parse_str(&partition.map_id).map_err(|e| {
  432 |                 corrupt(format!(
  433 |                     "invalid stable partition map_id {:?}: {e}",
  434 |                     partition.map_id
  435 |                 ))
  436 |             })?;
  437 |             if partition.map_size_bytes == 0 {
  438 |                 return Err(corrupt("stable partition map_size_bytes must be positive"));
  439 |             }
  440 |             Mapping::StablePartition(partition)
  441 |         }
  442 |         None => return Err(corrupt("transition has no mapping")),
  443 |     };
  444 |     Ok(Transition {
  445 |         fingerprint,
  446 |         sources: value.sources,
  447 |         destinations: value.destinations,
  448 |         mapping,
  449 |     })
  450 | }

  452 | fn order_lineage(transitions: Vec<Transition>) -> Result<Vec<Transition>> {
  453 |     let mut producers = HashMap::new();
  454 |     let mut consumers = RoaringBitmap::new();
  455 |     for (index, transition) in transitions.iter().enumerate() {
  456 |         for destination in &transition.destinations {
  457 |             if producers
  458 |                 .insert(destination.id, (index, destination.physical_rows))
  459 |                 .is_some()
  460 |             {
  461 |                 return Err(corrupt(format!(
  462 |                     "duplicate producer for fragment {}",
  463 |                     destination.id
  464 |                 )));
  465 |             }
  466 |         }
  467 |         for source in &transition.sources {
  468 |             if !consumers.insert(source.id as u32) {
  469 |                 return Err(corrupt(format!(
  470 |                     "duplicate consumer for fragment {}",
  471 |                     source.id
  472 |                 )));
  473 |             }
  474 |         }
  475 |     }
  476 |     let mut incoming = vec![0; transitions.len()];
  477 |     let mut outgoing = vec![Vec::new(); transitions.len()];
  478 |     for (consumer, transition) in transitions.iter().enumerate() {
  479 |         for source in &transition.sources {
  480 |             if let Some(&(producer, physical_rows)) = producers.get(&source.id) {
  481 |                 if source.physical_rows != physical_rows {
  482 |                     return Err(corrupt(format!(
  483 |                         "inconsistent physical_rows for fragment {}",
  484 |                         source.id
  485 |                     )));
  486 |                 }
  487 |                 incoming[consumer] += 1;
  488 |                 outgoing[producer].push(consumer);
  489 |             }
  490 |         }
  491 |     }
  492 |     let mut ready: VecDeque<_> = incoming
  493 |         .iter()
  494 |         .enumerate()
  495 |         .filter_map(|(i, &n)| (n == 0).then_some(i))
  496 |         .collect();
  497 |     let mut ordered = Vec::with_capacity(transitions.len());
  498 |     let mut transitions: Vec<_> = transitions.into_iter().map(Some).collect();
  499 |     while let Some(index) = ready.pop_front() {
  500 |         // Each transition is queued once, when its incoming count reaches zero.
  501 |         let transition = transitions[index]
  502 |             .take()
  503 |             .ok_or_else(|| corrupt("lineage visited a transition twice"))?;
  504 |         ordered.push(transition);
  505 |         for &consumer in &outgoing[index] {
  506 |             incoming[consumer] -= 1;
  507 |             if incoming[consumer] == 0 {
  508 |                 ready.push_back(consumer);
  509 |             }
  510 |         }
  511 |     }
  512 |     if ordered.len() != transitions.len() {
  513 |         return Err(corrupt("fragment lineage contains a cycle"));
  514 |     }
  515 |     Ok(ordered)
  516 | }

  326 |                          as it is while its file still holds rows of the withdrawn retired \
  327 |                          fragments; withdrawing it whole so the segment is rebuilt",
  328 |                         index.name,
  329 |                         index.uuid,
  330 |                         bitmap.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>()
  331 |                     );
  332 |                     withdrawn |= &*bitmap;
  333 |                     bitmap.clear();
  334 |                 }
  335 |             }
  336 |             if bitmap.is_empty() {
  337 |                 emptied.push(index.uuid);
  338 |             }
  339 |             log::warn!(
  340 |                 "index {} (segment {}): withdrew {} fragment(s) of coverage after an in-place \
  341 |                  rewrite of an indexed column; the rows they covered are scanned until the index \
  342 |                  is optimized",
  343 |                 index.name,
  344 |                 index.uuid,
  345 |                 withdrawn.len()
  346 |             );
  347 |         }
  348 |         Self::retire_emptied_segments(indices, &emptied);
  349 |     }

  351 |     /// Drop the metadata of every segment in `emptied` whose logical index
  352 |     /// still has another segment with coverage (or with unknown coverage).
  353 |     /// The last segment of a name is kept, empty, as the record of what to
  354 |     /// rebuild.
  355 |     fn retire_emptied_segments(indices: &mut Vec<IndexMetadata>, emptied: &[Uuid]) {
  356 |         let removable: Vec<Uuid> = emptied
  357 |             .iter()
  358 |             .copied()
  359 |             .filter(|uuid| {
  360 |                 let Some(name) = indices
  361 |                     .iter()
  362 |                     .find(|index| index.uuid == *uuid)
  363 |                     .map(|index| index.name.as_str())
  364 |                 else {
  365 |                     return false;
  366 |                 };
  367 |                 indices.iter().any(|sibling| {
  368 |                     sibling.name == name
  369 |                         && sibling.uuid != *uuid
  370 |                         && sibling
  371 |                             .fragment_bitmap
  372 |                             .as_ref()
  373 |                             .is_none_or(|bitmap| !bitmap.is_empty())
  374 |                 })
  375 |             })
  376 |             .collect();
  377 |         if removable.is_empty() {
  378 |             return;
  379 |         }
  380 |         indices.retain(|index| {
  381 |             let retired = removable.contains(&index.uuid);
  382 |             if retired {
  383 |                 log::info!(
  384 |                     "index {} (segment {}): every fragment of its coverage was withdrawn and a \
  385 |                      sibling segment still serves the index; the segment leaves the manifest and \
  386 |                      its files are reclaimed by index cleanup",
  387 |                     index.name,
  388 |                     index.uuid
  389 |                 );
  390 |             }
  391 |             !retired
  392 |         });
  393 |     }

  395 |     /// If an operation modifies one or more fields in a fragment then we need to remove
  396 |     /// that fragment from any indices that cover one of the modified fields.
  397 |     pub fn prune_updated_fields_from_indices(
  398 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  399 |         updated_fragments: &[Fragment],
  400 |         fields_modified: &[u32],
  401 |     ) {
  402 |         if fields_modified.is_empty() {
  403 |             return;
  404 |         }
  405 | 
  406 |         // If we modified any fields in the fragments then we need to remove those fragments
  407 |         // from the index if the index covers one of those modified fields.
  408 |         let fields_modified_set = fields_modified.iter().collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  409 |         for index in indices.iter_mut() {
  410 |             if index
  411 |                 .fields
  412 |                 .iter()
  413 |                 .any(|field_id| fields_modified_set.contains(&u32::try_from(*field_id).unwrap()))
  414 |                 && let Some(fragment_bitmap) = &mut index.fragment_bitmap
  415 |             {
  416 |                 for fragment_id in updated_fragments.iter().map(|f| f.id as u32) {
  417 |                     fragment_bitmap.remove(fragment_id);
  418 |                 }
  419 |             }
  420 |         }
  421 |     }

  423 |     /// Map each (non-tombstoned) field id in a fragment to the path of the data
  424 |     /// file that backs it.
  425 |     fn fragment_field_paths(frag: &Fragment) -> HashMap<i32, &str> {
  426 |         let mut map = HashMap::new();
  427 |         for file in &frag.files {
  428 |             for &field_id in file.fields.iter() {
  429 |                 if field_id >= 0 {
  430 |                     map.insert(field_id, file.path.as_str());
  431 |                 }
  432 |             }
  433 |         }
  434 |         map
  435 |     }

  437 |     /// The columns a `Merge` rewrote in place: for each fragment present in
  438 |     /// both lists, the fields still present whose backing data file path
  439 |     /// changed. Brand-new fragments carry nothing stale.
  440 |     pub fn merge_rewritten_fields(
  441 |         prev_fragments: &[Fragment],
  442 |         new_fragments: &[Fragment],
  443 |     ) -> Vec<(u64, Vec<u32>)> {
  444 |         let prev_by_id: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> =
  445 |             prev_fragments.iter().map(|f| (f.id, f)).collect();
  446 |         new_fragments
  447 |             .iter()
  448 |             .filter_map(|new_frag| {
  449 |                 let prev = prev_by_id.get(&new_frag.id)?;
  450 |                 let prev_paths = Self::fragment_field_paths(prev);
  451 |                 let new_paths = Self::fragment_field_paths(new_frag);
  452 |                 let mut changed: Vec<u32> = prev_paths
  453 |                     .iter()
  454 |                     .filter(|(field_id, prev_path)| {
  455 |                         new_paths
  456 |                             .get(*field_id)
  457 |                             .is_some_and(|new_path| new_path != *prev_path)
  458 |                     })
  459 |                     .map(|(field_id, _)| *field_id as u32)
  460 |                     .collect();
  461 |                 changed.sort_unstable();
  462 |                 (!changed.is_empty()).then_some((new_frag.id, changed))
  463 |             })
  464 |             .collect()
  465 |     }

  467 |     /// After a `Rewrite` fully compacts a fragment, its data overlays are baked
  468 |     /// into the new fragment's base data. An index built *before* one of those
  469 |     /// overlays (`overlay.committed_version > index.dataset_version`) indexed the
  470 |     /// stale pre-overlay values -- and unlike a live overlay, the compacted
  471 |     /// fragment no longer signals that staleness to the query path. Drop each
  472 |     /// rewritten (new) fragment from the coverage of any index covering a field
  473 |     /// such an overlay supplied, so those rows fall back to a flat scan.
  474 |     pub(super) fn prune_overlay_stale_fields_from_indices(
  475 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  476 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  477 |     ) {
  478 |         for group in groups {
  479 |             // field id -> newest overlay committed_version supplying that field
  480 |             let mut overlaid_field_versions: HashMap<i32, u64> = HashMap::new();
  481 |             for old_frag in &group.old_fragments {
  482 |                 for overlay in &old_frag.overlays {
  483 |                     for &field_id in overlay.data_file.fields.iter() {
  484 |                         if field_id < 0 {
  485 |                             // Tombstoned (obsolete) overlay field: supplies nothing.
  486 |                             continue;
  487 |                         }
  488 |                         let entry = overlaid_field_versions.entry(field_id).or_insert(0);
  489 |                         *entry = (*entry).max(overlay.committed_version);
  490 |                     }
  491 |                 }
  492 |             }
  493 |             if overlaid_field_versions.is_empty() {
  494 |                 continue;
  495 |             }
  496 | 
  497 |             let new_fragment_ids = group
  498 |                 .new_fragments
  499 |                 .iter()
  500 |                 .map(|f| f.id as u32)
  501 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  502 |             for index in indices.iter_mut() {
  503 |                 let is_stale = index.fields.iter().any(|field_id| {
  504 |                     overlaid_field_versions
  505 |                         .get(field_id)
  506 |                         .is_some_and(|&overlay_version| overlay_version > index.dataset_version)
  507 |                 });
  508 |                 if is_stale && let Some(fragment_bitmap) = &mut index.fragment_bitmap {
  509 |                     for new_id in &new_fragment_ids {
  510 |                         fragment_bitmap.remove(*new_id);
  511 |                     }
  512 |                 }
  513 |             }
  514 |         }
  515 |     }

  517 |     pub(crate) fn retain_relevant_indices(
  518 |         indices: &mut Vec<IndexMetadata>,
  519 |         schema: &Schema,
  520 |         fragments: &[Fragment],
  521 |     ) {
  522 |         let field_ids = schema
  523 |             .fields_pre_order()
  524 |             .map(|f| f.id)
  525 |             .collect::<HashSet<_>>();
  526 | 
  527 |         // Remove indices for fields no longer in schema
  528 |         indices.retain(|existing_index| {
  529 |             existing_index
  530 |                 .fields
  531 |                 .iter()
  532 |                 .all(|field_id| field_ids.contains(field_id))
  533 |                 || is_system_index(existing_index)
  534 |         });
  535 | 
  536 |         let mut indices_by_name: std::collections::HashMap<String, Vec<&IndexMetadata>> =
  537 |             std::collections::HashMap::new();
  538 | 
  539 |         for index in indices.iter() {
  540 |             if index.name != FRAG_REUSE_INDEX_NAME {
  541 |                 indices_by_name
  542 |                     .entry(index.name.clone())
  543 |                     .or_default()
  544 |                     .push(index);
  545 |             }
  546 |         }
  547 | 
  548 |         let mut uuids_to_keep = std::collections::HashSet::new();
  549 | 
  550 |         let existing_fragments = fragments
  551 |             .iter()
  552 |             .map(|f| f.id as u32)
  553 |             .collect::<RoaringBitmap>();
  554 | 
  555 |         // Under a tagged fragment reuse history a segment's stored bitmap is
  556 |         // its provenance (the retired source fragments it was built from),
  557 |         // not the fragments it serves: its live coverage is derived at query
  558 |         // time by translating through the history, and is empty against the
  559 |         // live fragments by construction once its sources were rewritten.
  560 |         // Measuring such a segment here would drop it. Every segment is kept
  561 |         // instead; superseded segments are pruned by the tagged maintenance
  562 |         // path, which reasons on derived coverage.
  563 |         let tagged = indices.iter().any(is_tagged);
  564 | 
  565 |         for (_, same_name_indices) in indices_by_name {
  566 |             if tagged {
  567 |                 for index in same_name_indices {
  568 |                     uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  569 |                 }
  570 |                 continue;
  571 |             }
  572 |             // Unknown coverage is not empty coverage: a segment whose bitmap is
  573 |             // missing has never been measured, and dropping it deletes an index
  574 |             // that migration could not open yet.
  575 |             let (unknown_coverage, same_name_indices): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = same_name_indices
  576 |                 .into_iter()
  577 |                 .partition(|index| index.fragment_bitmap.is_none());
  578 |             for index in unknown_coverage {
  579 |                 uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  580 |             }
  581 | 
  582 |             if same_name_indices.len() > 1 {
  583 |                 let (empty_indices, non_empty_indices): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) =
  584 |                     same_name_indices.iter().partition(|index| {
  585 |                         index
  586 |                             .effective_fragment_bitmap(&existing_fragments)
  587 |                             .as_ref()
  588 |                             .is_none_or(|bitmap| bitmap.is_empty())
  589 |                     });
  590 | 
  591 |                 if non_empty_indices.is_empty() {
  592 |                     // All indices are empty -- keep only the oldest definition.
  593 |                     //
  594 |                     // An empty index definition is still correct: the scanner
  595 |                     // falls back to scanning unindexed fragments, and normal
  596 |                     // index maintenance rebuilds coverage once rows accrue.
  597 |                     // Dropping the definition instead would silently lose the
  598 |                     // index whenever an operation replaces every fragment it
  599 |                     // covered (e.g. a full table rewrite), leaving the dataset
  600 |                     // without its declared index.
  601 |                     let mut sorted_indices = empty_indices;
  602 |                     sorted_indices.sort_by_key(|index: &&IndexMetadata| index.dataset_version);
  603 | 
  604 |                     if let Some(oldest) = sorted_indices.first() {
  605 |                         uuids_to_keep.insert(oldest.uuid);
  606 |                     }
  607 |                 } else {
  608 |                     for index in non_empty_indices {
  609 |                         uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  610 |                     }
  611 |                 }
  612 |             } else {
  613 |                 // Single index whose column is still in schema: keep it, even
  614 |                 // when its coverage is empty (see the all-empty note above).
  615 |                 if let Some(index) = same_name_indices.first() {
  616 |                     uuids_to_keep.insert(index.uuid);
  617 |                 }
  618 |             }
  619 |         }
  620 | 
  621 |         indices.retain(|index| {
  622 |             index.name == FRAG_REUSE_INDEX_NAME || uuids_to_keep.contains(&index.uuid)
  623 |         });
  624 |     }
  625 | 
  626 |     /// The rewrite groups whose index bitmaps follow the rewrite (source ids
  627 |     /// swapped for destination ids). Groups covered by the stable-partition
  628 |     /// transitions' sources are excluded: they redistribute rows, so their
  629 |     /// bitmaps keep the retired source ids as provenance and the tagged
  630 |     /// fragment reuse index entry records the row-level translation. A group
  631 |     /// must be entirely reordered or entirely order-preserving.
  632 |     pub(super) fn ordered_rewrite_groups(
  633 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  634 |         reordered_sources: Option<&RoaringBitmap>,
  635 |     ) -> Result<Vec<RewriteGroup>> {
  636 |         let Some(sources) = reordered_sources else {
  637 |             return Ok(groups.to_vec());
  638 |         };
  639 |         let mut ordered = Vec::new();
  640 |         for group in groups {
  641 |             let covered = group
  642 |                 .old_fragments
  643 |                 .iter()
  644 |                 .filter(|frag| sources.contains(frag.id as u32))
  645 |                 .count();
  646 |             if covered == 0 {
  647 |                 ordered.push(group.clone());
  648 |             } else if covered != group.old_fragments.len() {
  649 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(
  650 |                     "a rewrite group mixes transition-covered and order-preserving source fragments",
  651 |                 ));
  652 |             }
  653 |         }
  654 |         Ok(ordered)
  655 |     }
  656 | 
  657 |     pub(super) fn recalculate_fragment_bitmap(
  658 |         old: &RoaringBitmap,
  659 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  660 |     ) -> Result<RoaringBitmap> {
  661 |         let mut new_bitmap = old.clone();
  662 |         for group in groups {
  663 |             let any_in_index = group
  664 |                 .old_fragments
  665 |                 .iter()
  666 |                 .any(|frag| old.contains(frag.id as u32));
  667 |             let all_in_index = group
  668 |                 .old_fragments
  669 |                 .iter()
  670 |                 .all(|frag| old.contains(frag.id as u32));
  671 |             // Any rewrite group may or may not be covered by the index.  However, if any fragment
  672 |             // in a rewrite group was previously covered by the index then all fragments in the rewrite
  673 |             // group must have been previously covered by the index.  plan_compaction takes care of
  674 |             // this for us so this should be safe to assume.
  675 |             if any_in_index {
  676 |                 if all_in_index {
  677 |                     for frag_id in group.old_fragments.iter().map(|frag| frag.id as u32) {
  678 |                         new_bitmap.remove(frag_id);
  679 |                     }
  680 |                     new_bitmap.extend(group.new_fragments.iter().map(|frag| frag.id as u32));
  681 |                 } else {
  682 |                     return Err(Error::invalid_input(
  683 |                         "The compaction plan included a rewrite group that was a split of indexed and non-indexed data",
  684 |                     ));
  685 |                 }
  686 |             }
  687 |         }
  688 |         Ok(new_bitmap)
  689 |     }

  691 |     pub(super) fn handle_rewrite_indices(
  692 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  693 |         rewritten_indices: &[RewrittenIndex],
  694 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  695 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  696 |         let mut modified_indices = HashSet::new();
  697 | 
  698 |         for rewritten_index in rewritten_indices {
  699 |             if !modified_indices.insert(rewritten_index.old_id) {
  700 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  701 |                     "An invalid compaction plan must have been generated because multiple tasks modified the same index: {}",
  702 |                     rewritten_index.old_id
  703 |                 )));
  704 |             }
  705 | 
  706 |             // Skip indices that no longer exist (may have been removed by concurrent operation)
  707 |             let Some(index) = indices
  708 |                 .iter_mut()
  709 |                 .find(|idx| idx.uuid == rewritten_index.old_id)
  710 |             else {
  711 |                 continue;
  712 |             };
  713 | 
  714 |             index.fragment_bitmap = Some(Self::recalculate_fragment_bitmap(
  715 |                 index.fragment_bitmap.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
  716 |                     Error::invalid_input(format!(
  717 |                         "Cannot rewrite index {} which did not store fragment bitmap",
  718 |                         index.uuid
  719 |                     ))
  720 |                 })?,
  721 |                 groups,
  722 |             )?);
  723 |             index.uuid = rewritten_index.new_id;
  724 |             // Update file sizes to match the new index files. When not available
  725 |             // (e.g., from older writers), clear the old file sizes to avoid
  726 |             // using stale sizes from the pre-remap index.
  727 |             index.files = rewritten_index.new_index_files.clone();
  728 |         }
  729 |         Ok(())
  730 |     }

  732 |     pub(super) fn handle_rewrite_fragments(
  733 |         final_fragments: &mut Vec<Fragment>,
  734 |         groups: &[RewriteGroup],
  735 |         fragment_id: &mut u64,
  736 |         version: u64,
  737 |         _next_row_id: Option<&u64>,
  738 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  739 |         for group in groups {
  740 |             // If the old fragments are contiguous, find the range
  741 |             let replace_range = {
  742 |                 let start = final_fragments
  743 |                     .iter()
  744 |                     .enumerate()
  745 |                     .find(|(_, f)| f.id == group.old_fragments[0].id)
  746 |                     .ok_or_else(|| {
  747 |                         Error::commit_conflict_source(
  748 |                             version,
  749 |                             format!(
  750 |                                 "dataset does not contain a fragment a rewrite operation wants to replace: id={}",
  751 |                                 group.old_fragments[0].id
  752 |                             )
  753 |                             .into(),
  754 |                         )
  755 |                     })?
  756 |                     .0;
  757 | 
  758 |                 // Verify old_fragments matches contiguous range
  759 |                 let mut i = 1;
  760 |                 loop {
  761 |                     if i == group.old_fragments.len() {
  762 |                         break Some(start..start + i);
  763 |                     }
  764 |                     if final_fragments[start + i].id != group.old_fragments[i].id {
  765 |                         break None;
  766 |                     }
  767 |                     i += 1;
  768 |                 }
  769 |             };
  770 | 
  771 |             let new_fragments = Self::fragments_with_ids(group.new_fragments.clone(), fragment_id)
  772 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  773 | 
  774 |             // Version metadata for rewritten fragments is handled by the compaction code
  775 |             // (recalc_versions_for_rewritten_fragments) which preserves version information
  776 |             // from the original fragments. We don't modify it here.
  777 | 
  778 |             if let Some(replace_range) = replace_range {
  779 |                 // Efficiently path using slice
  780 |                 final_fragments.splice(replace_range, new_fragments);
  781 |             } else {
  782 |                 // Slower path for non-contiguous ranges
  783 |                 for fragment in group.old_fragments.iter() {
  784 |                     final_fragments.retain(|f| f.id != fragment.id);
  785 |                 }
  786 |                 final_fragments.extend(new_fragments);
  787 |             }
  788 |         }
  789 |         Ok(())
  790 |     }
  791 | }

 1399 |     /// Under a tagged history a translating segment's stored bitmap is its
 1400 |     /// retired provenance, empty against the live fragments by construction,

 1403 |     #[test]
 1404 |     fn test_retain_keeps_every_segment_under_tagged_history() {
 1405 |         let schema = create_test_schema(&[1, 2]);
 1406 |         let fragments = vec![Fragment::new(10), Fragment::new(11)];
 1407 |         let mut indices = vec![
 1408 |             create_system_index(FRAG_REUSE_INDEX_NAME, 1),
 1409 |             // Two translating segments: provenance {0} and {1} are both dead.
 1410 |             create_test_index("idx_a", 1, 1, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([0])), false),
 1411 |             create_test_index("idx_a", 1, 2, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([1])), false),
 1412 |             // A rebuilt sibling directly covering a live destination.
 1413 |             create_test_index("idx_a", 1, 3, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([10])), false),
 1414 |             // An all-dead group and an all-empty group: every member kept.
 1415 |             create_test_index("vec_b", 1, 1, Some(RoaringBitmap::from_iter([0])), true),
