   59 | /// Table config key that opts a table into writing clustered deletions as
   60 | /// `Range` segments (`U64Segment::Ranges`). Set it to `true` with
   61 | /// `update_config`.
   62 | ///
   63 | /// Manifests written afterwards re-encode bitmap row id segments as runs of
   64 | /// `Range` segments where that is smaller. That is the
   65 | /// existing wire format, so any version reads the result, but a reader without
   66 | /// the compact in-memory form handles thousands of segments per fragment
   67 | /// slowly. That is why it is opt-in rather than the default.
   68 | ///
   69 | /// Setting the key back to `false` only stops further conversions. Fragments
   70 | /// already written as `Range` segments keep that encoding until something else
   71 | /// rewrites their row ids (compaction, for example), so coordinate reader
   72 | /// upgrades before enabling it.
   73 | pub const RANGE_SEGMENTS_CONFIG_KEY: &str = "lance.row_ids.range_segments";
   74 | 
   75 | fn range_segments_enabled(manifest: &Manifest) -> bool {
   76 |     manifest
   77 |         .config
   78 |         .get(RANGE_SEGMENTS_CONFIG_KEY)
   79 |         .is_some_and(|value| str_is_truthy(value))
   80 | }
   81 | 
   82 | /// Re-encode inline row id sequences as runs of `Range` segments when the
   83 | /// table has opted in.
   84 | ///
   85 | /// Fragments that the previous manifest already re-encoded are left alone
   86 | /// (their inline bytes are the very same allocation), so a commit pays only
   87 | /// for the fragments it changed; enabling the key re-encodes every fragment
   88 | /// once.
   89 | fn apply_range_segments(
   90 |     manifest: &mut Manifest,
   91 |     current_manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
   92 | ) -> Result<()> {
   93 |     if !range_segments_enabled(manifest) {
   94 |         return Ok(());
   95 |     }
   96 |     let unchanged: HashMap<u64, *const u8> = current_manifest
   97 |         .filter(|current| range_segments_enabled(current))
   98 |         .map(|current| {
   99 |             current
  100 |                 .fragments
  101 |                 .iter()
  102 |                 .filter_map(|fragment| match &fragment.row_id_meta {
  103 |                     Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) => Some((fragment.id, data.as_ptr())),
  104 |                     _ => None,
  105 |                 })
  106 |                 .collect()
  107 |         })
  108 |         .unwrap_or_default();
  109 |     let fragments = Arc::make_mut(&mut manifest.fragments);
  110 |     for fragment in fragments.iter_mut() {
  111 |         let Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) = &fragment.row_id_meta else {
  112 |             continue;
  113 |         };
  114 |         if unchanged.get(&fragment.id) == Some(&data.as_ptr()) {
  115 |             continue;
  116 |         }
  117 |         let mut sequence = read_row_ids(&data[..])?;
  118 |         if sequence.use_range_segments() {
  119 |             fragment.row_id_meta = Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(write_row_ids(&sequence).into()));
  120 |         }
  121 |     }
  122 |     Ok(())
  123 | }

  207 |     /// Every non-system logical index, mapped to what determines its coverage.
  208 |     ///
  209 |     /// A logical index may be backed by several physical segments, so "did this
  210 |     /// index change" is a question about the whole set. Sorted by UUID so the
  211 |     /// two sides compare positionally.
  212 |     pub fn logical_index_segments(indices: &[IndexMetadata]) -> LogicalIndexSegments {
  213 |         let mut by_name: LogicalIndexSegments = BTreeMap::new();
  214 |         for idx in indices.iter().filter(|idx| !is_system_index(idx)) {
  215 |             by_name
  216 |                 .entry(idx.name.clone())
  217 |                 .or_default()
  218 |                 .push(CoverageIdentity {
  219 |                     uuid: idx.uuid,
  220 |                     fragment_bitmap: idx.fragment_bitmap.clone(),
  221 |                 });
  222 |         }
  223 |         for segments in by_name.values_mut() {
  224 |             segments.sort_unstable_by_key(|segment| segment.uuid);
  225 |         }
  226 |         by_name
  227 |     }

  229 |     /// Apply MemWAL index-coverage rules once the final index list is known.
  230 |     ///
  231 |     /// Coverage records that a base-table index contains the rows a compaction
  232 |     /// copied in, and the WAL pod retires SSTables against it.
  233 |     ///
  234 |     /// It is derived, not reported. An index covering every fragment live at the
  235 |     /// transaction's read version holds every row compaction had copied in by
  236 |     /// then, so it is caught up to that version's `compacted_sstables`. That is
  237 |     /// the only proof available: nothing maps a generation to the fragments its
  238 |     /// rows landed in, so covering the table as the transaction read it is how
  239 |     /// an index shows it covered those rows. Fragments appended since are a
  240 |     /// later gap.
  241 |     ///
  242 |     /// Deriving rather than transmitting means no claim can go stale between
  243 |     /// inspection and commit, the answer survives rebase (`read_version` is
  244 |     /// fixed for a transaction's life), and any operation can earn coverage --
  245 |     /// an ordinary reindex that fully covers no longer has to throw its work
  246 |     /// away and wait for a repair.
  247 |     ///
  248 |     /// Only meaningful once catch-up is required, where a missing entry means
  249 |     /// "not caught up" and the SSTables stay. A legacy table reads a missing
  250 |     /// entry as "fully caught up", so this leaves it untouched rather than
  251 |     /// making the table look more covered than it is.
  252 |     pub fn apply_mem_wal_index_coverage(
  253 |         final_indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  254 |         segments_before: &LogicalIndexSegments,
  255 |         read_version_state: Option<ReadVersionState<'_>>,
  256 |         new_version: u64,
  257 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  258 |         let Some(pos) = final_indices
  259 |             .iter()
  260 |             .position(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  261 |         else {
  262 |             // The system index went away with this transaction (MemWAL disable,
  263 |             // or an overwrite). There is no coverage left to maintain.
  264 |             return Ok(());
  265 |         };
  266 | 
  267 |         let mut details = load_mem_wal_index_details(final_indices[pos].clone())?;
  268 | 
  269 |         // Nothing has ever been compacted, so no index can be behind and there
  270 |         // is no coverage to invalidate.
  271 |         if details.compacted_sstables.is_empty() && details.index_catchup.is_empty() {
  272 |             return Ok(());
  273 |         }
  274 | 
  275 |         let segments_after = Self::logical_index_segments(final_indices);
  276 |         let catchup_before = std::mem::take(&mut details.index_catchup);
  277 | 
  278 |         // Per shard: what this commit records as compacted, and the most the
  279 |         // read version may credit. Generations compacted after that read landed
  280 |         // in fragments no index under consideration has seen; the committed
  281 |         // value caps it in turn, so a read version since rolled back cannot
  282 |         // retire SSTables no live commit copied in.
  283 |         let read_details = read_version_state
  284 |             .map(|state| {
  285 |                 state
  286 |                     .indices
  287 |                     .iter()
  288 |                     .find(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  289 |                     .cloned()
  290 |                     .map(load_mem_wal_index_details)
  291 |                     .transpose()
  292 |             })
  293 |             .transpose()?
  294 |             .flatten();
  295 |         let shards: Vec<(Uuid, u64, u64)> = details
  296 |             .compacted_sstables
  297 |             .iter()
  298 |             .map(|committed| {
  299 |                 let at_read = read_details
  300 |                     .as_ref()
  301 |                     .and_then(|read| {
  302 |                         read.compacted_sstables
  303 |                             .iter()
  304 |                             .find(|s| s.shard_id == committed.shard_id)
  305 |                     })
  306 |                     .map_or(0, |s| s.generation);
  307 |                 (
  308 |                     committed.shard_id,
  309 |                     committed.generation,
  310 |                     at_read.min(committed.generation),
  311 |                 )
  312 |             })
  313 |             .collect();
  314 | 
  315 |         // Every fragment live when the transaction read the table. An index
  316 |         // spanning all of them holds every row compacted by then.
  317 |         let read_fragments: Option<RoaringBitmap> = read_version_state.map(|state| {
  318 |             state
  319 |                 .manifest
  320 |                 .fragments
  321 |                 .iter()
  322 |                 .map(|fragment| fragment.id as u32)
  323 |                 .collect()
  324 |         });
  325 | 
  326 |         let covers_read_version = |segments: &[CoverageIdentity]| -> bool {
  327 |             let Some(required) = read_fragments.as_ref() else {
  328 |                 return false;
  329 |             };
  330 |             if required.is_empty() {
  331 |                 // Subset-of-empty is trivially true, so this would credit every
  332 |                 // index on a table with no fragments. Refused because an empty
  333 |                 // fragment list is not only what an emptied table looks like:
  334 |                 // it is also what a manifest written before #8438 looks like,
  335 |                 // where UpdateMemWalState published no fragments at all. On
  336 |                 // such a table the SSTables are the last copy of those rows,
  337 |                 // and crediting coverage would retire them. The cost is that a
  338 |                 // genuinely emptied table keeps its SSTables.
  339 |                 return false;
  340 |             }
  341 |             let mut covered = RoaringBitmap::new();
  342 |             for segment in segments {
  343 |                 match segment.fragment_bitmap.as_ref() {
  344 |                     Some(bitmap) => covered |= bitmap,
  345 |                     // An unknown bitmap cannot be shown to cover anything.
  346 |                     None => return false,
  347 |                 }
  348 |             }
  349 |             required.is_subset(&covered)
  350 |         };
  351 | 
  352 |         let mut rebuilt: Vec<IndexCatchupProgress> = Vec::new();
  353 |         for (name, after) in segments_after.iter() {
  354 |             // Compared by [`CoverageIdentity`], not segment UUID: an Update
  355 |             // that touches an indexed field prunes a segment's fragment bitmap
  356 |             // in place while keeping its UUID, so a UUID-only comparison would
  357 |             // carry a position forward that the index no longer earns.
  358 |             let unchanged = segments_before.get(name) == Some(after);
  359 |             let carried = unchanged
  360 |                 .then(|| catchup_before.iter().find(|e| e.index_name == *name))
  361 |                 .flatten();
  362 |             let proven = covers_read_version(after);
  363 | 
  364 |             if carried.is_none() && !proven {
  365 |                 // Changed, and nothing shows the new index covers the read
  366 |                 // version. No entry: a missing one reads as "not caught up".
  367 |                 continue;
  368 |             }
  369 | 
  370 |             let generations = shards
  371 |                 .iter()
  372 |                 .map(|&(shard_id, committed, creditable)| {
  373 |                     let prior = carried
  374 |                         .and_then(|entry| entry.caught_up_generation_for_shard(&shard_id))
  375 |                         .unwrap_or(0);
  376 |                     let credited = if proven { creditable } else { 0 };
  377 |                     // Takes the better of what this commit proves and what an
  378 |                     // unchanged index already held, so a commit reading an older
  379 |                     // version does not lower a position it cannot re-prove. The
  380 |                     // clamp is the exception: a position above what this commit
  381 |                     // records as compacted describes rows no live commit copied
  382 |                     // in.
  383 |                     CompactedSsTable::new(shard_id, prior.max(credited).min(committed))
  384 |                 })
  385 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  386 |             if generations.iter().all(|g| g.generation == 0) {
  387 |                 continue;
  388 |             }
  389 |             rebuilt.push(IndexCatchupProgress::new(name.clone(), generations));
  390 |         }
  391 |         rebuilt.sort_by(|a, b| a.index_name.cmp(&b.index_name));
  392 | 
  393 |         let mut before_sorted = catchup_before;
  394 |         before_sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.index_name.cmp(&b.index_name));
  395 |         if rebuilt == before_sorted {
  396 |             return Ok(());
  397 |         }
  398 | 
  399 |         let dropped: Vec<&str> = before_sorted
  400 |             .iter()
  401 |             .map(|e| e.index_name.as_str())
  402 |             .filter(|name| !rebuilt.iter().any(|kept| kept.index_name == *name))
  403 |             .collect();
  404 |         if !dropped.is_empty() {
  405 |             // The first thing to check when SSTables stop becoming trimmable.
  406 |             log::info!(
  407 |                 "MemWAL index catch-up invalidated at version {new_version} for {dropped:?}: \
  408 |                  these indices changed and no longer cover the version this commit read"
  409 |             );
  410 |         }
  411 | 
  412 |         details.index_catchup = rebuilt;
  413 |         final_indices[pos] = new_mem_wal_index_meta(new_version, details)?;
  414 |         Ok(())
  415 |     }

  417 |     /// Drop coverage for indices a post-`build_manifest` step narrowed.
  418 |     ///
  419 |     /// The derivation runs while the manifest is being built, but the index list
  420 |     /// is not final there: `migrate_indices` can recalculate a segment's
  421 |     /// fragment bitmap and keep its UUID, so an index can narrow after its
  422 |     /// position was decided. It reports which ones it touched rather than the
  423 |     /// caller re-snapshotting every bitmap to find out. Only ever removes.
  424 |     pub fn withdraw_coverage_invalidated_after_build(
  425 |         indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  426 |         changed: &[String],
  427 |         new_version: u64,
  428 |     ) -> Result<()> {
  429 |         if changed.is_empty() {
  430 |             return Ok(());
  431 |         }
  432 |         let Some(pos) = indices
  433 |             .iter()
  434 |             .position(|idx| idx.name == MEM_WAL_INDEX_NAME)
  435 |         else {
  436 |             return Ok(());
  437 |         };
  438 |         let mut details = load_mem_wal_index_details(indices[pos].clone())?;
  439 |         let before = details.index_catchup.len();
  440 |         details
  441 |             .index_catchup
  442 |             .retain(|entry| !changed.contains(&entry.index_name));
  443 |         if details.index_catchup.len() == before {
  444 |             return Ok(());
  445 |         }
  446 |         log::info!(
  447 |             "MemWAL index catch-up withdrawn at version {new_version} for {changed:?}: \
  448 |              these indices were recalculated after their coverage was derived"
  449 |         );
  450 |         indices[pos] = new_mem_wal_index_meta(new_version, details)?;
  451 |         Ok(())
  452 |     }

  454 |     /// Step one of a commit attempt: what the operation settles about the
  455 |     /// index list, computed against the manifest current at the attempt.
  456 |     ///
  457 |     /// Runs the tagged-table write gate (`system_index::frag_reuse::gate`)
  458 |     /// before anything is derived, keeps `current_indices` as the original
  459 |     /// list, and derives the prepared list: on an in-place column rewrite
  460 |     /// (an update with `fields_modified`, a merge swapping a column's data
  461 |     /// file, a data replacement) the coverage it invalidates is withdrawn
  462 |     /// along a tagged fragment reuse history or pruned by fragment id on any
  463 |     /// other table (`withdraw_in_place_rewrites`). Every other operation
  464 |     /// prepares the list unchanged; `Restore` never reaches the builder and
  465 |     /// restores its snapshot's list whole.
  466 |     ///
  467 |     /// `frag_reuse_ledger` is the decoded history of the current entry when
  468 |     /// the caller read it (the commit path decodes it once per attempt for
  469 |     /// the operations above); without it an inline history is decoded from
  470 |     /// the entry and an external one is refused, so a commit never guesses
  471 |     /// at the lineage. A history that does not decode is an error, never
  472 |     /// treated as "no lineage". `frag_reuse` is what the commit path settled
  473 |     /// about the entry itself.
  474 |     pub fn prepare_indices(
  475 |         &self,
  476 |         current_manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
  477 |         current_indices: Vec<IndexMetadata>,
  478 |         config: &ManifestBuildConfig,
  479 |         frag_reuse_ledger: Option<Arc<crate::system_index::frag_reuse::ledger::FragReuseLedger>>,
  480 |         frag_reuse: FragReuseUpdate,
  481 |     ) -> Result<PreparedIndices> {
  482 |         crate::system_index::frag_reuse::gate::classify(
  483 |             &self.operation,
  484 |             current_manifest,
  485 |             &current_indices,
  486 |             &frag_reuse,
  487 |             config.migration_next_row_id,
  488 |         )?;
  489 |         let mut prepared = current_indices.clone();
  490 |         if let Some(manifest) = current_manifest {
  491 |             let rewrites = Self::rewritten_physical_columns(
  492 |                 &self.operation,
  493 |                 &manifest.schema,
  494 |                 &manifest.fragments,
  495 |             );
  496 |             if !rewrites.is_empty() {
  497 |                 let lineage =
  498 |                     crate::system_index::frag_reuse::lineage::TaggedLineage::from_indices_with_ledger(
  499 |                         &current_indices,
  500 |                         frag_reuse_ledger,
  501 |                     )?;
  502 |                 let live: RoaringBitmap = manifest
  503 |                     .fragments
  504 |                     .iter()
  505 |                     .filter_map(|fragment| u32::try_from(fragment.id).ok())
  506 |                     .collect();
  507 |                 Self::withdraw_in_place_rewrites(
  508 |                     &mut prepared,
  509 |                     rewrites,
  510 |                     &manifest.schema,
  511 |                     &live,
  512 |                     lineage.as_ref(),
  513 |                 );
  514 |             }
  515 |         }
  516 |         Ok(PreparedIndices::new(
  517 |             current_manifest.map(|manifest| manifest.version),
  518 |             current_indices,
  519 |             prepared,
  520 |             frag_reuse,
  521 |         ))
  522 |     }

  543 |     /// [`Self::build_manifest`] with the version this transaction read.
  544 |     ///
  545 |     /// Supplied by the commit path, which already materializes that version.
  546 |     /// `None` where there is none to read -- dataset creation and detached
  547 |     /// commits -- in which case no index can be shown to cover it and coverage
  548 |     /// is left as the invalidation rules put it.
  549 |     ///
  550 |     /// Prepares the index list itself with nothing settled about the
  551 |     /// fragment reuse entry and no history read, so it stays safe on its
  552 |     /// own: a tagged entry on a `Rewrite` or a `CreateIndex` touching a
  553 |     /// tagged entry is refused, an inline history is decoded from the entry

 4150 |     fn test_data_overlay_build_manifest_multi_fragment() {
 4151 |         // Overlays targeting two distinct fragments are each applied and stamped.
 4152 |         // A targeted fragment already carrying an overlay (committed at v3) gets
 4153 |         // the new overlay appended and stamped while its existing overlay is
 4154 |         // preserved, and a fragment the operation does not target is passed
 4155 |         // through with its existing overlays untouched.
 4156 |         let mut frag0 = Fragment::new(0);
 4157 |         frag0.overlays = vec![overlay_with_field(5, 3)]; // targeted, pre-existing at v3
 4158 |         let frag1 = Fragment::new(1);
 4159 |         let mut frag2 = Fragment::new(2);
 4160 |         frag2.overlays = vec![overlay_with_field(9, 3)]; // untargeted, committed at v3
 4161 |         let schema = ArrowSchema::new(vec![ArrowField::new("id", DataType::Int32, false)]);
 4162 |         let mut manifest = Manifest::new(
 4163 |             LanceSchema::try_from(&schema).unwrap(),
 4164 |             Arc::new(vec![frag0, frag1, frag2]),
 4165 |             crate::format::DataStorageFormat::new(ConcreteFileVersion::V2_0),
 4166 |             HashMap::new(),
 4167 |         );
 4168 |         // The pre-existing overlays were committed at v3, so the current
 4169 |         // manifest must be at least that version; the new commit then stamps
 4170 |         // its overlay at v4, keeping the fragment's overlays newest-last.
 4171 |         manifest.version = 3;
 4172 | 
 4173 |         let txn = Transaction::new(
 4174 |             manifest.version,
 4175 |             Operation::DataOverlay {
 4176 |                 groups: vec![
 4177 |                     DataOverlayGroup {
 4178 |                         fragment_id: 0,
 4179 |                         overlays: vec![overlay_with_field(1, 0)],
 4180 |                     },
 4181 |                     DataOverlayGroup {
 4182 |                         fragment_id: 1,
 4183 |                         overlays: vec![overlay_with_field(2, 0)],
 4184 |                     },
 4185 |                 ],
 4186 |             },
 4187 |             None,
 4188 |         );
 4189 | 
 4190 |         let (result, _) = txn
 4191 |             .build_manifest(Some(&manifest), vec![], "txn", &default_build_config())
 4192 |             .unwrap();
 4193 | 
 4194 |         let frag = |id: u64| {
 4195 |             result
 4196 |                 .fragments
 4197 |                 .iter()
 4198 |                 .find(|f| f.id == id)
 4199 |                 .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("fragment {id} missing from result"))
 4200 |         };
 4201 |         // The already-overlaid target keeps its v3 overlay and appends the new
 4202 |         // one, stamped to the new version.
 4203 |         assert_eq!(frag(0).overlays.len(), 2);
 4204 |         assert_eq!(frag(0).overlays[0].committed_version, 3);
 4205 |         assert_eq!(frag(0).overlays[1].committed_version, result.version);
 4206 |         // The fresh target gets its overlay, stamped to the new version.
 4207 |         assert_eq!(frag(1).overlays.len(), 1);
 4208 |         assert_eq!(frag(1).overlays[0].committed_version, result.version);
 4209 |         // The untargeted fragment is unchanged: same overlay, original version.
 4210 |         assert_eq!(frag(2).overlays.len(), 1);
 4211 |         assert_eq!(frag(2).overlays[0].committed_version, 3);
 4212 |         assert!(result.version > manifest.version);
 4213 |     }

  264 |                         // UPDATE branch: stable row ID resolves to a source row in an
  265 |                         // existing fragment.  Copy created_at from the original row so
  266 |                         // the row's first-appearance version is preserved across rewrites.
  267 |                         resolve_created_at_version(rid, &row_id_to_source, &version_cache)
  268 |                     } else {
  269 |                         // INSERT branch: stable row ID has no source in existing fragments
  270 |                         // (e.g. NOT MATCHED arm of MERGE INTO).  The row first appears in
  271 |                         // this commit, so created_at equals the new commit version.
  272 |                         new_version
  273 |                     }
  274 |                 })
  275 |                 .collect();
  276 |             debug_assert_eq!(created_at_versions.len(), physical_rows);
  277 | 
  278 |             let created_at_seq = RowDatasetVersionSequence::from_versions(&created_at_versions);
  279 |             fragment.created_at_version_meta = Some(
  280 |                 RowDatasetVersionMeta::from_sequence(&created_at_seq).map_err(|e| {
  281 |                     Error::internal(format!(
  282 |                         "Failed to create created_at version metadata: {}",
  283 |                         e
  284 |                     ))
  285 |                 })?,
  286 |             );
  287 | 
  288 |             fragment.last_updated_at_version_meta = build_version_meta(fragment, new_version);
  289 |         } else {
  290 |             let version_meta = build_version_meta(fragment, new_version);
  291 |             fragment.last_updated_at_version_meta = version_meta.clone();
  292 |             fragment.created_at_version_meta = version_meta;
  293 |         }
  294 |     }
  295 |     Ok(())
  296 | }

  298 | impl Transaction {
  299 |     /// collect the pure(the num of row IDs are equal to the physical rows) "rewrite rows" updated fragment ids
  300 |     pub(super) fn collect_pure_rewrite_row_update_frags_ids(
  301 |         fragments: &[Fragment],
  302 |     ) -> Result<Vec<u64>> {
  303 |         let mut pure_update_frag_ids = Vec::new();
  304 | 
  305 |         for fragment in fragments {
  306 |             let physical_rows = fragment
  307 |                 .physical_rows
  308 |                 .ok_or_else(|| Error::internal("Fragment does not have physical rows"))?
  309 |                 as u64;
  310 | 
  311 |             if let Some(row_id_meta) = &fragment.row_id_meta {
  312 |                 let existing_row_count = match row_id_meta {
  313 |                     RowIdMeta::Inline(data) => {
  314 |                         let sequence = read_row_ids(data)?;
  315 |                         sequence.len() as u64
  316 |                     }
  317 |                     // A spilled sequence always covers every physical row.
  318 |                     RowIdMeta::Column => physical_rows,
  319 |                 };
  320 | 
  321 |                 // only filter the fragments that match: all the rows have row id,
  322 |                 // which means it does not contain inserted rows in this fragment
  323 |                 if existing_row_count == physical_rows {
  324 |                     pure_update_frag_ids.push(fragment.id);
  325 |                 }
  326 |             }
  327 |         }
  328 | 
  329 |         Ok(pure_update_frag_ids)
  330 |     }
  331 | 
  332 |     pub(super) fn assign_row_ids(next_row_id: &mut u64, fragments: &mut [Fragment]) -> Result<()> {
  333 |         for fragment in fragments {
  334 |             let physical_rows = fragment
  335 |                 .physical_rows
  336 |                 .ok_or_else(|| Error::internal("Fragment does not have physical rows"))?
  337 |                 as u64;
  338 | 
  339 |             if fragment.row_id_meta.is_some() {
  340 |                 // we may meet merge insert case, it only has partial row ids.
  341 |                 // so here, we need to check if the row ids match the physical rows
  342 |                 // if yes, continue
  343 |                 // if not, fill the remaining row ids to the physical rows, then update row_id_meta
  344 | 
  345 |                 // Check if existing row IDs match the physical rows count
  346 |                 let existing_row_count = match &fragment.row_id_meta {
  347 |                     Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) => {
  348 |                         // Parse the serialized row ID sequence to get the count
  349 |                         let sequence = read_row_ids(data)?;
  350 |                         sequence.len() as u64
  351 |                     }
  352 |                     // A spilled sequence always covers every physical row.
  353 |                     Some(RowIdMeta::Column) => physical_rows,
  354 |                     _ => 0,
  355 |                 };
  356 | 
  357 |                 match existing_row_count.cmp(&physical_rows) {
  358 |                     Ordering::Equal => {
  359 |                         // Row IDs already match physical rows, continue to next fragment
  360 |                         continue;
  361 |                     }
  362 |                     Ordering::Less => {
  363 |                         // Partial row IDs - need to fill the remaining ones
  364 |                         let remaining_rows = physical_rows - existing_row_count;
  365 |                         let new_row_ids = *next_row_id..(*next_row_id + remaining_rows);
  366 | 
  367 |                         // Merge existing and new row IDs
  368 |                         let combined_sequence = match &fragment.row_id_meta {
  369 |                             Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(data)) => read_row_ids(data)?,
  370 |                             _ => {
  371 |                                 return Err(Error::internal(
  372 |                                     "Failed to deserialize existing row ID sequence",
  373 |                                 ));
  374 |                             }
  375 |                         };
  376 | 
  377 |                         let mut row_ids: Vec<u64> = combined_sequence.iter().collect();
  378 |                         for row_id in new_row_ids {
  379 |                             row_ids.push(row_id);
  380 |                         }
  381 |                         let combined_sequence = RowIdSequence::from(row_ids.as_slice());
  382 | 
  383 |                         let serialized = write_row_ids(&combined_sequence);
  384 |                         fragment.row_id_meta = Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(serialized.into()));
  385 |                         *next_row_id += remaining_rows;
  386 |                     }
  387 |                     Ordering::Greater => {
  388 |                         // More row IDs than physical rows - this shouldn't happen
  389 |                         return Err(Error::internal(format!(
  390 |                             "Fragment has more row IDs ({}) than physical rows ({})",
  391 |                             existing_row_count, physical_rows
  392 |                         )));
  393 |                     }
  394 |                 }
  395 |             } else {
  396 |                 let row_ids = *next_row_id..(*next_row_id + physical_rows);
  397 |                 let sequence = RowIdSequence::from(row_ids);
  398 |                 // TODO: write to a separate file if large. Possibly share a file with other fragments.
  399 |                 let serialized = write_row_ids(&sequence);
  400 |                 fragment.row_id_meta = Some(RowIdMeta::Inline(serialized.into()));
  401 |                 *next_row_id += physical_rows;
  402 |             }
  403 |         }
  404 |         Ok(())
  405 |     }
  406 | }

   92 |                     }
   93 |                 }
   94 |             }
   95 |             Ok(())

  101 | // An overwrite's fragments are newly written, so they are given fresh ids at
  102 | // commit time. A deletion file cannot come along for that ride: its path embeds
  103 | // the fragment id, so renumbering the fragment would orphan the deletion vector
  104 | // and silently resurrect deleted rows.
  105 | fn overwrite_fragments_valid(fragments: &[Fragment]) -> Result<()> {
  106 |     for fragment in fragments {
  107 |         if let Some(deletion_file) = &fragment.deletion_file {
  108 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  109 |                 "Overwrite fragments must be newly written, but fragment {} carries \
  110 |                  deletion file {}. Use Delete to commit deletions against existing \
  111 |                  fragments, or Merge to change their schema.",
  112 |                 fragment.id,
  113 |                 relative_deletion_file_path(fragment.id, deletion_file)
  114 |             )));
  115 |         }
  116 |     }
  117 |     Ok(())
  118 | }

  120 | fn schema_fragments_valid(
  121 |     manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
  122 |     schema: &Schema,
  123 |     fragments: &[Fragment],
  124 | ) -> Result<()> {
  125 |     if let Some(manifest) = manifest {
  126 |         return match manifest.data_storage_format.lance_file_format() {
  127 |             ConcreteFileVersion::V1 => schema_fragments_legacy_valid(schema, fragments),
  128 |             ConcreteFileVersion::V2_0
  129 |             | ConcreteFileVersion::V2_1
  130 |             | ConcreteFileVersion::V2_2
  131 |             | ConcreteFileVersion::V2_3 => schema_fragments_modern_valid(schema, fragments),
  132 |         };
  133 |     }
  134 |     schema_fragments_modern_valid(schema, fragments)

  137 | pub fn schema_fragments_modern_valid(_schema: &Schema, fragments: &[Fragment]) -> Result<()> {

  139 |     for fragment in fragments {
  140 |         for data_file in &fragment.files {
  141 |             if data_file.fields.iter().len() == 0 {
  142 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  143 |                     "Datafile {} does not contain any fields",
  144 |                     data_file.path
  145 |                 )));
  146 |             }
  147 |         }
  148 |     }
  149 |     Ok(())

  155 | pub fn schema_fragments_legacy_valid(schema: &Schema, fragments: &[Fragment]) -> Result<()> {
  156 |     // TODO: add additional validation. Consider consolidating with various
  157 |     // validate() methods in the codebase.
  158 |     for fragment in fragments {

  161 |                 .files
  162 |                 .iter()
  163 |                 .flat_map(|f| f.fields.iter())
  164 |                 .any(|f_id| f_id == &field.id)

  169 |                 )));

  172 |     }
  173 |     Ok(())

  176 | /// Returns true if Operation::Merge rewrote this fragment's column data files (Fragment::files
  177 | /// changed versus the previous manifest). Used to bump last_updated_at_version_meta only when
  178 | /// new column values were materialized to disk.
  179 | ///
  180 | /// Deletion file changes alone are not treated as rewrites: tombstones remove rows but
  181 | /// survivors did not receive new column bytes; stamping last_updated for those rows would be
  182 | /// incorrect for CDF.
  183 | #[inline]
  184 | pub(super) fn merge_fragment_physically_rewritten(prev: &Fragment, merged: &Fragment) -> bool {
  185 |     debug_assert_eq!(prev.id, merged.id);
  186 |     if prev.files.len() != merged.files.len() {
  187 |         return true;
  188 |     }
  189 |     // Compare identity fields only. file_size_bytes is an AtomicU64 cache that
  190 |     // concurrent scans can populate in place on the manifest's DataFile, so it
  191 |     // must not be part of the rewrite check.
  192 |     prev.files.iter().zip(merged.files.iter()).any(|(p, m)| {
  193 |         p.path != m.path
  194 |             || p.fields != m.fields
  195 |             || p.column_indices != m.column_indices
  196 |             || p.file_major_version != m.file_major_version
  197 |             || p.file_minor_version != m.file_minor_version
  198 |             || p.base_id != m.base_id
  199 |     })
  200 | }

  202 | /// Validate that Merge operations preserve all original fragments.
  203 | /// Merge operations should only add columns or rows, not reduce fragments.
  204 | /// This ensures fragments correspond at one-to-one with the original fragment list.
  205 | fn merge_fragments_valid(manifest: &Manifest, new_fragments: &[Fragment]) -> Result<()> {
  206 |     let original_fragments = manifest.fragments.as_ref();
  207 | 
  208 |     // Additional validation: ensure we're not accidentally reducing the fragment count
  209 |     if new_fragments.len() < original_fragments.len() {
  210 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  211 |             "Merge operation reduced fragment count from {} to {}. \
  212 |              Merge operations should only add columns, not reduce fragments.",
  213 |             original_fragments.len(),
  214 |             new_fragments.len()
  215 |         )));
  216 |     }
  217 | 
  218 |     // Collect new fragment IDs
  219 |     let new_fragment_map: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> =
  220 |         new_fragments.iter().map(|f| (f.id, f)).collect();
  221 | 
  222 |     // Check that all original fragments are preserved in the new fragments list
  223 |     // Validate that each original fragment's metadata is preserved
  224 |     let mut missing_fragments: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
  225 |     for original_fragment in original_fragments {
  226 |         if let Some(new_fragment) = new_fragment_map.get(&original_fragment.id) {
  227 |             // Validate physical_rows (row count) hasn't changed
  228 |             if original_fragment.physical_rows != new_fragment.physical_rows {
  229 |                 return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  230 |                     "Merge operation changed row count for fragment {}. \
  231 |                      Original: {:?}, New: {:?}. \
  232 |                      Merge operations should preserve fragment row counts and only add new columns.",
  233 |                     original_fragment.id,
  234 |                     original_fragment.physical_rows,
  235 |                     new_fragment.physical_rows
  236 |                 )));
  237 |             }
  238 |         } else {
  239 |             missing_fragments.push(original_fragment.id);
  240 |         }
  241 |     }
  242 | 
  243 |     if !missing_fragments.is_empty() {
  244 |         return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  245 |             "Merge operation is missing original fragments: {:?}. \
  246 |              Merge operations should preserve all original fragments and only add new columns. \
  247 |              Expected fragments: {:?}, but got: {:?}",
  248 |             missing_fragments,
  249 |             original_fragments.iter().map(|f| f.id).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
  250 |             new_fragment_map.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>()
  251 |         )));
  252 |     }
  253 | 
  254 |     Ok(())
  255 | }

  257 | /// Validate that a Merge schema preserves the dataset's field id bindings.
  258 | ///
  259 | /// Readers resolve columns by field id (name -> schema id -> DataFile::fields
  260 | /// position), so renumbered ids silently rebind live columns to other columns'
  261 | /// bytes. Shared ids must keep their field path. Their logical type,
  262 | /// nullability, storage encoding, and dictionary may change only when every
  263 | /// existing base or overlay file carrying the id is replaced and every
  264 | /// proposed fragment materializes the id in a base data file. New ids must
  265 | /// exceed the manifest's max so a dropped field's id is never reused. An
  266 | /// existing path may move to a fresh id only when every proposed fragment
  267 | /// materializes that id in a base data file (the `alter_columns` cast path).
  268 | /// Omitting a field (dropping it) and updating field metadata remain legal.
  269 | fn merge_schema_valid(
  270 |     manifest: &Manifest,
  271 |     new_schema: &Schema,
  272 |     fragments: &[Fragment],
  273 | ) -> Result<()> {
  274 |     let prior_schema = &manifest.schema;
  275 |     let new_fragment_map: HashMap<u64, &Fragment> = fragments
  276 |         .iter()
  277 |         .map(|fragment| (fragment.id, fragment))
  278 |         .collect();
  279 | 
  280 |     // Remap and semantic errors first: a renumbered schema usually violates
  281 |     // both the shared-id and new-id clauses.
  282 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  283 |         let Some(prior_field) = prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id) else {
  284 |             continue;
  285 |         };
  286 |         let prior_path = prior_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  287 |         let new_path = new_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  288 |         if prior_path != new_path {
  289 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  290 |                 "Merge operation remaps field id {} from \"{}\" to \"{}\". \
  291 |                  Merge must preserve the dataset's field ids: derive the new schema \
  292 |                  from the dataset's current schema instead of renumbering fields.",
  293 |                 field.id, prior_path, new_path
  294 |             )));
  295 |         }
  296 |         if let Some(changes) = shared_field_binding_changes(prior_field, field)
  297 |             && !is_field_binding_fully_rewritten(manifest, &new_fragment_map, field.id)
  298 |         {
  299 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  300 |                 "Merge operation changes field id {} (\"{}\") without rewriting it in \
  301 |                  every existing fragment: {}. Merge must preserve each existing field's \
  302 |                  logical type, nullability, storage encoding, and dictionary unless all \
  303 |                  existing base and overlay files carrying that field are replaced.",
  304 |                 field.id, new_path, changes
  305 |             )));
  306 |         }
  307 |     }
  308 | 
  309 |     let max_field_id = manifest.max_field_id();
  310 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  311 |         if prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id).is_none() && field.id <= max_field_id {
  312 |             let next_id_msg = match max_field_id.checked_add(1) {
  313 |                 Some(next_id) => format!("New fields must use ids of at least {}.", next_id),
  314 |                 None => {
  315 |                     "No further field id can be allocated because ids are exhausted.".to_string()
  316 |                 }
  317 |             };
  318 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  319 |                 "Merge operation assigns id {} to new field \"{}\", but ids up to {} are \
  320 |                  already used by current or dropped fields. {}",
  321 |                 field.id,
  322 |                 new_schema.field_path(field.id)?,
  323 |                 max_field_id,
  324 |                 next_id_msg
  325 |             )));
  326 |         }
  327 |     }
  328 | 
  329 |     let mut prior_paths = HashMap::with_capacity(prior_schema.fields_pre_order().count());
  330 |     for field in prior_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  331 |         prior_paths.insert(prior_schema.field_path(field.id)?, field);
  332 |     }
  333 |     for field in new_schema.fields_pre_order() {
  334 |         if prior_schema.field_by_id(field.id).is_some() {
  335 |             continue;
  336 |         }
  337 |         let new_path = new_schema.field_path(field.id)?;
  338 |         let Some(prior_field) = prior_paths.get(&new_path) else {
  339 |             continue;
  340 |         };
  341 |         let materialized = fragments.iter().all(|fragment| {
  342 |             fragment
  343 |                 .files
  344 |                 .iter()
  345 |                 .any(|file| file.fields.contains(&field.id))
  346 |         });
  347 |         if !materialized {
  348 |             return Err(Error::invalid_input(format!(
  349 |                 "Merge operation remaps existing field \"{}\" from id {} to id {} without \
  350 |                  rewriting its data. Every proposed fragment must materialize the new field \
  351 |                  id in a base data file.",
  352 |                 new_path, prior_field.id, field.id
  353 |             )));
  354 |         }
  355 |     }
  356 | 
  357 |     Ok(())
  358 | }
  359 | 
  360 | fn is_field_binding_fully_rewritten(
  361 |     manifest: &Manifest,
  362 |     new_fragment_map: &HashMap<u64, &Fragment>,
  363 |     field_id: i32,
  364 | ) -> bool {
  365 |     manifest.fragments.iter().all(|prior_fragment| {
  366 |         let Some(new_fragment) = new_fragment_map.get(&prior_fragment.id) else {
  367 |             return false;
  368 |         };
  369 | 
  370 |         let is_materialized = new_fragment
  371 |             .files
  372 |             .iter()
  373 |             .any(|file| file.fields.contains(&field_id));
  374 |         if !is_materialized {
  375 |             return false;
  376 |         }
  377 | 
  378 |         prior_fragment
  379 |             .referenced_lance_files()
  380 |             .filter(|file| file.fields.contains(&field_id))
  381 |             .all(|prior_file| {
  382 |                 !new_fragment.referenced_lance_files().any(|new_file| {
  383 |                     new_file.fields.contains(&field_id)
  384 |                         && new_file.base_id == prior_file.base_id
  385 |                         && new_file.path == prior_file.path
  386 |                 })
  387 |             })
  388 |     })
  389 | }
  390 | 
  391 | fn shared_field_binding_changes(prior: &Field, new: &Field) -> Option<String> {
  392 |     let mut changes = Vec::with_capacity(4);
  393 |     if prior.logical_type != new.logical_type {
  394 |         changes.push(format!(
  395 |             "logical type {} -> {}",
  396 |             prior.logical_type, new.logical_type
  397 |         ));
  398 |     }
  399 |     if prior.nullable != new.nullable {
  400 |         changes.push(format!("nullable {} -> {}", prior.nullable, new.nullable));
  401 |     }
  402 |     if prior.encoding != new.encoding {
  403 |         changes.push(format!(
  404 |             "storage encoding {:?} -> {:?}",
  405 |             prior.encoding, new.encoding
  406 |         ));
  407 |     }
  408 |     if prior.dictionary != new.dictionary {
  409 |         changes.push("dictionary".to_string());
  410 |     }
  411 |     if changes.is_empty() {
  412 |         None
  413 |     } else {
  414 |         Some(changes.join(", "))
  415 |     }
  416 | }

## SharedStream state transitions

The queue belongs to whichever side lags; the other side must have zero buffered count. A bounded permit is forgotten when a clone is enqueued and restored when that clone is consumed or discarded on dead-side drop. Polling upstream happens with the mutex released, but ownership prevents the peer from polling concurrently. Ready clears ownership; Pending keeps it. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:28-45; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:82-247)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Owned: obtain permit and claim side
    Owned --> Owned: upstream Pending
    Owned --> Idle: item ready; clone for live peer
    Owned --> Exhausted: upstream None
    Owned --> Idle: owning handle dropped
    Exhausted --> Exhausted: drain own buffer, then repeat None
```

This diagram omits per-side queue and permit substates; the transition implementation and ordering are given above, including capacity acquisition before poll-owner arbitration. Bounded(0) cannot reach Owned; upstream panic can remove inner without restoration; clone panic poisons the mutex. These are not recoverable states implemented by the diagram. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:47-80; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:127-247)

## CPU runtime publication and child reset

The first caller sets the installation-election flag, optionally registers the child hook, allocates/leaks a Runtime, then publishes its pointer. Other callers yield until non-null publication. The pointer lifetime comments justify unsafe shared references because allocation is never reclaimed; SeqCst is used throughout publication/reset. Child reset clears pointer and election flag without reclaiming the inherited runtime, while retaining the hook-installed flag. Initialization panic and ignored registration errors are limitations, not successful recovery paths. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:89-134)

## Error identity, classification and cloning

The full [error API/conversion matrix](../L1-modules/rust-lance-core-errors.md) is part of the core contract. An unknown commit outcome is Wrapped(CommitStatusUnknownError), keeping version and source while preserving the exhaustive Error enum. is_not_found explicitly vetoes that wrapper even if its source says a manifest was missing. Treating it as ordinary absence could drive a retry without establishing whether the first commit applied; the error itself instructs checking table state. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:94-127; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:601-615; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:748-761)

Not-found traversal is narrower than arbitrary source walking: direct NotFound, IO and Wrapped chains are recognized; an encountered Lance Error delegates to its own predicate and can stop traversal. Other typed accessors match direct variants/sources only. Thus maintaining an inspectable source chain does not automatically preserve top-level fence/backpressure/unknown-commit predicates. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:541-565; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:601-615; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:753-821)

Owned Arrow external and direct std IO boxed-Lance conversions attempt to recover the exact original Error. Borrowed Arrow and serde_json conversion stringify; Schema crosses Arrow through SchemaError and returns as Lance Arrow. DataFusion Context/Diagnostic wrappers are consumed, Collection keeps the first failure, and multi-owner Shared remains boxed External rather than recursively reclassified. Consumers modifying these mappings must preserve intended user-input categories and explicitly decide whether type/metadata loss is acceptable. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:843-955; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:981-1039)

CloneableError selectively preserves not-found semantics, Timeout/IO categories, fence reason, backpressure and unknown-commit version. Its other cases become Cloned(text), including External; it does not promise retained original source types, locations or traces. CloneableResult derives cloning only for cloneable success T. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:1058-1147)

Field-not-found suggestions are computed only when formatting, but every candidate participates; the ten-name display cap does not bound search work. Distance counts Unicode scalars, threshold is floor(input scalar length/3), equal-distance ties preserve input option order, and exact short inputs can qualify. Changing any of these alters user-visible diagnostic text and potentially formatting cost. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:57-88; rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:17-89)

## Field representation and tree operations

A Field is publicly mutable, but data_type() indexes required children and unwraps logical parsing. Fallible Arrow import checks only its explicit guards. Changes to child retention or logical grammar must preserve reconstructibility, or this apparently infallible accessor can panic. View types intentionally normalize, and reverse Arrow conversion does not restore field-ID metadata. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-195; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1204-1348; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1531-1546)

Default comparison ignores dictionaries/metadata/field IDs; strict nullability remains checked. OneWay's expected/actual direction is expected || !actual. Two recognized logical blob forms compare only their shared prefix, so minimal-vs-complete can match while complete-vs-complete exposes range differences. Altering that distinction changes schema compatibility and diagnostics together. ## Row-version alignment, errors and mutation

Run span lengths define positional versions. version_at skips zero lengths, the range cursor skips arbitrary empty runs, but VersionsIter can emit one value for an empty run it advances into. Direct mutable runs and protobuf decoding admit those shapes locally. Changing iterator behavior can affect zipped threshold filtering and partial refresh; tests currently cover empty runs only through the cursor. ### Raw values and fixed-size lists

ValueEncoder implements three distinct interfaces. Block compression accepts FixedWidth only and returns its unchanged buffer as Some, including empty buffers. Mini-block compression handles FixedWidth and nested FSL, with parallel validity buffers followed by the unchanged leaf buffer. Per-value compression handles FixedWidth or FSL; nullable FSL is copied into row-major validity bytes followed by leaf bytes, while nonnullable FSL moves its leaf storage. None of these paths performs IO. Invalid input handling differs: block/mini-block unsupported variants return errors, while per-value unsupported variants panic. Raw mini-block selection starts with two byte-aligned values, or eight nonaligned values using an estimated sixteen-value size. It doubles while estimated bytes remain strictly below 8186 and doubled count stays within the cached maximum. Initial count can already exceed a small configured maximum. Zero width reaches a debug assertion; malformed byte/count relationships are not validated. Full chunks retain a positive count log even when last; only a residual chunk gets log0. ### Variable-width interfaces and validation

Binary mini-blocks encode their own offset table at the beginning of each chunk, using signed32/64-bit input offsets rebased to chunk start plus table bytes. Each chunk is padded with0x48 to4/8-byte alignment respectively. The output is one concatenated buffer plus external chunk descriptors; logical num_values is retained from input even though chunk partitioning uses offsets.len()-1. Per-value VariableEncoder and VariableDecoder instead move an existing VariableWidthBlock unchanged. Whole-block VariableEncoder writes a separate width/data-start header, then original offsets and all original value bytes. These interfaces are not interchangeable. Chunk search starts at two values, grows by powers of two and treats final-tail fitting separately. The target is not a hard bound; alignment follows estimation, the initial two may exceed it, and the tail-fit branch bypasses MAX_MINIBLOCK_VALUES. The normal branch checks doubled candidate against the cap before accepting candidate, so cap4096 can stop at2048. new(Some(...)) still evaluates the lazy default because unwrap_or is eager. It does not validate UTF-8 or unrequested offsets. new asserts32/64, whereas from_variable directly casts a nested Flat width to u8; malformed width can reach division by zero or the fallback32 branch. ### Byte-stream split and entropy

BSS groups each byte position across values in a single chunk: out[j*n+i]=in[i*width+j]. Compression preserves total byte length and needs separate outer compression to save space. The encoder does not compare configured width to DataBlock width or validate physical size; short data panics, trailing data is ignored. Empty encode emits no buffers. Statistics sample the first min(num_values,64) rows, compute per-byte Shannon entropy and truncate entropy*1000 to integers. Missing physical bytes are skipped while sample-count denominator stays fixed. Selector does not verify statistic length/range or Arrow numeric type. Fixed packing transposes child buffers into row-major bytes. Mini-block packing reads DataSize and all children as FixedWidth, forwards the zipped block to raw ValueEncoder and stores field widths plus nested Flat metadata. Fixed per-value packing validates nonempty/equal-count/direct-fixed children, checked-sums widths and stores raw interleaved bytes. Exact field declarations and enum/oneof values are incorporated through the thirteen frozen schema records below; implementation claims below carry source ranges. ## How to use this contract

For a persisted change, select the owning schema in the field directory, then read its cited runtime gate. That is at most two KB hops. A schema arm's existence is not permission to emit it in every stable version. Preserve stable backward/forward contracts and frozen legacy read behavior; design new features in current writers. ### Physical V2 envelope

```text
file
  data buffers and applicable padding
  global payloads (including descriptor where present)
  column metadata protobuf payloads
  column metadata offset table: (position:u64, size:u64) entries
  global buffer offset table: (position:u64, size:u64) entries
  footer: column_metadata_start:u64
          column_table_start:u64
          global_table_start:u64
          global_buffer_count:u32
          column_count:u32
          major:u16, minor:u16, magic:[u8;4] = LANC
```

All footer/table integers are little-endian; footer length is 40 bytes. The tables contain raw offset/size entries, not length-prefixed protobuf messages. A self-described file identifies its schema through the descriptor/global metadata; an embedded mini representation can require an externally supplied schema. Alignment, column mapping and accepted page grammar depend on the exact runtime. Corruption checks are not universally exhaustive: preserve the explicit validation limits in the reader section. Persisted stable schemas must retain existing tags; schemas used exclusively in unstable formats may change without old-unstable compatibility. Verify shared use before making a breaking change. Overlay interpretation is ordered by committed_version, then list position. Deleted offsets never become visible because of an overlay. A version selects an inline root or 16-byte display-order UUID root stored at _bt/root/{lowercase hyphenated UUID}.root, plus mutations absent from the root. Children partition fragment IDs by half-open min-key boundaries; counts include buffered changes. Leaf materialization watermarks certify no earlier pending mutation above the leaf, while interiors use zero. Mutations carry exact signed aggregate deltas. These describe persisted state, not a verified balancing or commit algorithm. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:317-405)

## V2 envelope and encoding layers

The minimal envelope permits independent item counts per column and stores byte buffers without imposing logical types. Data precedes column metadata, column metadata offset table, global buffer offset table, then the footer. Footer fields in order are three little-endian u64 offsets (column metadata start, column metadata table, global buffer table), two u32 counts (global buffers, columns), two u16 versions (major, minor), and LANC. The shared reader consumes exactly 40 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-861). Padding may precede aligned buffers/metadata/table starts. Page buffers may be noncontiguous; 8 MB pages are advice, not a hard validity bound. (protos/file2.proto:11-115)

```text
file2 envelope
  data buffers
  column metadata blocks
    column encoding + optional column buffers
    pages: buffers + length + encoding + priority
  column metadata position/size table
  global buffer position/size table
  footer: A:u64 B:u64 C:u64 globals:u32 columns:u32 major:u16 minor:u16 LANC
```

The tree above reproduces the schema's composition: encoding locations are direct bytes, deferred byte range, or explicit none; page/column buffer offsets and sizes must have matching cardinality. Top-level row priority is distinct from a page's logical length. (protos/file2.proto:117-216)

The older lance.encodings namespace models Nullable/List/FixedSizeList and scalar transformations as ArrayEncoding, with ColumnEncoding wrappers for plain values, zone maps and blob descriptions. Its List encoding folds nullness into end offsets, but a strict greater-than null test in the comments conflicts with the formula at an equality boundary; see the [full analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_0.proto.md). This must be resolved from the decoder before implementing compatible list bytes. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:59-155; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:307-358)

The newer lance.encodings21 namespace separates structural layouts from compressive blocks. Layouts are MiniBlock, Constant, FullZip, Blob and Sparse; recursive compression alternatives include Flat, Variable, Constant, both bitpacking forms, FSST, Dictionary, RLE, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and both packed-struct forms. Exact fields and tag identities are in the [complete encoding analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_1.proto.md). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:341-357; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675)

## Transactions and MemWAL

External transaction files use _transactions/{read_version}-{uuid}.txn; inline transaction sections start with u32 message length. The transaction operation union uses tags 100..115, while old blob operations 200/202 are reserved. Every operation payload is retained in the [transaction L2 analysis](../L2-files/protos/transaction.proto.md). These declarations do not reconstruct commit conflict resolution by themselves. MemWAL metadata separates shard-manifest authority, background discovery snapshots, atomic compacted-generation progress, and asynchronous per-index catch-up. Recovery lists actual WAL state because last-seen position is a hint. Missing catch-up means unknown and keeps SSTables live. This separation prevents snapshot refresh from falsely certifying compaction/index coverage. (protos/table.proto:530-562; protos/table.proto:612-650; protos/table.proto:698-722)

## Generic split-block Bloom filters

Local SBBF raw bytes contain only concatenated32-byte blocks; each is eight little-endian u32 words. new accepts any multiple of32, including0, and no power-of-two/minimum/maximum check is imposed. There is no magic,version,seed,type,NDV orFPP header. to_bytes and write_bitset preserve block then lane order. # Dataset commit, transactions and conflict resolution

**Trust: source-verified contract and navigation, not runtime qualification.** Scope is the current Dataset commit/rebase path. The frozen [transaction definition](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/transaction.rs.md) and [table module](../L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) remain the authority for operation payloads, codecs and manifest application. [Dataset map](../L1-modules/rust-lance.md) · [Behavior contracts](behavior-contracts.md).

## Ownership and publication

A transaction describes intent relative to `read_version`. Data-file completion is not dataset publication. `InsertBuilder` writes fragments, constructs an Overwrite or Append transaction, then supplies it to `CommitBuilder`; `execute_uncommitted` stops before that publication. `CommitBuilder` selects new, existing or detached commit paths and constructs a new Dataset handle from the committed manifest. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:202-315; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-571)

For an existing dataset, the normal publication loop is:

1. Retain the transaction's read-version Dataset and index state. A strict Overwrite (`num_retries == 0`) skips automatic rebase; otherwise restore the original read snapshot when required. There are `max(num_retries, 1)` attempts, not `num_retries + 1`. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1581-1637)
2. Fetch the latest Dataset and intervening transactions; sort transactions by committed version. Check writer feature flags. Construct the resolver from original intent/read-state, load current lineage, check every intervening operation in order, then finish rebase. Resolver errors propagate out of this publication loop. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1515-1525; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1638-1683)
3. Serialize the rebased transaction, write an external transaction file when configured, and select the next non-detached version. Prepare index state afresh from the latest manifest on each attempt. Restore uses its separate old-manifest path. Build/migrate the candidate, fix schema, validate storage version and fragment IDs, and migrate/withdraw index coverage before publication. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1439-1513; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1684-1787)
4. Publish through `write_manifest_file` and the selected CommitHandler. On success cache transaction/manifest/index state and run automatic cleanup; a cleanup-hook error is logged, not converted into commit failure. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1531-1577; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1766-1796)
5. On a publication collision, establish the actual outcome before retry or cleanup. A retry fetches current state and rebuilds candidate/attempt-local index assembly; it must not feed prepared output back into original transaction intent. (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1479-1513; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1797-1937)

An optional overall `CommitBuilder` timeout is separately validated (zero is invalid). The lower commit retry timeout defaults to 30 seconds; `LANCE_COMMIT_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SECS` accepts a positive finite floating-point number, is cached on first access, and warns/falls back on invalid input. The lower retry clock starts after initial catch-up. Attempt zero is not bounded by the remaining-retry helper; later attempts use the remaining duration. First collision backoff derives from that attempt's elapsed time, excluding catch-up. These are different clocks, not one hard bound on all work. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:294-319; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:86-150; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1631-1683; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1797-1882)

| Result | Meaning and caller obligation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Publication `CommitConflict` | The commit loop may catch up, rebase and publish a new candidate within its attempt/time budget. This is not automatically an operation-level conflict. | rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1797-1882 |
| Resolver retryable conflict (**R** below) | Current operation payload cannot safely merge as-is. Error propagates from `check_txn`/finish; an outer operation may need to reread/recompute. Do not promise that this commit loop silently rebuilds arbitrary user work. | rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:325-382; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1643-1675 |
| Resolver incompatible conflict (**I** below) | Reject this stale/incompatible intent. Do not resubmit it unchanged as a publication collision. | rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:325-382 |
| `CommitStatusUnknown` | Publication could have succeeded. Preserve evidence/files, inspect durable table state, and reconcile before retrying or destructive cleanup. After a handler error, the commit path reads the target manifest and its durable transaction and compares **serialized protobuf transaction values**, not transient in-memory payloads. Do not place a new operation only in the top-level matcher. First define persistent intent and its compatibility/validation/application rules, then decide both directions of conflicts, then expose an API. The following sets deliberately separate definition/application from orchestration so each task starts with at most five files.

**Definition/application set:** [transaction definition, including PB conversion references](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/transaction.rs.md) → [table transaction map](../L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). Select the definition, codec, validation, index-maintenance and manifest-build records relevant to the new payload; frozen records hold exact ranges. Do not serialize attempt-local tagged assembly as user intent.

**Publication/conflict set:**

1. `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:294-571` — public builder validation and path dispatch.
2. `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1439-1937` — fresh-attempt state, catch-up, candidate building, publish/recovery.
3. `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:414-477` — global symmetric guards and directional dispatch; then the relevant rows/ranges above, and `2222-2262` for finish dispatch.
4. `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:222-332` — reconcile ambiguous outcomes; preserve durable transaction identity.

These are three unique source files. A concrete new operation must also choose its public caller and definition/application subtask; this document does not imply those can all be changed safely by editing one matcher. Validate input and preserve stable format/API contracts; no tests or generated/binary files were analyzed for this synthesis.

# Encoding selection and version admission

**Trust: synthesized from frozen deep records plus selected primitive dispatch ranges.** This is the decision contract; [format-spec](format-spec.md) owns persisted grammar and exact version matrices. [Encoding Module Map](../L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md) owns type/file navigation. Uncovered implementation details remain source-readable, not a transcription backlog.

## The four decisions must stay separate

1. **Choose exact file version.** Public selectors and strict persisted-version parsing differ. Current stable default is V2_2; next is unstable V2_3. File footer identity, dataset version, blob representation version and index version are different domains. Use the [exact identity table](format-spec.md#exact-file-identity-and-acceptance). (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:25-262)
2. **Choose structural field behavior.** Version composition supplies ordered field/page behaviors to the version-free mechanism. Primitive, blob, list, FSL, map and struct factories decide logical shape/column allocation. A metadata tag alone does not make every shape legal in every format. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:24-285; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:95-134; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:95-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:103-139)
3. **Choose page layout.** Dense-u16/u32, constant and sparse mechanisms interpret normalized rep/def structure and the selected version's behavior sequence. Sparse automatic selection is a lazy fallback when dense rep/def planning requires page splitting or one row exceeds budget, and any explicit setting suppresses that automatic path. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs:8-24; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7695-7880)
4. **Choose physical compression inside that layout.** `CompressionStrategy` has distinct block, mini-block and per-value factories. Production version modules compose helper selectors. A codec offered by one interface or generic decoder is not proof of admission in another interface or exact file reader. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:86-152; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:896-1236; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-93)

### Stable and unstable gates

V2_1 selects dense-u16, raw complex-null levels and a fixed-width dictionary policy excluding 64-bit values. It allows an all-null ConstantLayout without an inline scalar or compressed levels, but rejects scalar constants and sparse pages. V2_2 adds dense-u32 framing, compressed levels, scalar constants and the 64-bit dictionary policy, but still rejects sparse pages. V2_3 composes sparse planning before constant/dense-u32 fallbacks. The exact reader grammar remains the authority: enabling a writer mechanism without admitting its exact metadata on read creates unreadable output. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7730-7799; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:125-134; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:121-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:129-139; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:93-162; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:93-160)

Explicit sparse requests are case-insensitive. A format without sparse behavior rejects them. In sparse-capable composition, explicit sparse planning can defer constant-layout cases to later behavior. Automatic sparse checks supported value blocks, treats unavailable value preparation as dense fallback, but propagates actual sparse planning errors. A field marked sparse is therefore not a guarantee that every page is physically sparse. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7690-7705; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7802-7877)

Stable formats preserve backward/forward contracts; no compatibility obligation attaches to earlier unstable V2_3 revisions. Frozen legacy readers retain existing behavior and do not become foundations for new writers. Capability flags are an additional gate independent of the numeric file version; paired sticky mixed-version/tagged-FRI flags and unknown reader/writer flag checks are specified in the [frozen feature-flag contract](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs.md). (AGENTS.md:5-20; rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:100-378)

## Configuration and codec policy

Compression parameter precedence is exact dtype key → exact column key, otherwise first matching wildcard in HashMap iteration order → version strategy's field metadata overlay. An exact empty column entry suppresses wildcard selection; None cannot clear an inherited value. Multiple wildcard matches have no specificity ordering. Numeric metadata parse failures can be ignored, and BSS/chunk-size failures warn; do not describe this parser as strict validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:45-169; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:554-585; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-38)

The existing [shared compression contract](behavior-contracts.md#shared-compression-selection-and-decoder-dispatch) supplies exact RLE/bitpacking benefit comparisons and reader dispatch; [variable/FSST/BSS contract](behavior-contracts.md#variable-fsst-and-bss-behavior-contracts) supplies thresholds. Key decision hazards are:

- Mini-block and per-value `compression=none` shortcuts occur at different stages of validation. Explicit codec names are interpreted differently by the two factories. A named codec is not a universal promise of that output. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:655-696; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:797-841)
- Automatic FSST requires eligible non-binary values, maximum length at least 5 and data size at least 32,768 bytes. Large per-value compression can take precedence even over explicit FSST. BSS needs a non-none outer compression parameter; forced BSS alone is insufficient. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:148-185; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:655-696; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:797-841)
- RLE must strictly beat raw payload size; equal comparison against bitpacking can prefer RLE. An absent ratio threshold is not the named 0.5 threshold. Estimation and actual encoding can both perform work. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:174-510)
- Metadata-only output (`None`) differs from an empty payload (`Some(empty)`). Some compressor factories are feature-gated; successful construction can still defer failure to lazy codec initialization. Do not replace these states with one “empty” case. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:896-987; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:141-432)
- Statistics are shared/cached and can include physical null slots or unused values. Mutating a payload without invalidating/rebuilding its statistics can select the wrong codec. They are not uniformly logical-valid-row statistics. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:52-216; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:232-594)

## Lifecycle and extension obligations

Field lifecycle is construct → prepare all roots → maybe_encode/optional flush → final flush → await page tasks → finish. Preserve per-column page order, complete top-level rows and original top-row counts through nested flattening. `FieldEncoder` is Send, while strategies are Send+Sync; the traits do not enforce a complete state machine for callers. [Frozen encoder](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs.md) contains exact signatures and failure/mutation details. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:39-234)

An encoding extension must choose whether it changes logical structure, page layout, compression, or only policy. Add the mechanism at that seam, descriptor fields where needed, exact-version writer composition **and** reader grammar/decoder dispatch. Keep metadata/data counts, buffer order/alignment, rep/def coordinates, null meaning and optional payload distinctions consistent. Existing unsafe buffer/codec preconditions and corruption-check limits are documented in [behavior contracts](behavior-contracts.md); a new selector does not validate them automatically. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:117-254; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:988-1236; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:8-675)

## Ordered read sets

**New structural mechanism, five files:**

1. [Frozen structural builder record](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs.md) → `rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder/structural.rs:24-285` for field recognition/allocation.
2. `rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:5410-5480,7690-7930` for behavior interfaces and planning/encoding dispatch.
3. [Frozen V2_3 composition](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs.md) → `rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:103-139` to opt an unstable writer into the mechanism.
4. [Frozen V2_3 reader](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs.md) for exact reader grammar before changing admission.
5. [Frozen structural schema](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_1.proto.md) for persisted tags/descriptor contract.

**Physical compression/policy subtask, five files:** [compression helpers](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs.md), [parameters](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs.md), [V2_3 compression composition](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/compression.rs.md), [statistics](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs.md), and the one codec file selected through the [Module Map](../L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). Each frozen record supplies exact implementation ranges. Do not include every codec in a routine task.
