# Index creation, querying and maintenance

**Trust: checked orchestration and extension contracts; algorithm internals are mapped unless separately deep-linked.** [Index Module Map](../L1-modules/rust-lance-index.md) · [Dataset Module Map](../L1-modules/rust-lance.md) · [commit conflicts](protocol-commit.md) · [persisted index descriptors](format-spec.md#index-details).

## Identity, coverage and compatibility

An index name identifies a logical index that can have multiple physical UUID segments. Metadata includes indexed/covering field IDs, creation dataset version, fragment bitmap, Any details, index version, base ID and files. Keep dataset version, file format version and index implementation version distinct. Create names are reserved against **all** manifest entries, including unreadable ones. Query usability requires a known exact declared type and supported index version; hiding an unsupported entry from queries does not relinquish its name or coverage. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:182-200; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:659-681; rust/lance/src/index.rs:3042-3062)

`IndexPluginRegistry` stores case-insensitive plugin aliases and full protobuf names. `supports_details` validates the full qualified type suffix after the final slash; lookup-by-details separately derives a short terminal name. The short-name lookup is not a replacement for exact type-identity admission. Historical detail package identities remain stable; put new messages in the current schema rather than relocating old ones. (rust/lance-index/src/registry.rs:26-177; protos/index.proto:6-311; protos/index_old.proto:8-28)

Scalar SearchResult carries set certainty: Exact is exact; AtMost is a superset requiring post-filtering; AtLeast is a subset and matters when composing negation. Row IDs may be opaque stable IDs; an index returning row addresses must advertise that distinction. Old-index filters use fragment membership only for address-style IDs and exact row-ID membership for stable IDs. Reinterpreting an opaque ID's high bits as fragment identity can revive or discard the wrong rows. (rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:397-479; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:530-563; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:627-711)

## Build and publish

`DatasetIndexExt::create_index` configures `CreateIndexBuilder`. It accepts one keyed column at this entry. Before training, vector/FTS requests undergo fragment-reuse admission. Scalar FTS resolves document granularity/nested paths separately. `execute_uncommitted` builds files and metadata without publishing; ordinary execution creates a `CreateIndex {new_indices, removed_indices}` transaction, applies the commit and reloads the committed UUID. Replacement removes the selected prior same-name declarations through that transaction; file creation alone has not made an index visible. Multi-segment FM construction has its own builder branch. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:1858-1883; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-236; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:688-759)

### Scalar plugin path

Resolve a field and plugin by `ScalarIndexParams.index_type`. The plugin must provide a BasicTrainer or this generic path rejects it. `new_training_request(params, field)` defines ordering and row-ID/address needs; the Dataset prepares a stream satisfying that request (or accepts caller-provided preprocessed data), then `train_index` writes to the new IndexStore and returns `CreatedIndex`. The result's details/version/file list must be persisted; the trainer does not commit a Dataset. FTS training can project resolved nested documents rather than treating every requested name as an ordinary scalar field. (rust/lance/src/index/scalar.rs:349-443; rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:29-100; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:482-528)

The plugin contract includes name, exactness, supported version, optional query parser, load/cache behavior, segment-compatibility validation and optional seed hooks. A default segment validator accepts any combination, so plugins needing identical models/hash parameters must override it. Seed-writer construction must derive parameters from details and perform no I/O; `might_use_seeds=false` avoids probing data files; `update_from_seeds=None` requests full-scan fallback. User-visible details JSON is part of the public API. (rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:102-190; rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:274-357)

Advertising asynchronous batch row-ID remapping requires implementing `load_index_with_remapping`; its default rejects a present remapper. Cache entries are already namespaced per index by the caller; serialized/store-bound representations must reconstruct against the correct store/remapping context. The load future supplied to single-flight caching is awaited at most once on a miss and may be dropped unawaited on a warm hit. (rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:173-213; rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:360-365)

### Vector path, including IVF-PQ

Whole-table builds may retain an index definition without training when the dataset is empty or has too few vectors for its quantizer. Such metadata has empty coverage and records details for later training. A caller-selected vector fragment subset is validated and owns its training-row math; it does not use whole-table definition-only fallback. Do not interpret an empty definition as a fully indexed table. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:659-678; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:1008-1049)

Modern IVF-PQ uses `IvfIndexBuilder<FlatIndex, ProductQuantizer>`. The entry dispatches on index kind, element type and IndexFileVersion, propagates fragment filtering and transpose selection. The retained legacy IVF-PQ route rejects filtered builds; it is a frozen compatibility path, not the route for a new format feature. (rust/lance/src/index/vector.rs:1201-1318)

The modern builder stages are: load/train IVF → load/train quantizer → shuffle input into partitions → build partition streams → merge/write partition files. Pre-supplied IVF/quantizer objects skip their respective training. Quantizer training samples requested fragments, normalizes cosine data, filters nonfinite values, optionally computes IVF residuals, and invokes the quantizer with L2 training distance. These preparation choices must stay consistent with query-time distance/quantization interpretation. This contract does not qualify every numerical kernel. (rust/lance/src/index/vector/builder.rs:552-593; rust/lance/src/index/vector/builder.rs:703-804)

## Query contract

`VectorIndex::search` returns row-ID/distance batches and receives a PreFilter for deleted or otherwise excluded rows. Partition discovery returns partition IDs paired with centroid distances, closest first. A Query specifies k, inclusive lower/exclusive upper distance bounds, minimum/maximum probes, optional HNSW ef, refine factor, metric, index-use flag, parallelism and RQ approximation mode. ApproxMode currently affects RQ only; “Accurate” is not a global exact-search guarantee. Query parallelism 0 is automatic, -1 uses CPU-pool size, 1 is sequential and larger values are bounded by the execution layer. These are interface contracts; concrete implementations may override scheduling. (rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:93-169; rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:203-265)

Default `search_partitions` validates equal partition/distance counts and a valid half-open interval, then searches sequentially, sets each partition's centroid distance and consults optional stop/control callbacks. Prepared-partition and batch-search methods require implementation support; callers must gate batch search with `supports_batch_partition_search` (default false). Partition selection, approximate scoring and later refine/filter work are separate stages. (rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:252-265; rust/lance-index/src/vector.rs:294-383)

Dataset Scanner validates incompatible search options and chooses vector/FTS/MinHash/ordinary filtered-read sources before residual filter, ordering, limit and take/projection stages. Scalar-index eligibility is conditional on scanner options and vector prefiltering. Preserve the SearchResult certainty and fragment coverage when composing this plan; a physical index hit is not proof that all rows or predicates are covered. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3210-3375; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:397-479)

## Update, merge and rebuild

`optimize_indices` groups the complete manifest list by name, excluding system indices. Any unknown type or too-new segment skips that whole logical group. Covering-field indices are skipped with a warning for table-wide maintenance but explicitly naming one returns an error, because current rebuilders do not preserve those carried values. A fully covered scalar group can skip work when neither retrain nor explicit merge is requested. A no-file-work optimize can still need a CreateIndex commit to advance MemWal catch-up state. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:2577-2729)

### Scalar maintenance

Select old segments and calculate live/deleted coverage. If no unindexed data and at most one selected segment, return no work. Merge old data without a full rebuild only when live old coverage exists, UpdateCriteria does not require old data, NGram fragment reuse does not force rebuilding, and either there is one selected segment or the type has an N:1 merge primitive (BTree/NGram). Otherwise rebuild precisely the intended fragment set. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:435-523)

The merge path tries compatible seeds only when the plugin says they might exist and harvesting succeeds for the relevant unindexed fragments. Otherwise scan new data, merge BTree/NGram with per-segment filters, or call the scalar index's `update` with a mode-correct old-data filter. Return new UUID/files/details/coverage and the minimum selected source dataset version; replacement publication goes through the normal CreateIndex transaction. A new index implementation must honor the old-data filter rather than copying every old posting. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:524-613; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:530-563; rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:627-711)

### Vector maintenance

Stored coverage with no live coverage is **dormant**, distinct from a born-empty definition. Dormant stored vectors must be replaced, not merged back under stable row IDs. A deferred definition trains from saved parameters over the current column. Retrain/dormant rebuild checks exact expected coverage; definition-only degradation is accepted only when too-few-vector state is established and no files/coverage were produced. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:667-831; rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:899-1013)

`num_indices_to_merge=Some(0)` appends a segment for unindexed rows without removing old ones; no unindexed rows makes that explicit append a no-op. The default can also append when existing segments are query-compatible but have different models, reusing the current suffix model. With no new rows, default optimize may rebalance. Ordinary merge selects a suffix, removes only segments actually merged, and derives metadata from those actual sources rather than an incompatible earlier segment. Preserve raw/provenance coverage and effective live coverage distinctions instead of replacing one with the other. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:1016-1251)

Concurrent changes are resolved at commit: CreateIndex/Rewrite ordering can withdraw coverage, preserve partial tagged provenance with scan fallback, or require a rebuild. A new segment's bitmap is a correctness assertion, not just a performance hint. Read the [directional conflict contract](protocol-commit.md#index-coverage-and-rewrite-lineage) before changing that assertion.

## Adding a scalar index: bounded subtasks

**Contract and implementation set (up to five files):**

1. `rust/lance-index-core/src/scalar.rs:397-711` — certainty, identity, training/update/filter contracts.
2. `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/registry.rs:29-357` — implement ScalarIndexPlugin and optionally BasicTrainer/query parser/seed/remapping hooks.
3. A new implementation under `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/` — new path chosen by the developer; use the [Module Map](../L1-modules/rust-lance-index.md) to select one comparable existing index, not all algorithms.
4. `rust/lance-index/src/scalar.rs:36-52` — expose the module.
5. `rust/lance-index/src/registry.rs:26-177` — register aliases and exact detail identity in the built-in registry when this is a built-in plugin.

**Persistence/integration set (up to five files):**

1. [Frozen index schema](../L2-files/protos/index.proto.md) — add details without moving historical identities or reusing stable tags.
2. `rust/lance/src/index/scalar.rs:349-443` — verify generic training request/data/CreatedIndex integration; specialized non-BasicTrainer construction needs an explicit route.
3. `rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-236,659-735` — metadata, FRI admission and transaction publication.
4. `rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:435-613` — update/merge/rebuild behavior and filters.
5. `rust/lance/src/index.rs:2577-2729,3042-3062` — whole-name maintenance and version admission.

Using the existing generic scalar plugin route does not by itself require inventing a new IndexType enum variant. ## Dataset ownership, version and mutation

A Dataset represents a checked-out manifest snapshot. `Dataset::open(uri)` loads through DatasetBuilder. Numeric checkout stays on the current branch; a named tag resolves its recorded branch/version. Checkout returns a new Dataset, while `checkout_latest(&mut self)` replaces manifest and derived fragment bitmap; it clears base-store caches if base paths changed. `main` is the default-branch alias in reference contexts. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:520-588)

Restore creates a **new** transaction based on the latest version, pointing at the currently checked-out historical version. It is not an in-place rewrite of that historical manifest. Detached commits do not become latest and do not join ordinary history; the builder also enforces existing-dataset/v2-manifest-path requirements. Public commit entry points accept operation/read version/store/handler/session parameters and delegate to the common path. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1459-1474; rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1620-1669; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-513)

Mutation methods have distinct handle effects: Rust builders commonly return a new Dataset/result; `&mut Dataset` convenience methods replace their state after success. Python native delete/update/restore/compaction/index methods replace the internal Arc after successful execution; an existing independently checked-out handle remains its own snapshot. Do not describe every Python method as returning a new Dataset: delete/update return count dictionaries, create_index returns the facade, and uncommitted index creation does not update the snapshot. (python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098; python/src/dataset.rs:2274-2288; python/src/dataset.rs:2867-2884; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:509-523; python/python/lance/dataset.py:4575-4606)

Storage mutation is not atomic merely because the public function returns Result: data files can exist before commit, and a storage error can follow successful publication. Use the [commit outcome contract](protocol-commit.md#errors-retries-and-ambiguous-success) before retrying or cleaning files. Cleanup of old versions is separately destructive: removed versions cannot be checked out/restored and their unique data can be lost. The explanation path computes a cleanup plan without deleting files. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1477-1483; python/src/dataset.rs:2291-2338)

## Dataset open reference resolution

When a named branch is requested through an unmanaged store, DatasetBuilder marks checkout as delayed. Numeric-only version references remain relative to the URI chain. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:734-744)

For delayed checkout, the initial load_by_uri now receives None and loads the URI chain's latest version; it must not require the target branch's requested version number to exist on that initial chain. Non-delayed loading still passes the requested version number. This is a source-verified behavior change in the refresh. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:807-828)

After that initial load, delayed tag lookup resolves its branch/version on the loaded Dataset, and differing branch/version triggers checkout_version. The new initial-load rule preserves this later checkout stage rather than changing file-format gates or transaction conflict rules. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:844-866)

[Ordered reference-open route](../L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md#dataset-open) · [Java mapped interface notes](../L1-modules/java.md#refresh-reference-based-opening-and-value-identity--mapped-only). Python declarations themselves did not change; its open/version family uses the shared DatasetBuilder boundary.

## Read/query contracts

Rust `Dataset::scan()` creates a Scanner. `try_into_stream` builds a physical plan and executes it; collecting batches is a separate operation. Plan order is source → filter → sort → limit/offset → late take/projection as required. Source selection and index use depend on search and prefilter options. Invalid combinations fail validation, and requesting projected constants alone is not automatically a supported row-count source. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2675; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3210-3375)

`take` selects logical row positions; `take_rows` selects internal row IDs. IDs and encoded physical addresses are separate when stable IDs are enabled. Unfiltered count sums fragment counts; a filtered count uses a scanner with empty user projection plus row ID. Python's Arrow-expression count uses its scanner directly, whereas string/None count goes through the native Dataset count method. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1705-1778; python/python/lance/dataset.py:2616-2622; python/src/dataset.rs:1656-1685)

Python scanner defaults are applied before explicit non-None options. The final builder forwards options to the native scanner. Projection by names and projection by SQL transforms are mutually exclusive; string and Substrait filters are also mutually exclusive at the binding. Row-ID/address flags are separate; row-address prefilter bytes use the shared RowAddrMask decoder. FTS phrases cannot target multiple columns in the native dict-query route. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:1496-1565; python/python/lance/dataset.py:7348-7385; python/src/dataset.rs:1232-1437)

`LanceScanner.to_table` materializes the entire reader; `to_batches` iterates it. The native LanceReader owns a background stream producer, cancellation channel and bounded output channel. It terminates on first stream error/end or caller/channel cancellation; an unexpectedly closed producer channel becomes an error rather than silent EOF. Retaining all yielded batches can consume unbounded caller memory even though the channel is bounded. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:7399-7409; python/src/reader.rs:48-123)

DataFusion integration parses/qualifies identifiers according to planner options: exact field-name matching precedes ASCII case-insensitive matching; relation qualification is disabled by default and otherwise dots can represent nested access. The Dataset TableProvider translates projection/filter/limit into Scanner and declares Exact filter pushdown. Multiple output partitions are merged preserving known ordering, otherwise coalesced; a single partition executes directly. Preserve declared pushdown exactness when adding expressions. (rust/lance-datafusion/src/planner.rs:280-350; rust/lance/src/datafusion/dataframe.rs:132-197; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)

## Write, update and index contracts

`Dataset::write` accepts an iterator/stream conversion and InsertBuilder writes fragments before CommitBuilder publishes an Overwrite or Append operation. `execute_uncommitted` returns staged intent/data, not a visible new version. Python `write_dataset` validates/converts its input and destination, then native `_write_dataset` converts a native Scanner or Arrow stream and calls Rust Dataset::write. The binding recognizes case-insensitive create/append/overwrite and rejects other modes. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:202-315; python/python/lance/dataset.py:8350-8377; python/src/dataset.rs:4849-4888)

Python delete/update accept SQL or serialize Arrow expressions as Substrait. The native layer rejects predicates of other types, configures retry parameters, and delegates to DeleteBuilder/UpdateBuilder. Update assignments are strings parsed by the Rust builder; input/build errors map to ValueError and operation execution errors to IOError in this route. Returned keys are `num_deleted_rows` and `num_rows_updated`. The [conflict protocol](protocol-commit.md) determines whether operation recomputation is required. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:2938-2943; python/python/lance/dataset.py:3147-3158; python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098)

Python native index creation uppercases a supported high-level type discriminator. Generic `SCALAR` requires a config carrying its plugin type and serialized parameters, so custom plugin names need not be added as new built-in discriminators. Named FTS parameters are checked against an allowlist. Missing replace/train flags default true here. If fragment_ids are present, native creation uses execute_uncommitted and does not update the Dataset; ordinary creation publishes then replaces the handle. The Python scalar facade explicitly directs distributed forms that require it to create_index_uncommitted. (python/src/dataset.rs:2616-2819; python/src/dataset.rs:2834-2884; python/python/lance/dataset.py:3905-3932)

Compaction has plan → execute tasks → commit phases for distributed use; the convenience execute path performs the whole operation and updates the Python handle. Commit may use a subset of completed task results. Preserve original read versions and deletion/rewrite reconciliation; [L0 compaction](../L0-orientation.md) and [commit lineage](protocol-commit.md#index-coverage-and-rewrite-lineage) explain why the driver must not substitute its newer snapshot for task intent. OptimizeIndices similarly delegates options to DatasetIndexExt and updates the native snapshot after success. (python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:479-523; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:559-606; python/src/dataset.rs:2587-2613; rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3156-3260)
